INTRODUCTION

=== Page 6 ===
Introduction 13
Astrology has its roots in antiquity back as far as the
memory of recorded history. It comprises one of
humankind's first and oldest scientific studies, perhaps
the first and oldest. As such, astrology was the domain
of priests and scholars in ancient times.
As modern scientific thought developed, science
accepted that part of astrology which dealt with
celestial phenomena and planetary motion and called
it astronomy; the human element was discarded as
bunk and along with the title, astrology, was swept
into the dustbins of superstition.
But astrology is a proud name given to a study based
on principles that could not be destroyed and would
not be forgotten. A new era is awakening for
astrology, an era guided by a scientific approach and
geared to objective examination and research.
Astrology's birth pangs are part of the distant past;
growing pains continue in the present; astrology's
rightful place in the scheme of human development
is in the near future. You, too, can be part of that
future, an important factor in what lies ahead for
astrology. The age of Aquarius, the age of astrology,
is fast approaching. The time to begin is at hand.
Modem astrology, with its rich heritage steeped in
symbolism and tradition, is not a stagnant art. As
awareness of the universe has increased, so has
astrological knowledge. The discoveries of Uranus
(1781), Neptune (1846) and Pluto (1930) have enabled
astrologers to account, at least in part, for conditions
that previously did not fit into the astrological scheme.
The astrological significance of Chiron, a planetoid
discovered in 1977, is currently under study. Recent
space research has shown that Pluto is not as large
as was formerly believed. The planet's orbital
eccentricities raise the scientific possibility that another
planet travels in the outer reaches of our solar system,
a theory long held by many astrologers. New
discoveries that will enrich astrology most certainly
lie ahead.
Modern astrology has not abandoned traditional
theory; it has updated outmoded concepts and refined
application of astrological principles to meet modern
needs. Astrology has emerged from the cocoon of
fatalism so prevalent in bygone eras. Today, it
provides the means by which one can gain insight into
human behavior, attain self-understanding and achieve
full self-development.
To students and teachers of astrology, this book offers
more than the basic information needed to erect a
horoscope and sketchy interpretations on which to draw
astrological conclusions. It is a comprehensive text
designed to lead the student toward an understanding
of astrological principles, calculations and delineation
and to pique the student's interest in further astrological
study and research. Many obscure astrological factors
missing from other texts are discussed.
Part 1, THEORY, offers the reader a thorough
grounding in the principles and theory on which
horoscope analysis is based. It explores less familiar
topics such as the Vertex, East Point and asteroids;
it covers finer points of theory including sub-
rulerships, abstract points and the Prenatal Eclipse as
well as the meanings of signs, planets and houses and
the interrelationships that exist among the various
astrological elements.
Part 11, CALCULATIONS, introduces several house
systems. Alternate methods of chart calculation
complete with easy-to-follow examples are presented
so that the student can choose the method best suited
to his or her talents. Both the log method and regular
method of computation, which can be easily adapted
to hand calculator use, are presented. Commonly used
mathematical approximations are shown, along with
precise calculations to alert the reader to the difference
between an approximate chart and an accurate
horoscope. In addition to calculation and tabulation
of aspects and aspect patterns, the basic significance
of applying, separating, approaching and departing
aspects is discussed in the final chapter of Part 11.
Part III, DELINEATION, shows the student how to
assemble and synthesize the numerous astrological
factors contained in a horoscope. Interpretational
examples clarify delineation techniques. Interpretations
are given for all major aspects (parallel and contra parallel
included) formed by planets, angles, the Moon's Nodes
and Part of Fortune. The general influence of minor
aspects is discussed. Special techniques that are helpful
in understanding relationships and revealing future
trends that supplement the natal horoscope are
introduced. Combined, Parts I, II and 111 form a complete
guidebook for horoscope construction and analysis.
Astrology is reaching into every area of life.
Hopefully, this book will enable you to become better
informed as to what astrology is really all about and will
whet your appetite for more knowledge about this
fascinating subject through which you can enrich the
lives ol yourself and others

THEORY

=== Page 8 ===
Fundamentals of Astrology
Simply stated, astrology deals with the relationship
between humankind and celestial phenomena. It is
concerned with correlating planetary movements with
the human condition and events on Earth. Various
specialized branches of astrology are directed toward the
study of human relationships, politics, current events,
weather and the answers to specific questions of
immediate interest. This book is devoted primarily to
the branch called natal astrology, the study of one's
personality and the conditions of one's life in all its facets
according to the principles of astrology.
A natal horoscope is a map of the heavens that charts
the positions of the Sun, Moon and the eight planets
(Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Satum, Uranus,
Neptune and Pluto) as they appeared at the birthplace
of a particular individual at the exact time of his or her
birth. From this horoscope, sometimes called a birth map
or nativity, deductions are made according to
astrological logic. These deductions describe one's
personal characteristics, behavior patterns, emotional
responses, inborn drives, natural abilities, potential for
achievement and capacity for growth and development
as seen from the astrological point of view.
Circumstances that arise in various areas of life are
revealed in the horoscope.
The apparent path of the Sun during the course of
a year as viewed from Earth forms the basis for
astrological measurements necessary to charting a
horoscope. (A horoscope that shows the Earth at the
center of the map and the positions of planets as
observed from the birthplace is called a geocentric or
Earth-centered map. Maps that chart the planets as
observed from the Sun are heliocentric or Sun-centered
maps.) To earthlings, the Sun appears to travel around
Earth; in reality. Earth orbits the Sun, as do all planets
in our solar system. The Tropical (movable) Zodiac
follows the apparent path of the Sun. This path is
called the ecliptic. The plane of the ecliptic is actually
the plane in which Earth orbits the Sun. The planes
of all planetary orbits except that of Pluto lie within
7° (seven degrees) of the plane of the eclipitc; Pluto's
orbit varies about 17° from the ecliptic.
The path of the ecliptic as it encircles the Earth forms
an elliptical (oval) pattern that approximates a circle,
which contains 360°. That part of space surrounding
Earth, which includes the ecliptic and the orbits of the
planets, forms the Zodiac Belt, a circular band
approximately 18° thick that extends about 9° on
either side of the ecliptic. This circular belt is divided
into twelve equal sections of 30° each, designated signs
of the zodiac. Signs of the zodiac describe parts of the
heavens much like lines of longitude describe parts of
Earth. The zodiacal position of a planet is called its
zodiacal longitude.
A circle such as the Zodiac Belt has no beginning
or end, but for astrological purposes that point on the
ecliptic where the Sun appears to cross over the
equator as it travels from south to north each year
is defined as 0° Aries. At that time, the time of the
vernal equinox, the Sun appears to be directly above
Earth's equator. The vernal equinox heralds the
beginning of spring and the Sun s entry into the sign
of Aries. The Sun's position on the ecliptic at the first
moment of spring marks the starting point of the
zodiac. Aries is the first sign ot the zodiac; the other
eleven signs follow in order: Taurus Gemini, Cancer,

Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn,
Aquarius and Pisces (see Figure 1). This zodiacal
sequence makes it possible to identify consistently
certain parts of the heavens. Because of the particular
spatial relationship between each sign and Earth, each
sign's influence on Earth is uniquely significant. The
way planetary energy manifests on Earth depends
upon characteristics peculiar to the sign a planet
occupies. Signs do not alter the nature of planets; they
color the mode of planetary action.

Figure 1. The Zodiac Belt
The signs of the Tropical Zodiac are not to be
confused with constellations of the same name. At one
time, over two thousand years ago, constellations and
like signs coincided in space. However, at the spring
and fall equinoxes the Sun appears to cross the equator
slightly westward of the points it crossed the year
before. Because of this gradual westward movement
of the equinoctial points along the ecliptic, called
Precession of the Equinoxes, the position of the
Tropical Zodiac shifts slightly each year. In 1980 the
constellations lagged about 24° behind signs of the
same name. The constellation Pisces appeared in the
background over the eastern horizon when the sign
Aries rose over the horizon. The sidereal zodiac
describes positions of constellations. The point 6°
Pisces on the sidereal zodiac corresponds roughly to
0° Aries on the Tropical Zodiac. The word zodiac in
this book refers to the Tropical Zodiac unless
otherwise stated.
The first coordinate for identifying a planet's position
in space is zodiacal longitude. A second coordinate,
declination, measures the distance in degrees a planet lies
north or south of the celestial equator (the projection of
Earth's equator into space). Zodiacal longitude and
declination are the only measurements needed to
pinpoint the location of a planet in our solar system.
(Celestial latitude defines a planet's position north or
south of the ecliptic. This text follows the more common
practice of using declination instead.)
Once a planet's zodiacal position is established, the
planet is placed in the corresponding degree in the
horoscope. The sign and degree of the zodiac that rises
over the eastern horizon at the time of birth is the
"starting point" or Ascendant of the horoscope. The
Ascendant is marked in the eastern section of the
horoscope; the remaining degrees of the zodiac continue
counterclockwise around the horoscope in order until
the circle is closed and the entire zodiac is contained
within. The declination of a planet is not entered in the
face of a horoscope; it is listed separately.
Beginning with the Ascendant, the horoscope is
sectioned into twelve parts called houses, each numbered
consecutively from one to twelve in the same order as
the signs, counterclockwise. The point of the zodiac at
which a house begins is the house cusp. A house ends
where the next begins. Cusp lines which separate the
houses resemble the spokes of a wheel (see Figure 2).
After the houses are marked in a horoscope, the planets
are entered in the houses according to sign and degree.
The planets, signs and houses have specific functions
in a horoscope, functions that are interrelated. Each
house represents a particular area of life; the planets
activate the affairs of the houses and energize the drives
of the individual; the signs influence the expression of
planetary drives and house affairs.
The houses are divisions of a horoscope. The signs
are divisions of the zodiac. Note that the directional
points east, west, north and south in an astrological
map are the reverse of those designated on a geographic
map (see Figure 2).
Certain of the planets, signs and houses are closely
allied by virtue of natural rulership. Each house is
associated with a particular sign called its natural sign;
each sign is ruled by a particular planet(s) called its
natural planetary ruler; each house is ruled (governed)
naturally by the planet(s) that rules its natural sign.

=== Page 10 ===
Fundamentals of Astrology 19
For example, Aries, the first sign of the zodiac, is the
natural sign of the first house; both Aries and the first
house are ruled naturally by the planet Mars (see
Figure 2). To say that a planet naturally rules a
particular house and sign means that the three elements
(planet, sign and house) have a natural affinity for each
other and share common attributes. For example,
among characteristics shared by the first house, Aries,
and Mars are initiatory qualities. The first house
represents beginnings; Aries expresses initiative; Mars,
the energy planet, is associated with igniting action.

In a horoscope, a planet is said to rule the house
whose cusp bears the sign naturally ruled by that
planet. If Aries is placed on the cusp of the fifth house
in a particular horoscope, Mars, as natural planetary
ruler of Aries, rules the fifth house of that horoscope,
Regardless of horoscope placement, signs and planets
retain their natural rulerships. The affairs of a house
are energized by the planets occupying and ruling that
house; the activities of a house are expressed in
accordance with the sign on the cusp.
Aspects, the angular relationships between planets,
influence the quality and dispersion of planetary
energies. To be in aspect, two planets must be placed
a specified number of degrees apart in the zodiac. The
energy of a planet is channeled into houses occupied
and ruled by other planets if it is in aspect with those
planets. Planetary action directed by aspect is modified
according to the nature of the aspect and the planets
involved. Aspects bring into sharper focus the
information provided by the distribution of the signs
and planets throughout the houses of the horoscope.
The astrologer studies the signs, planets, houses,
aspects and interrelationships that exist among the
various elements of a horoscope. Each factor is assessed
in light of all other relevant factors and interpreted
accordingly. The effectiveness of astrology depends not
only upon the astrologer's knowledge, but also upon the
astrologer's ability to communicate with a client. The
rich symbolism of astrology must be interpreted in
language that is meaningful to the client, leaving no room
for doubt or misunderstanding. Many common
astrological terms have no meaning in everyday
conversation; technical terms are obscure and often
misleading to those who are not well versed in astrology.
Archaic terms that sprang from traditional
astrological literature and are still in use today do not
carry the same connotation as in the past. Words such
as "affliction" and "malefic" as currently used in
astrology do not have dire meanings An afflicted
planet does not indicate calamity; it is one that forms
disharmonious aspects with other planets so that
planetary energies do not combine compatibly.
Afflictions tend to motivate negative expression of
planetary energies; positive expression depends upon
the effort and direction supplied by the individual. A
planet described as malefic is not "evil"; planets do
not have the powers of good or evil. Afflictions to
malefic planets are, perhaps, more difficult to handle
in terms of directing energies productively, but
whether energies are helpful or not rests ultimately
with the individual who utilizes them.
Modem astrology is not fatalistic: it cannot be equated
with "fortune telling," It demands a psychological
approach, for it deals with the individual's potentials as
defined by motivation and need.
If the astrologer is to awaken self understanding in
the client and acquaint her or him with the potentials
for growth and self-realization that are described in
the horoscope, the astrologer must be able to
communicate on a level that is consistent with the
client's needs. Some people identify with material or
physical concepts while others relate on an intellectual,
inspirational or emotional level. A client can be

=== Page 11 ===
20 Compendium of Astrology
alienated by an astrologer who is insensitive to his or
her needs and who fails to approach the client on a
level to which that client responds. Some people expect
readings couched in esoteric language and sprinkled
with astrological philosophy, but few can apply such
readings to their own lives. A person who does not
understand the message of the horoscope cannot
benefit from that knowledge. Through study of a
person's horoscope, much can be learned that enables
the astrologer to reach that particular individual. The
appropriate approach can create awareness within a
client and understanding of potentials on which that
person can draw, potentials that may have been
unrecognized, and if developed and utilized, can enrich
the client's life. Once a person recognizes weaknesses
and strengths and understands natural motivations
and drives (the inner urges which prompt action), that
person is better able to control and direct innate drives
and thereby develop more fully the potentials
described in the horoscope. A person may experience
anger and frustration because energy is wasted in
fruitless endeavors; that same person can derive
satisfaction and fulfillment by directing energy toward
productive activities as indicated in the horoscope.

The Signs of the Zodiac
Each of the twelve signs that make up the zodiac appears
in a horoscope in natural sequence as shown in Figures
1 and 2. No matter where Aries is placed in a horoscope,
the next sign is Taurus, followed by Gemini, then Cancer
and so on to Pisces, which directly precedes Aries. The
signs act as twelve distinct mediums through which
planetary energies and house affairs are expressed. For
example, a person whose horoscope has Leo on the cusp
of the second house, which rules personal finances,
handles money in a manner characteristic of Leo;
financial interests differ from those of one whose
horoscope has Virgo, Libra or any sign other than Leo
on the second house cusp. If Mercury, which energizes
the mind, is in Capricorn, Capricomian qualities
influence thought, communication and other mental
functions. Signs do not change the natures of planets or
the meanings of houses. The influence of a sign on a
planet or house is similar to the affect of a colored lens
on light. Dispersion of light varies with the color of the
lens, but colored lenses do not change the form (nature)
of light energy, radiation.
Sign Classifications
Although each sign has its own unique characteristics,
it shares some attributes with other signs. Signs are
classified in several groups according to their
similarities. The signs in a particular group do not
share all characteristics; they may also appear with
different signs under another classification. A group

Triplicities (Elements)
One major classification is called triplicities or
elements. There are four triplicities: fire, earth, air and
water. Each triplicity contains three signs; each sign
is separated from the other two belonging to the same
triplicity by 120° zodiacal longitude (see Figure 3).
Signs that belong to the same triplicity are compatible.
That is, the mode of expression of any one sign in a given
triplicity harmonizes with the mode of expression of the
other two members even though sign characteristics
differ in some respects. Characteristics common to each
triplicity are summarized below.
An individual whose horoscope contains a predomi-
nating number of planets in a particular triplicity exhibits
traits associated with that triplicity. For example, the
fiery individual probably has many planets in fire signs;
heavily populated earth signs are indicative of the "solid
citizen"; an abundance of air signs signifies the
intellectual; water signs, the sensitive.

quadruplicities: cardinal (movable), fixed and mutable
(common). Quadruplicities are also referred to as
modes and qualities. Signs which lie 90° apart or
alike frequently rub each other the wrong way, signs
of the same quadruplicity are uneasy with each other.
Those in polarity complement each other although
tension exists between them. Each sign of a polar

The predominating quadruplicity in a horoscope
describes in part that person's attitudes and approach
to circumstances. Cardinal people act promptly; fixed
people resist change; mutable people adapt easily to
changing conditions.
Positive and Negative Signs
All fire and air signs are classified as positive
(masculine); earth and water signs are classed as
negative (feminine). Positive signs indicate dynamic,
outgoing expression; negative signs denote receptivity
and passive expression.
Articulate and Human Signs
Gemini, Virgo, Libra, Sagittarius and Aquarius are called
articulate signs. These signs are also classed as human
by some authorities. Others who do not combine the two
classifications omit Libra and the last 15s of Sagittarius
from the human category but include them in the
articulate group. Articulate and human signs are
associated with human qualities such as speech and
sparse body hair. With the exception of Libra and
Sagittarius, these signs are symbolically represented by
human figures. The scales is the pictorial symbol for
libra; the centaur-archer is the symbol for Sagittarius.
Inarticulate Signs (Quadrupedian, Bestial)
The inarticulate signs are Aries, Taurus, Leo and
Capricorn. These signs are also called quadrupedian
and bestial signs. They are symbolized by four-footed
animals that have voices but lack power of speech.
Capricorn is pictured either as the goat-fish (two-
footed) or a mountain goat. The last 15° of Sagittarius
is classed as quadrupedian or bestial by authorities
who do not classify it as human, but it is not included
in the inarticulate category.
Mute Signs
The water signs. Cancer, Scorpio and Pisces, are
termed mute signs. They are characterized by the crab,
the scorpion and the fish respectively, all voiceless
creatures. These signs are often associated with an
inability to communicate freely.
Fruitful Signs
This classification describes another attribute of the
water signs. Cancer, Scorpio and Pisces. These signs
are associated with fertility.
Barren Signs
Gemini, Leo and Virgo are considered barren signs and
are associated with infertility.
Double Signs
The double signs, Gemini, Sagittarius and Pisces, also
called double-bodied or bicorporeal signs, are
characterized by dual qualities. Double signs imply
dualism in the area of activity described by their
position in a horoscope.
Equinoctial Signs
The Sun's ingress (entry) into the equinoctial signs, Aries
and Libra, ushers in two seasons of the year. In the
northern hemisphere, spring commences at the time of
the vernal equinox when the Sun enters 0° Aries. The
Sun's entrance into 0° Libra coincides with the autumnal
equinox and the beginning of autumn. These signs are
associated with beginnings and announcements.
Solstice Signs (Tropical Signs)
Cancer and Capricorn are solstice signs. The Sun's
entrance into 0° Cancer marks the summer solstice and
the official start of summer in the northern hemisphere.
As the Sun enters 0° Capricorn, the winter solstice
begins the winter season. These signs are also called
tropical signs because they occupy the parts of the
ecliptic where the Sun reaches its farthest point north
(the Tropic of Cancer) and south (Tropic of Capricorn)

=== Page 16 ===
Signs of the Zodiac 25
each year. These signs are associated with beginnings
and turning points.
Ingress Signs
The equinoctial and solstice signs, Aries, Cancer, Libra
and Capricorn, all cardinal signs, are classed together
as ingress signs. As a group, these signs represent
beginnings.
Spring Signs
Aries, Taurus and Gemini, the spring signs, are the signs
that the Sun traverses during the spring each year in the
northern hemisphere. These signs are associated with the
planting of seed and the budding stage of new growth.
Summer Signs
Cancer, Leo and Virgo are the summer signs in the
northern hemisphere. The Sun transits these signs
during the summer months. These signs are indicative
of growth and development.
Autumn Signs
Libra, Scorpio and Sagittarius are the autumn signs
in the northern hemisphere. The Sun crosses these
signs in autumn. The maturing phase of growth and
the harvest are associated with these signs.
Winter Signs
Capricorn, Aquarius and Pisces, the signs through
which the Sun travels during winter in the northern
hemisphere, are the winter signs. They are associated
with the dormant period of growth. Note that the
seasons and the growth cycle are reversed in the
southern hemisphere.
Signs of Long Ascension
Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio and Sagittarius,
the summer and autumn signs, are signs of long
ascension in the northern hemisphere. Since there are
twelve signs and twenty-four hours in a day, it would
seem logical that a different sign would rise over the
eastern horizon every two hours. This is true only at
the equator. These slow-rising signs take more than
two hours to pass over the eastern horizon and
represent the longer phase of an uneven cycle.
Signs of Short Ascension
Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Capricorn, Aquarius and
Pisces, the spring and winter signs, are signs of short
ascension in the northern hemisphere. These fast-rising
signs take less than two hours to rise over the eastern
horizon and represent the shorter phase of an uneven
cycle. Signs of long and short ascension are reversed
in the southern hemisphere.
Northern Signs (Nocturnal Signs)
Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo and Virgo are called
northern signs because they occupy the northern half
(lower section) of a chart with Aries on the cusp of the
first house. (A natural chart is shown in Chapter 1, Figure
2.) They are also called nocturnal or night signs because
their natural positions are in the section of the chart that
is below the horizon. In Figure 2, the Aries/Libra axis
represents the horizon. Northern signs express personal
needs and self-interests.
Southern Signs (Day Signs)
The southern signs, also called day signs, are Libra,
Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius and Pisces.
In a natural chart these signs are placed in the southern
(upper) half, which represents that part of the sky
above the horizon. Southern signs are associated with
objective needs and external interests.
Although each group of signs is based on common
properties of its members, the diversity of signs is
apparent from the number of different categories to
which each sign belongs. The various groups of which
each sign is a part are as follows:
Aries: Fire, cardinal, positive, inarticulate, quadru-
pedian, bestial, equinoctial, ingress, spring, short
ascension, northern and nocturnal.
Taurus; Earth, fixed, negative, inarticulate, quadru-
pedian, bestial, spring, short ascension, northern
and nocturnal.
Gemini: Air, mutable, positive, articulate, human,
barren, double, spring, short ascension, northern
and nocturnal.
Cancer: Water, cardinal, negative, mute, fruitful,
solstitial, tropical, ingress, summer, long ascension,
northern and nocturnal.

Signs of the same group do not express like qualities
in an identical manner. For example, cardinal signs Aries
and Cancer both express initiative, a cardinal quality.
However, Arian initiative is spontaneous (fire) and
dynamic (positive). Cancerian initiative reflects
sensitivity (water) and receptivity (negative).
Characteristics common to the triplicity, quadru-
plicity and positive or negative classifications of a sign
are among more prominent sign qualities. These
categories are noted in the sections of this chapter that
describe individual sign attributes.

is composed of variations of the following astrological

Sign glyphs are pictured and described in the part of
this chapter devoted to individual signs. The glyphs are
more than a convenient shorthand. Each symbolizes the
meaning of the sign it represents. Some glyphs picture
parts of the body ruled by corresponding signs, although
it may take some imagination to discern this. With each
glyph an historical symbol that portrays sign character-
istics is shown.
Characteristics of the Signs
The extent or sphere of a sign's influence on an
individual cannot be ascertained until the horoscope
is drawn up, showing the relation of signs to planets
and houses. Bear in mind that if a sign is a personal
factor in a horoscope its astrological qualities will be
prominent in that person's nature. For example, the
sign occupied by the Sun, which represents the ego
and creative self-expression, and the one placed on the
Ascendant (the rising sign), which governs appearance
and attitudes, describe personal characteristics. Signs
associated with houses that concern outside interests
such as finances or work are not interpreted in the
same manner as those which influence the personality.
Nevertheless, the essential qualities of a sign remain
the same whether expressed in one's character or
applied to less personal areas of activity.

Aries, ruled by the planet Mars, is the natural sign of
the first house. It signifies beginnings and new
enterprises; hence, Aries is indicative of thepioneerspirit.
A cardinal-fire-positive sign, Aries represents
dynamic action, initiative, self-motivation, enthusi-
astic drive, aggressive effort and impulsiveness.
People born when the Sun is in Aries (March
21-April 19) are highly competitive, outgoing,
resourceful, confident and decisive. They step into the
thick of things boldly, sure of themselves, fearless of
adverse consequences, unafraid of failure.
Arians are real go-getters. Aries women are
especially well-equipped for the career world. They
are aggressive, sure in the knowledge that they can
do anything a man or another woman can do and
more. There is no place for male chauvinism in the
life of an Aries woman.
Quick-thinking and impetuous, headstrong and
audacious, Arians often act without giving adequate
consideration to the ultimate results of their actions.
Aries men, cocky and brash, may project a "macho"
image. They perform daring deeds, but many take
reckless and foolhardy chances to prove themselves.
Impatient, Arians are not content to work for years
toward singular goals. Once they lose enthusiasm for
an idea or project, as they quite frequently do, they are
quick to tum to something new. Arians needs to develop
the habit of thinking things through before acting hastily.
In order to realize fulfillment and success, they must leam
to direct their boundless energies toward productive and
attainable objectives.
Arians require the reinforcement of immediate
feedback and tangible rewards if they are to stick with
their endeavors. What Arians lack in persistence, they
make up for in ambition and the will to succeed. They
are natural-born achievers who, because of their
dauntless courage and drive to be first, are leaders in
their peer groups.
Conscious of the importance of appearance, Arians
dress well and act in a self-assured manner. They talk
about their successes but usually neglect to mention
their failures. Arians believe that projecting a
successful image ensures success. The Aries person
projects a confidence that tells the world, "I am ready
for anything," and, more importantly, the Arian is.
Outspoken, Arians are seldom tactful, often
argumentative. An Arian's temper surfaces quickly but
just as quickly evaporates. They are warm human
beings, spontaneous in friendship and ardent in love.
Arians are energetic people who gravitate toward
active jobs and hobbies. Both Aries men and women
are able executives, capable of making decisions and
acting on their own volition. They excel in jobs that
require individual skills.
Most Arians enjoy outdoor sports such as hunting,
tennis and golf. The more daring are often enthusiasts
of auto racing and rougher sports such as football,
wrestling or boxing. Needlework or carving may
appeal to the Arian as an indoor hobby.
Particular physical characteristics are associated

noticeable at the crown of the head where balding is

of red usually colors the hair.

Taurus, a fixed-earth-negative sign, characterizes
purposeful action, steady drive, determined effort,
endurance, reliability, conservatism and fixed attitudes.
Persons bom under a Taurus Sun (April 20-May 20)
work long and hard to achieve their objectives.
Industrious and persevering, they are not easily
discouraged by difficulties; they endure as much
hardship as is necessary to pursue their goals. Taureans
do not jump into things without a great deal of
forethought. Once they choose a course, they stick with
it unless unalterable circumstances dictate otherwise.
Taureans go about their business quietly.
Uncomplaining, they shoulder responsibility with
fortitude, wear down obstacles by refusing to yield
or turn back, and proceed with relentless deter-
mination along their chosen paths.
Set in their ways, Taureans resent anyone who
interferes or attempts to force them to alter their
habits. They try to establish a pattern to their lives.
Taureans do not readily adapt to fluctuating trends
or inconsistent situations and find it difficult to
restructure their plans and actions around changing
circumstances. They need to develop a greater degree
of flexibility. The singularity of purpose and practical
utilization of resources (skills and material assets) that
are basic to their natures compensate largely for the
Taurean lack of enterprise and versatility. Because of
determination and persistence, many Taureans succeed
where others fail. Taureans are patient; they can wait
a long time, years if need be, to act on their plans.
When they do, little can stop them.
Taureans make every effort to obtain creature
comforts and material security. They are as devoted
to their friends and loved ones as they are to the
material goals to which they aspire. Although they
may be possessive, jealous and stubborn, they are
steadfast, sincere and warmhearted as well. Usually
gentle and good-natured, it takes a lot to provoke
them, but when their anger is aroused they are
formidable and unrelenting.
Taureans possess an instinctive sense of color and
beauty which is reflected in their taste in art, their
clothing and their flair for home decor.
Taureans are usually practical money managers and
have an inborn sense of value. A Taurean will buy
one genuine article of real worth instead of two or
three cheap imitations at the same price. From the
possessions they acquire and the money they
accumulate, Taureans derive emotional security and
inner satisfaction.
Taureans are not essentially initiators or idea people;
they are the ones who follow through and get things
done. They are creative but not especially innovative.
Taureans prefer jobs along established, reliable lines
over those which are insecure or risky.
Taureans like to do things with their hands, and
crocheting, flower arranging, gardening, painting, or
sculpting are spare-time interests a Taurean might
enjoy. A love of music might prompt membership in

The natural sign of the third house, it is ruled by
the planet Mercury.
The mutable-air-positive sign, Gemini, typifies
diversified action, intellectual drive, diffuse effort,
dexterity, fluency and attitudes that are both flexible
and skeptical. A Gemini Sun (May 21-June 21) gives
a person a lifelong thirst for knowledge without the
persistence to concentrate on one particular field or
topic for a long period of time.
Geminis leam easily, remember what they leam and
are ever curious to know more. They accept little at
face value or on the basis of popular opinion. Geminis
must find out and prove for themselves, for only in
fact and logic is their skepticism satisfied.
Geminis' interests are broad, but most need to
develop continuity of thought and action. Usually they
have too many overlapping interests or conflicting
objectives, which siphon energy away from main
concerns. However, Geminis are able to handle two
or more separate concepts at the same time. They can
mull over several ideas and work on various endeavors
concurrently. They may splinter their energies and
talents, but Geminis have the capacity to unite the
"splinters" into a cohesive effort toward an overall
goal, and this they must do if they are to reach their
full potentials.
Restless in body and mind, most Geminis have
nervous dispositions. If routine becomes monotonous,
a Gemini is apt to grow fidgity; pencil twirling, toe
tapping, finger drumming or excessive chattering are
attempts at alleviating boredom.
Geminis are non-conformists who resist cumber-
some regulations that constrain their individuality.
They do not function at best in a highly disciplined
or regimented atmosphere.
The Gemini personality gives the impression of
being perpetually lighthearted and carefree. These
people are good company, witty, charming and
entertaining. However, they can be overly clever and
adroit: smooth talkers who are a bit too glib.
Intellectual and conversational skills are two of
Gemini's strongest assets. A variety of interests, the
aptitude to learn and retain knowledge, the capacity
to reason and express ideas, and the ability to think
and act quickly enable Geminis to cope with almost
any circumstances that arise. Their success lies in part
in a versatile approach to life and the ease with which
they are able to adapt to ever-changing situations. If
they cannot adjust (and Geminis are wise enough to
know when they cannot), they deftly sidestep obstacles
that impede progress. For Gemini, there is always
another, perhaps more interesting, course ahead.
The Gemini temperament is best suited to an
occupation that offers intellectual stimulation and
permits diversified activity, though not necessarily of
a physically strenuous nature.
Fencing, jogging, reading, traveling, writing or just
visiting and chatting with friends appeal to most
Geminis during free hours.
Typically, a Gemini has an ever-youthful appear-
ance which is emphasized by refined, clear-cut
features, alert, twinkling eyes, a slightly turned up
nose, quick movements, an agile step and a slender
build. As with all human signs, body and facial hair

Cancerians are somewhat retiring and unassuming,

Cancer people are difficult to understand because

Cancerians do not*readily reveal themselves, partly

Cancerians face a need to overcome lack of
confidence and a tendency toward self-centeredness;
they can do so by tapping the deep well of emotional

Cancerians seek material as well as emotional
security. They need a few dollars to fall back on in

save part of their earnings for the proverbial rainy day

Noncombative by nature, Cancerians do not like

Cancerians are warm and affectionate. Many are
self-sacrificing in love. They can become overly

they remember the kindnesses others bestow upon

Natural-bom hosts and hostesses, Cancerians have a

acquaintances alike. They respond intuitively to the
needs of people whom they encounter. Many serve well
in public capacities because most people feel comfortable

From their jobs, Cancerians need both the
reassurance of approval and a paycheck that equals

things or people, for both men and women of this sign

Authoritative action, power-seeking drive, noble

Whatever Leos do, they do with dramatic flair. It
is almost impossible for them not to attract attention.
Leos harbor much pride in themselves; they try to
live up to a reputation of honesty, integrity, reliability
and generosity. Because self-esteem is important to
Leos, they seldom act in a manner that is demeaning
or might give them cause for regret.
Leos stand firm in their ideas and beliefs. They can
be opinionated, stubborn, bossy and egotistical despite
the fact that they are basically broad-minded, just and
kind. Many tend to get all wrapped up in their own

As a rule, Leos are popular. They work hard, and
play hard. Warm, gregarious and fun-loving, they are

friendship, they form many lasting associations.
Leos' flamboyant style and personal magnetism
appeal to the opposite sex. In romance Leos are ardent,
affectionate, sentimental and extravagant. Love is
important to them; they need someone to adore,
admire and flatter them, for in love, as in everything
else, Leos must play the leading role. If they do not
receive the affection and attention they need, their
vanity and pride suffer as well as their hearts.
Leos have optimistic, cheerful, good-natured
dispositions. At times they are hot-headed, but do not
harbor resentment or thoughts of revenge. There is
too much in life for Leos to do and enjoy for them
to waste energy in self-defeating efforts.
Although Leo is a barren sign, it rules children. Leo
parents are not noted for large families, but most are
genuinely fond of youngsters. They demand obedience
and respect from their offspring (no one questions the
authority of a Leo mother or father): however, Leos
are demonstrative parents who express their love in
ways that children can understand.
The ability to take charge, to exert authority and
to execute responsibility combined with a natural
aptitude for the spotlight qualify the Leo individual
for a leader's role. Proud and ambitious they are ill
at ease in subordinate positions. Women of this sign
are as discontented in secondary posts as are the men.
Whatever course Leos choose, they will probably be
found at the helm eventually.

Although career-oriented, Virgos are more interested
in doing an efficient job than in taking over as boss. Most
do not resent the detailed work that others consider

much on trivia that they "can't see the forest for the
trees." Virgo's strongest point is the ability to analyze
data and reach reasonable and accurate conclusions
though they need to leam to distinguish between the
relevant and the extraneous.
Because they are basically insecure, Virgos are often
indecisive. The drive toward perfection that most of
them exhibit is a means of bolstering self-confidence.
Meticulous in everything they do, Virgos can be real
"nit-pickers" who expect their associates to be as
fastidious and efficient as they are.
Most Virgos are worriers who fret over anything
and everything.
Diet and hygiene are important to Virgos. Many are
vegetarians; some make a fetish of cleanliness, bathing
several times a day.
Virgos are modest, gentle, somewhat reticent indi-
viduals. They seldom fritter away precious time in
pointless socializing and have little regard for purely
hedonistic activities. Most are drawn to persons who
are intellectually stimulating or who share similar job
interests.
Thoughtful of friends in practical ways, Virgos are
more apt to help needy acquaintances help themselves
than to extend outright handouts.
Undemonstrative and inhibited, most Virgos appear
indifferent to romance. A Virgo's standards in a mate
are high, perhaps more idealistic than realistic, and
many choose to remain single rather than lower their
expectations.
Virgos are happiest in jobs that serve a useful
purpose. To achieve fulfillment, they must feel that
their work is of practical value to society.
Herb gardens, weaving, pets, volunteer service,
walking and writing provide healthy spare time outlets
for Virgos' nervous tension.
Most Virgos are meticulously groomed, though
some may be so occupied with mental details that they

Libra
The scales is the symbol for
Libra, the sign of balance
and justice. This theme is
further pictured in the
glyph, an inverted crescent
above the double line of
power, which symbolizes
the soul of justice ruling the
Scepter of Authority. The
glyph resembles the setting sun; appropriately, Libra
is the natural sign of the seventh house, the cusp of
which is the sunset portion of a horoscope. Venus is
the planetary ruler of Libra, a cardinal-air-positive
sign. The sign rules the kidneys.
Libra stands for cooperative action, approval-
seeking drive, mentally motivated effort, harmony,
teamwork and impartial attitudes. Persons with a
Libra Sun (September 23-October 22) are mild-
mannered and peace-loving. Librans try to resolve
their problems by arbitration rather than by force.
Violence is repugnant to Librans; they will fight,
especially if principles of justice are at stake, but
usually only as a last resort.
Librans like to argue in the sense of debate, not in
the sense of quarreling. They are strategists who
outsmart their opponents. Subtly persuasive, they are
masters at the art of suggestion. If overt persuasion
does not work, a Libran will plant the seed of an idea
and nurture it so skillfully that opponents frequently
fail to realize they are playing into Libra's hands.
The gentle, amiable, courteous manner of most
Librans may fool others into thinking they are push-
overs, but a Libran is not weak. Instead of Drawn or
physical intimidation Librans rely on intelligence and
diplomacy to get their way.
An instinctive sense of fair play motivates Librans.
They weigh all aspects of an issue before forming a
final judgment. In so doing, they frequently appear
to be vacillating; however, once Librans arrive at
decisions they back them up fully, sure that their
conclusions are unbiased and just.
Librans try hard to please others because the
approval of their peers is necessary to their inner
security. They need companionship. A Libran is
happier and more productive as part of a team or
partnership endeavor than when working alone.
Socially inclined, they instinctively know how to
get along with their associates and acquaintances.
Although they seldom display anger, when a Libran s
temper does erupt, one can expect a stormy session
while it lasts.
Librans possess a highly developed sense of aesthetic
sensitivity. Everything about these people spells
refinement and graciousness. A Libran s choice of
friends, clothing and furnishings reflects an aversion
for the ugly, the crude, the vulgar, the garish. They
shy away from anything or anyone who offends their
sense of delicacy and good taste.
Because Librans desire a companion with whom to
share their life, they are susceptible to romance. The
Libran is a romantic, tender, passionate lover who enjoys
the intimacy of a candlelight dinner for two. Few Librans
go through life without marrying at least once.
The lifestyle of most Librans mirrors a yearning for
luxury and the finer things of life. They are not
extravagant in the strictest sense of the word: few
squander their money or buy indiscriminately. They do
however, spend as much as they can afford and more
on beautiful possessions and expensive social habits.
Librans may have little money in the bank, but they
derive great pleasure from what their money buys.
Librans prefer to work in congenial surroundings
that are pleasing to the eye. Discordancies of any kind
upset and distract them. Harmony and cooperation
are important to a Libran s job performance.
Librans enjoy intellectual pastimes such as chess,
word games, reading and puzzles. Cultural activities
such as the ballet, concerts, the opera and art also
appeal to them.

Scorpio
Historically, the symbol for
Scorpio is the scorpion,
whose venomous sting
characterizes the biting
sarcasm attributed to this
sign. Some authorities also
ascribe the eagle and/or the
phoenix to Scorpio. The
eagle expresses the potential
for greatness inherent in this sign; the phoenix represents
the resurrectional or regenerative powers associated with
Scorpio. The glyph represents female genitalia; it
resembles the glyph for Virgo, but the last leg of the
Scorpio glyph is open, indicating sexual activity. The
Scorpio glyph is sometimes written with an arrowhead
to better distinguish it from that of Virgo.
Scorpio rules the sex organs and rectum and has part
rulership over the human reproductive system.
Traditionally Mars was given rulership of this sign and
more recently, Pluto. Scorpio is the natural sign of
the eighth house. It is associated with regeneration,
sexual expression, death, metamorphosis, transfor-
mation and life after death.
Intense action, passionate drive, resolute effort,
endurance, unflinching courage, unswerving purpose
and inscrutable attitudes are qualities basic to this
fixed-water-negative sign. The innate power in
Scorpio can be likened to that of a seething volcano,
impossible to contain.
A typical Scorpio (October 23-November 21) is
strong-willed, masterful, obdurate, stout-hearted.
Scorpiosfear nothing. They plowinto anything that suits
their purposes, overriding opposition and pushing aside
obstacles much as a steam roller clears a path. The
capacity to overcome almost insurmountable barriers
is largely responsible for the success Scorpios achieve.
Their weakness, if any exists, is in the tendency to drive
themselves too hard. Scorpios do not admit to fatigue
or illness until they reach the point of exhaustion where
they can no longer continue on will power alone. The
same characteristics that enable Scorpios to accomplish
great deeds can lead to nithlessness, violence and cruelty
if energy is misdirected.
Scorpios are reserved and taciturn yet argumen-
tative and capable of explosive rage. They never
pretend to agree with anyone in the interests of peace
or harmony and can be brusque and sarcastic. Most
are able to get across in a few words more than other
people can express in a paragraph or two. Often, only
a piercing look is all that is needed for a Scorpio to
make a point.
Despite the emotional depth and passion in their
nature, Scorpios seldom reveal their inner feelings by
facial expresion or mannerism except in anger. A stony
mask hides their secrets well.
Selective in their choice of companions and intensely
loyal to the chosen few, Scorpios can be vindictive
and vengeful toward anyone who hurts their friends
or loved ones. There is no in-between for Scorpios.
They approve or disapprove, agree or disagree, like
or dislike, love or hate—they are never indifferent.
Scorpios are passionate lovers who are inclined to be
jealous and possessive.
These people possess a natural curiosity and suspicion
that is not satisfied with pat answers and superficialities.
They probe until they ferret out any concealed facts.
Naturally shrewd, Scorpios are seldom fooled or
victimized by swindlers and con-artists.
Most Scorpios have the physical strength to carry
out strenuous tasks as well as the intelligence to handle
intricate mental problems. They are industrious and
thorough as employees, masterful and domineering as
employers.
Many Scorpios are sports enthusiasts who prefer
demolition derbies, football and hunting over less
violent sports. Other sideline activities might include
herpetology, secret societies and the occult.

ically describes dual

A mutable-fire-positive sign, Sagittarius is
representative of zealous action, idealistic drive, eager
effort, positive thought, adventurous spirit and a
philosophical attitude. This sign is linked to religion,
spiritual concepts, and moral and ethical standards.
A person with a Sagittarius Sun (November
22-December 21) is a high-minded individual who is
honest and straightforward. Sagittarians seek the truth
in the most profound sense, and speak the truth as
they believe it to be. They see things in broad terms,
leaving the specifics to somebody else.
Sagittarians greet the world with verve and
confidence. They aim their arrows boldly toward the
stars, confident of success. Frequently Sagittarians
bring problems on themselves because they are in too
much of a hurry. They are overly optimistic,
indifferent to details and prone to making impulsive
decisions. Consequently, they trip over their own feet
literally and figuratively.
Sagittarians take their setbacks philosophically.
Failure does not hinder their chances for future success,
for they are quick to pick up the pieces and launch
a fresh start.
Sagittarians are goal-oriented; however, they are
not so driven that they stoop to petty tactics in order
to reach their objectives. Unwilling to compromise
their ideals or principles to get ahead, they forge
onward immune to the blandishments of greed and
self-serving interests. Sagittarians are not looking for
free rides; they refuse to be beholden to anyone for
their success. They trust their own abilities to get them
to the top.
The Sagittarian is a daring free spirit who will not
be chained to a confining life style, to freedom-
threatening relationships or to narrow ideas. These
people want to come and go when they please, eat
when they are hungry and say what they think without
varnishing the truth.
Sagittarians are physically active and intellectually
aware. They are explorers at heart who are interested
in distant places and profound mental concepts.
Whether physical or intellectual in nature, their
exploits are motivated by the desire to learn.
Sagittarians are outgoing and friendly, though
sometimes they come on too strongly as backslappers
or practical jokers. Utterlycandid, most Sagittarians are
short on tact. They are impatient and quick-tempered.
Even so, they are immensely popular; much of their
exuberance rubs off on their friends and associates. They
are respected for their sincerity and good will, liked for
their generosity and sense of humor.
Most Sagittarians are flirtatious, but few are
seriously interested in romance. They are naturally
chary of involvements that might curtail their
activities. A desire for freedom causes many
Sagittarians to remain single or marry late in life.
Sagittarians are extremely versatile They are averse
to a rigid routine and a sedentary way of life. A job
atmosphere that satisfies the restless Sagittarian
temperament is as important to their success as the
job itself.
Sagittarians enjoy active hobbies and those that are
mentally stimulating. Archery horseback riding.

Aquarius
Aquarius, the sign of
compassion, is aptly
symbolized by the water-
bearer generously pouring
the waters of humanitari-
anism. Curiously, the

a graphic representation of
electro-magnetic waves,
which come under the dominion of Uranus, one of the

originated long before the phenomenon of electro-
magnetic radiation was discovered. Uranus shares
rulership of this sign with Saturn, the traditional ruler.
Aquarius is the natural sign of the eleventh house and
governs the ankles, shins and circulatory system.
A fixed-air-positive sign, Aquarius signifies
progressive action, altruistic drive, community effort,
inventive genius, unpredictability and unconventional
attitudes.
Aquarians (January 20-February 18), never quite
satisfied with the status quo, are the vanguards of
social reform and community betterment programs.
Humanity at large is their concern. Aquarians are far
ahead of the times in thought and action, A farsighted
approach to the problems that beset humankind lends
to the potential to affect great advances in the quality
of life. Traditionalists frequently resist Aquarian-
inspired changes but Aquarians do not give up easily.
With determined effort, they often overthrow firmly
entrenched conventions.
Aquarians are a paradox in human nature. They are
stubborn, inconsistent, unselfish, conceited, tolerant,
impatient, rebellious, peace-loving. Erratic attitudes and
behavior make them difficult to understand.
Aquarians value their freedom and privacy, yet they
are the "joiners" of the zodiac. The satisfaction they
derive from the friendship and companionship
provided by group activities is essential to their inner
confidence and sense of well-being.
Aquarians have a large assortment of friends, male
and female, from all walks of life. They choose their
friends on the basis of common concerns and
intellectual rapport, not status or background. Neither
bigoted nor snobbish, Aquarians care little about the
trappings of society. Instead they look for the
redeeming values in a person and seldom make moral
judgments about another person's character or
lifestyle. Most Aquarians accept people as they are.
Aquarian objectives for reform lie on a broader plane,
devoted to furthering the general welfare.
Although their interest in people and the human
condition is genuine, Aquarians do not get emotionally
involved with the majority of their associates or the
causes they promote. They view their relationships
and activities from an impersonal, intellectual
standpoint. Aquarians must maintain their individu-
ality in all relationships, including marriage, if the
relationship is to survive.
Aquarians are fascinated by that which is different.
They tend to choose jobs that allow freedom of
thought and originality of action.
In their spare time Aquarians like to experiment with
novel ideas. Many devise useful gadgets. Some
Aquarians like to tinker with motorcycles and sports
cars; others create original designs for clothing and
jewelry. Other Aquarian pastimes include citizen's band
or ham radio, fraternal clubs or sororities and flying.
A classic profile distinguished by strangely
fascinating, deep-set eyes is typically Aquarian.
Although they are usually well-proportioned,
incongruous movements and an uncoordinated walk
give the impression they are not.

Pisces
Two fish swimming in
opposing directions while
fastened together by the
silver cord of life symbolize
the dual aspects and
confusion attributed to
Pisces. The glyph supports
the same theme. Pisces, the
natural sign of the twelfth

associated with the lymphatic system.
A mutable-water-negative sign, Pisces epitomizes
subdued action, lethargic drive, disorganized effort,
compassion, martyrdom and vacillating attitudes.
Persons whose Sun falls in Pisces at birth (February
19-March 20) are gentle, modest, elusive, thoughtful and
sympathetic. Pisceans, sensitive to the needs and feelings
of fellow human beings, are deeply moved by the
tragedies that befall others.
Pisceans identify with their surroundings and
associates; chameleon-like, many assume the opinions
and moods of whomever they are with at a particular
moment. They are not necessarily equivocating or
intentionally insincere, but they are extremely
impressionable and tend to drift with the situations
in which they find themselves.
Pisceans respond with equal intensity to joy as to
sadness. Therefore, their moods range from the heights
of ecstacy to the depths of despair. Like all water signs,
Pisceans attempt to protect their emotional sensitivity.
They may feign indifference in order to shut out people
who are capable of inflicting emotional hurts;
however, they brood inwardly over harsh treatment
and slights, real or fancied. Many Pisceans fall into
the trap of self-pity. Some have difficulty controlling
and masking their feelings and may burst into tears
when they feel sad or rejected.
Idealistic and trusting, Pisceans frequently blind
themselves to the harsh realities of everyday living. They
may have good intentions, but many are unable to deal
effectively with practical responsibilities. Pisceans are
not motivated by the lure of worldly success. They think
in terms of "happy" rather than "dollars" and strive for
inner harmony. If they manage to achieve this harmony
without losing themselves in a world of escapism and
illusion, they become more self-assured, better able to
direct their efforts productively.
Pisceans possess a natural sense of rhythm. Under
suitable circumstances, many are able to convert their
dreams into lasting contributions to the arts in the form
of music, poetry or the dance.
Pisceans are mild-tempered, compliant, yielding and
tenderhearted. Easy targets for sob stories, they take
their friends' troubles to heart and suffer for others
as they do for themselves. They seldom refuse a
request for help and may sacrifice their own interests
for the welfare of others.
Romantic love is essential to Pisceans; without it
they feel lonely and unfulfilled. Because they need to
know they are loved, appreciated and desirable,
Pisceans seek attentive mates who can give them the
constant reassurances they crave.
A compatible job environment is necessary to
Pisceans' productivity. They do not function well when
they are ill at ease, unhappy or discontented. In a setting
that inspires encouragement, Pisceans can accomplish
wonders, for they are adaptable and multi-talented.
Sideline interests that appeal to Pisceans are mostly
those associated with water, rhythm and the mystic
such as scuba diving, fishing, dancing, poetry,
spiritualism and Yoga.
Some Pisceans tend to be plump, but even so they
appear delicate, almost fragile. They have liquid eyes
which seem to mirror the depths of the soul. Pursed
lips and a small chin make the lovely eyes more
prominent. Most Pisceans have dainty hands and tiny
feet. They move with the effortless grace of a dancer.
Occupations that are in some way related to the sea,
fish, oil, beverages, places of confinement (hospitals.

Planets in Our Solar System
Planetary Motion
The planets travel at varying rates of speed as they follow
their orbits around the Sun. Because a planetary orbit
is elliptical, some points of the orbital path lie closer to
the Sun than others. The nearer to the Sun a planet
moves, the faster it travels along its orbit. The point of
closest approach to the Sun is the perihelion of orbit;
the farthest point is the aphelion. The Moon's joumey
through the zodiac depends upon its orbit of Earth. The
point in the lunar orbit nearest the Earth is the perigee;
the most distant point is the apogee.
Distant planets take longer to complete their orbits
and, therefore, longer to traverse the zodiac. The
planets move through the zodiac in order of fastest
moving to slowest as follows: The Moon, Mercury,
Venus, the Sun, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus,
Neptune and Pluto.
The time it takes a planet to orbit the Sun is called the
period of orbit; the time a planet spends completing one
circuit of the zodiac is the zodiacal period. The average
longitudinal distance (distance in arc) a planet moves
each day is the mean daily motion. When a planet moves
faster than the mean daily motion it is said to be in swift
motion; when it moves more slowly than the mean, it
is said to be slow of course.
Planetary motion is described as direct (D),
retrograde (R) or stationary (S). Actually, all planetary
motion is forward or direct. Relative motion is not.
For example, when sitting in a parked car have you
suddenly hit the brake because your car started to drift
backward only to realize that your car had not moved?
The car beside yours had pulled ahead.
You may experience a similar sensation when riding
on a train. If parallel traffic moves faster than the train,
you feel like you are moving in reverse, providing
there are no landmarks or changing scenery to help
you get your bearings. If the train is moving at the
exact speed and in the same direction as traffic, you
seem to be motionless or stationary. You are not
passing the traffic nor is it pulling ahead of you. In
other words, the relative motion between the train and
the traffic is zero. Once one or the other speeds up,
slows down or alters direction, there is a change in
relative motion.
If a fast-moving car is assumed to be a stationary
reference point, a more slowly moving train is traveling
backward from the car's point of view. From the train's
point of view, the car is moving ahead.
Planetary motion is much more complicated than
that of either a car or a train. Celestial measurements
depend upon the frame of reference of the observer
and the angle of observation. For astrological mea-
surements, Earth is the designated frame of reference;
as observed from Earth, another planet may appear
to be in retrograde motion (moving backward in the
zodiac), stationary (motionless, stopped), or in direct
motion (moving forward in the zodiac). The only time
a planet is stationary is during the transition from
direct motion to retrograde or vice versa. A planet is
said to "make a station" at the degree of the zodiac
where it apparently stops.
A planet has greater influence in the horoscope
when it is stationary because its energy is concentrated

=== Page 32 ===
42 Compendium of Astrology
and focused at the degree of the zodiac it occupies.
Retrograde motion does not alter a planet's energy
principles, but the manifestation in the horoscope may
be of a less overt nature than otherwise. Direct motion
allows for an outward expression of planetary energy
as dictated by sign position, house placement and
aspects.
The Sun and those planets whose orbits lie between
the Sun and the Asteroid Belt are designated inner
planets. In addition to the Sun these are the Moon,
Mercury, Venus and Mars. The inner planets are also
called personal or "character building" planets. Jupiter.
Saturn, Uranus, Neptune and Pluto orbit outside the
Asteroid Belt and are termed outer, impersonal or
"event" planets.
Figure 5. Planetary Orbits
The orbital paths in order from the Sun are: Mercury,
Venus, Earth and Moon, Mars, the Asteroid Belt,
Jupiter, Satum, Uranus, Neptune and Pluto. Due to
orbital eccentricities, Pluto's orbit was inside that of
Neptune's during 1978-1980. Such eccentricities support
the belief that an undiscovered planet(s) may exist.
Asteroids
In late 1977, astronomer Charles Kowal discovered
a heavenly body that appears to have some of the
physical characteristics of a planet but is within the
size range of an asteroid, being only about four
hundred miles in diameter; however, its orbit falls in
the area of the outer planets, not in the Asteroid Belt.
For the time being, this body has been dubbed a
planetoid and named Chiron. It will be interesting to
see what astrological influence, if any, study of this
tiny planet-like body will reveal in the future.
Study of four other asteroids, which were
discovered in the early nineteenth century, has been
stepped up since 1973. These asteroids are Ceres, Pallas
(Pallas Athena), Juno and Vesta. There is no general
agreement as to th? astrological significance or
rulerships attached to these asteroids.
Many consider the zodiacal position of an asteroid
at birth to be a sensitive point in the horoscope that
describes general conditions that emerge later in life
when planets progress to or aspect its position.
Evidence is as yet too scanty to provide an accurate
evaluation. In 1980, the asteroids were not generally
accepted as basic elements of natal astrology.
Planet Classifications
Planets are classified benefic or malefic according to
the ease with which planetary energy may be utilized
constructively under difficult astrological circum-
stances. These terms are somewhat misleading;
planetary energy is neither "good" (benefic) nor "bad"
(malefic) per se. Like sign traits, planetary qualities
can manifest in a positive (constructive) or negative
(destructive) manner. However, improper use of the
energies of benefics is potentially less damaging than
misuse of the energies of malefics.
Jupiter is the Greater Benefic; Venus, the Lesser
Benefic. The Sun, Moon and Mercury are moderately
benefic. Satum is the Greater Malefic; Mars, the Lesser
Malefic. Uranus, Neptune and Pluto complete the list
of malefics.
Planets are also classed as masculine or feminine.
Mercury, which is androgynous (neutral), assumes the
gender of the sign in which it is placed.
Planets are described as hot, warm, cold, dry, moist,
electric, magnetic, fruitful and/or barren.
Planetary Standing
The strength of a planet in a horoscope depends upon
sign position, horoscope placement, aspects and motion.
Each planet rules one or two signs. A planet that
occupies a sign it rules is dignified. A dignified planet
is strengthened, and its energy is manifested in pure
form. Aside from that of dignity, one other sign, called

=== Page 33 ===
Planets in Our Solar System 43
the sign of exaltation, augments a planet's drive and
allows a high quality of expression. A planet is
essentially dignified when it falls in a sign of dignity
or exaltation. Planets that occupy a sign of essential
dignity command added strength in the horoscope.
When a planet occupies the sign opposite that of
dignity, it is in the sign of detriment: when a planet is
in the sign opposite that of exaltation, it is in fall.
Planetary action is weakened when a planet is in its sign
of detriment or fall; then it is considered to be debilitated.
Mutual reception strengthens planetary principles
even if a planet is in a sign of debilitation. Mutual
reception occurs when two planets are each placed in
the other's sign of essential dignity. For example, if
the Sun is in Cancer or Taurus, the Moon's signs of
rulership and exaltation, respectively, at the same time
the Moon is in Leo of Aries, the Sun's signs of essential
dignity (the Sun rules Leo and is exalted in Aries), these
two planets are in mutual reception. Planets in mutual
reception support each other; they are deemed as
effective as if each were placed in its own sign of
essential dignity.
If a planet occupies a sign other than one of its
essential dignity or debilitation, and it is not in mutual
reception with another planet, it is said to be peregrine.
A peregrine planet lacks standing: its dynamic
expression may be inhibited or reduced depending
upon other elements in the horoscope. Planetary
strength cannot be determined on the basis of one
criterion; planetary standing in the horoscope depends
upon all relevant factors.
A specific degree of the zodiac, called the degree of
exaltation, is assigned to each planet, A planet
functions freely in the degree of exaltation. At the
opposite point of the zodiac, the degree of fall, natural
expression of planetary energy is constrained.
A planet is accidentally dignified and thereby
strengthened when it is placed in its natural house in
the horoscope or within five degrees of one of the four
angles of the horoscope. The angles are: (1) the
Ascendant and (2) its opposite point, the Descendant,
(3) the Medium Coeli, commonly called the
Midheaven and abbreviated MC, which is the highest
point or culminating degree of the ecliptic, and (4) the
point opposite the MC, the Imum Coeli, customarily
shortened to 1C. The MC and IC are mistakenly
referred to as the zenith and nadir respectively; the
zenith and nadir are the poles of the horizon not the
ecliptic. The closer to the MC a planet falls, the more
powerful it is in the horoscope.
Planets that occupy the southern hemisphere of the
horoscope (above the horizontal axis) are more
influential than those in the northern hemisphere
(lower half of the horoscope) except for the Moon
whose natural position is in the night section below
the horizontal axis. The Moon functions equally well
above or below the horizon.
Planets that are placed in a house of natural
rulership or in a house they rule in the horoscope are
given greater emphasis regardless of the hemisphere
in which they are located.
A planet's effectiveness in the horoscope depends in
part upon the number and type of aspects it forms with
other planets. Through aspects, the energies of two
planets may unite and support mutual action; energies
may combine to nullify or weaken the action of one or
both planets involved; the action of one planet may
obstruct and frustrate the action of another in aspect.
Energies may oppose or they may blend harmoniously,
depending upon the type and strength of the aspect and
the nature of the planets involved,
A planet is said to be well aspected if it forms
harmonious aspects with other planets; if it forms
disharmonious aspects, it is said to be adversely
aspected or afflicted. Planets that form a large number
of harmonious aspects are more powerful than those
which form few aspects or are afflicted. The energies
of well-aspected planets flow smoothly and naturally.
The energy of an afflicted planet is in some way
distorted or weakened. A planet that forms no aspects
has no channel through which to direct its energy; its
influence in the horoscope is limited.
Planets moving in direct motion are emphasized
over those in retrograde motion; stationary planets
supercede both in terms of planetary standing, other
factors being equal.
One of the most important planets in a horoscope is
the planet that rules the sign on the Ascendant. This
planet is the horoscope ruler (chart ruler). If this planet
occupies a sign of detriment and or torms few aspects,
or is otherwise weakened, its importance is not lessened,
although it lacks strength in the horoscope. A weak or
afflicted horoscope ruler makes personal expression more
difficult since this planet is overshadowed by other
energies. This in itself is significant.
