Characteristics of the Planets
The glyphs for the planets are derived from the same
astrological symbols as the glyphs for the signs (Chapter
2) with the addition of a dot known as the Point of
Manifestation. When it is placed in the center of the
Circle of Spirit the resulting glyph represents the Sun and
signifies the emergence of the life force contained within
the Circle of Spirit. Planetary glyphs are commonly
referred to as symbols rather than glyphs.
The Sun
The Sun crosses the zodiac once each year and
spends about a month in each sign. The Sun's
mean daily motion is 59' 8" (fifty-nine minutes
and eight seconds). Its motion is always direct,
never retrograde or stationary.
The Sun, referred to as a planet in astrological
terminology, is also called a luminary or the Greater
Light. It is masculine, hot, dry, electric and essentially
barren, but it may be moderately fruitful if placed in
a fruitful sign.
An intensely hot star that emits life-sustaining
energy and heat, the Sun is essential to life on Earth.
In a horoscope, it represents a person's vital life force,
the ego, the individuality, the creative powers, the
drive for self-expression. A person's urge to achieve
is expressed through the Sun in accordance with the
sign it occupies and is directed toward areas defined
by the Sun's house placement. This most important
planet acts as a channel in the horoscope for all
planetary energies to the extent indicated by the
aspects between the Sun and the other planets.
The Sun embodies the principle of fatherhood; it
signifies a person's natural father and a woman's
husband in the horoscope. It rules children in general
and one's first offspring in particular.
The Sun symbolizes authority in the sense of
sovereignty and power as opposed to bureaucracy. A
well-placed Sun adds leadership ability; it reinforces a
person's capacity to take charge of affairs and to retain
command of the situations that arise. A person whose
Sun falls in a debilitating sign or is out of harmony with
other planets finds it difficult to express basic drives and
utilize talents. Natural vitality may be weakened.
The Sun has dominion from age twenty-four to
thirty-four, the years when most people begin their
families and try to establish themselves in life.
Developmental stages of life are more fully discussed
in Chapter 28.
The heart, back, spine, spinal cord and the right side
of the body are ruled by the Sun. It shares rulership over
the general glandular system with the planet Jupiter.
The Sun governs heads of state, gambling, gold
metal, daylight; Sunday and the number one. It is
associated with entertainment, speculation and all that
is showy, ornate or ostentatious.
The fifth house is the natural house of the Sun. It
rules the sign of Leo, which is the natural sign of the
fifth house. The Sun is dignified in Leo, exalted in
Aries, detrimented in Aquarius and in fall in Libra.
The degree of exaltation for the Sun is 19° Aries; the
degree of fall is 19° Libra.
The Moon
The Moon, Earth's satellite and the swiftest
moving "planet," completes one circuit of the
zodiac in a little less than twenty-eight days.
It averages two and one-half days in each
sign at a time. The mean daily motion is
13° 10' (thirteen degrees and ten minutes) and is
always direct. The Moon may be called a luminary
or the Lesser Light. It is feminine, cold, moist,
magnetic and fruitful.
Emotions are governed by the Moon. It indicates
the way people react emotionally to the situations and
people they encounter, and particularly how they
relate to women. The Moon describes the mother-child
relationship; in the horoscope it represents a person's
mother and a man's wife. The Moon reflects the way
people think of and feel toward their motheiis but does
not necessarily describe the mother's true nature.
The formative years from birth to age seven are
ruled by the Moon. The planet is associated with one's
inherited tendencies, early background and childhood
development.
The Moon is linked to the subconscious; it has much
to do with the memory, although it does not rule either
the concrete or abstract mind.
The Moon is passive, changeable, more fluctuating
than any other planet. It is the receiver of energy. The
Moon takes on the character of the sign it is in and of
the planets with which it is aspected in the horoscope.
The stomach, breasts, mammary glands, the womb,
conception, the fluids of the body in general and the left
side of the body are ruled by the Moon. It also governs
o

=== Page 35 ===
Planets in Our Solar Systeni 45
glandular processes and the natural body functions,
especially the female functions. The Moon is responsible
in part for bleeding because it has general rulership over
the fluids of the body and rules the blood serum,
although it does not specifically rule the blood.
An afflicted Moon can give rise to bleeding problems,
digestive upsets, difficulty in establishing an easy rapport
with the public and disharmonious relations with
women. A well-aspected Moon gives one the capacity
to create a comfortable atmosphere in almost any place
or situation, for it represents an instinctive sensitivity
to the needs and feelings of the public.
The Moon expresses the maternal instinct and the
essence of motherhood. It rules the home, water (in
conjunction with Neptune), the tides, silver, the night,
Monday and the number two. It also rules that which
is commonplace, ordinary, proletarian.
The fourth house is the natural house of the Moon.
It is dignified in Cancer, exalted in Taurus, detrimented
in Capricorn and in fall in Scorpio. The degree of
exaltation is 3° Taurus; the degree of fall is 3° Scorpio.
Mercury
■ m With the exception of the Moon, Mercury
is the fastest moving planet. It orbits the Sun
y J in approximately eighty-eight days, but
because of retrograde motion it takes about
a year to traverse the zodiac. Mercury passes
through a sign in less than three weeks when motion
is direct; it spends eight to ten weeks in a sign when
it is retrograde. The retrograde period averages three
and one-half weeks; the stationary period lasts from
a few hours up to three days as motion changes from
direct to retrograde or from retrograde to direct. Mean
daily motion is 1023'. Because Mercury is always
within 28° of the Sun's zodiacal position, it must
occupy the same sign as the Sun, the preceding sign
or the following sign.
Mercury is cold, magnetic and androgynous. It
assumes the gender of the sign it occupies; it is dry
when masculine and moist when feminine.
The mind, the mental processes and all forms of
communication including travel, touch, use of the
telephone, speaking and writing are ruled by Mercury.
Mercury takes on the character of the sign in which
it is posited and reflects the nature of the planets with
which it is configurated (aspected). Its placement in the
horoscope has a great deal to do with an individual's
innate intellectual and communicative skills. The sign
Mercury relates to a person's thinking habits, reasoning
ability and the capacity to formulate ideas and to
verbalize thoughts. The house in which Mercury is
placed describes the things about which a person thinks
and talks and where the individual gets ideas.
A well-placed Mercury confers dexterity, an agile,
perceptive mind, the ability to form judgments based
upon logic and sound reasoning, and the capacity to
express knowledge and ideas fluently through speech
or writing.
A lesser-placed Mercury gives the tendency to think
in broad terms, to deal intellectually with generalities
rather than particulars. Judgment is based on the
general picture rather than specific facts. A debilitated
Mercury indicates absent-mindedness, a tendency to
daydream, and sometimes clumsiness.
When Mercury is retrograde in the natal horoscope,
the individual is inclined to be introspective, subjective
in thinking and hesitant about expressing ideas aloud.
A stationary Mercury intensifies the intellectual and
communicative expression as described by sign
position, house placement and aspects.
The planet is associated with ages seven to fifteen, the
learning years during which an individual acquires basic
learning experiences and essential education.
Mercury rules the arms, hands, shoulders, lungs, solar
plexus, abdomen, intestines, the thymus gland, the
nervous system and the respiratory system. It also
governs the intellect and physical (motor) coordination.
In the horoscope. Mercury denotes a person's close
relatives other than parents, especially brothers and
sisters.
Mercury has dominion over messages, letters, books,
magazines, the signing of documents, neighbors and the
immediate neighborhood, commuter travel,
transportation facilities, paper, mercury (the metal),
Wednesday and the number five.
Mercury is the natural ruler of two houses, the third
and the sixth. This planet rules two signs, Gemini and
Virgo, and is, of course, dignified in both. Mercury
is exalted in Aquarius, detrimented in Sagittarius and
Pisces and in fall in Leo. The degree of exaltation is
15° Aquarius; the degree of fall is 15° Leo.

Retrograde Jupiter is indicative of the deep thinker,

Jupiter rules ages forty-five to fifty-seven, a

knees, the spleen, skin and teeth. Arthritis, rheuma-
tism, chills and diseases of the bones are under its
dominion. Chronic ailments are attributed, at least in
part, to Satum.
Each revolution of the horoscope that a planet
completes beginning with the natal position is called
a cycle. The first half of the cycle is the preparatory
or initial phase; the second half of the cycle is the
culminating or completion phase. As Satum moves
through the zodiac, it returns to the same position as
in the natal horoscope about every twenty-nine to
thirty years. Each Satum cycle completes a stage of
development in the life of the individual. Saturn-
induced discipline and restriction become easier to deal
with in each succeeding cycle.
Satum is associated with the age of full maturity,
the years fifty-seven to seventy. It is during this period
that most people grasp the total implications of their
life experiences and reap what they have sown.
In the horoscope Satum represents older persons.
It may signify the father or husband. Satum rules
politics, time, coal, lead, Saturday and the number
eight. It stands for that which is conservative, regular,
constant, conscientiftus, prudent, binding, suppres-
sing, old and austere.
The tenth and eleventh are the natural houses of
Satum. It is dignified in Capricorn and Aquarius,
exalted in Libra, detrimented in Cancer and Leo and
in fall in Aries. The degree of exaltation is 21° Libra;
the degree of fall is 21° Aries.
Uranus
Uranus takes eighty-four years to
traverse the zodiac and seven years
to travel through one sign. This
planet is retrograde for five months
at a time and stationary for up to
about two weeks. It moves but 4° each year, averaging
42" (seconds) per day. It is masculine, cold, dry,
electric and magnetic, and barren.
Uranus was formerly called Herschel after its
discoverer. The presence of Uranus in our solar system
has been known only since 1781. Much has been
learned about this planet in the almost two hundred
years since its discovery, but there remains much more
to determine.
The orbit of Uranus is irregular or eccentric and so
is its action. The planet represents the unpredictable,
the erratic, the different, the bizarre.
Uranian influence is disruptive. It breaks up existing
patterns to make room for progress. Uranus enforces
change and in so doing destroys in order to create.
Uranus is not destructive in the most negative sense
of the word, for it replaces what it removes. It breaks
with tradition and heralds the future.
Uranus embraces the principles of compassion, hu-
manitarianism and altruism; it introduces sodal reform.
Uranian action is sudden, unexpected, abrupt,
spasmodic, revolutionary and dictatorial. It expresses
the unconventional, the radical, the rebellious.
Uranus embodies the essence of freedom, originality
and inventiveness. Flashes of insight that inspire genius
are Uranian in nature.

Retrograde Uranus implies subjective expression of
the urge for freedom and the desire for change. If the
horoscope generally shows stability and perseverance,
advanced thought and progressive ideas may lead to
great discoveries. Otherwise, the individual may be
merely eccentric or malcontent, subject to erratic
notions. The retrograde motion of Uranus also
increases any occult tendencies shown in the
horoscope. Stationary Uranus emphasizes humani-
tarian principles and mandates change, as indicated
in the rest of the horoscope.
Uranus rules the general circulatory system, the
ankles, the shin bones, the pituitary gland and the aura.
As the higher octave of Mercury, it has influence over
the intuitive intellect and the nervous system, particu-
larly the motor nerves. Spasmodic ailments, convul-
sions, lack of coordination and accidents involving
electricity or lightning are due to Uranian influence.
Uranus is associated with the period in life from age
seventy to eighty-four. There is little doubt that during
these years a person's lifetime routine is changed and a
new sense of freedom emerges as one no longer faces the
responsibility of earning a living or rearing a family.
Uranus rules astrology, positive occultism, inven-
tions, discoveries, discrepancies, contradictions,
interruptions, abberations, homosexuality, the strange
and strangers, tremors, earthquakes, electricity,
magnetism, uranium and the number four. Uranus
signifies all that is new, novel, modern, avant garde.
The eleventh is the natural house of Uranus, and
Aquarius its sign of dignity. Uranus co-rules Aquarius
with Saturn, the traditional ruler. As more is learned
about Uranus, it becomes increasingly apparent that
it is probably the sole ruler of this sign. Uranus is
exalted in Scorpio, detrimented in Leo and in fall in
Taurus. The degree of exaltation is 7° Scorpio; the
degree of fall is 7° Taurus.
Neptune
Neptune crosses the zodiac once in 165 years
and spends about fourteen years in each sign.
The mean daily motion is 24"; it moves 2°
each year. The retrograde period lasts for
five months; it is stationary for approxi-
mately two weeks. Neptune is feminine, warm, moist,
magnetic and fruitful.
Having been discovered in 1846, Neptune is
considered one of the "newer" planets. It represents
the intangible, the vague, the nebulous and the elusive.
Neptunian influence is difficult to pinpoint: its action
is obscure, veiled, hidden.
Neptune energizes imagination, vision and spiritual
powers and governs rhythm. The higher octave of
Venus, this planet may inspire artistic genius in music,
art, poetry or the dance. It can also bring deception,
chaos and confusion. Neptune has dominion over the
unconscious. It is the planet of the mystic; it rules
escapism in all forms—drug addition, alcoholism and
delusion.
Retrograde Neptune increases the trend toward
inward forms of escapism and self-delusion. Artistic
inspiration and mystical tendencies may be enhanced
as well.
In a stationary position, the Neptunian qualities are
strengthened. A well-aspected stationary Neptune can
confer the highest level of spiritual attainment and
artistic vision; an afflicted stationary Neptune can
induce complete loss of touch with reality according
to how its influence is channeled.
Neptune's horoscope placement indicates the
illusions to which a person clings. This area represents
a blind spot in the individual's view of life.
Neptune rules the feet, the pineal gland and the
astral body. It is associated with hard-to-diagnose
ailments, hypochondria, catalepsy, drowning mishaps
and illnesses due to the introduction of toxic substances
into the body or the inhalation of noxious fumes.
Neptune is said to rule the years eighty-four to
ninety-nine, the so-called age of weakness when
physical strength is at low ebb.
The planet is associated with clairvoyants,
mediums, seances, yogis, hypnotism, instability,
bisexuality, solvents, synthetics, transparent materials,
camouflage, falsehoods, swindlers and places of
confinement such as hospitals, prisons and retirement
homes. Neptune governs salt water and the oceans (in
conjunction with the Moon), especially the deep seas.
Sleep, narcotics, photography, rubber, neptunium, the
number seven and all that is secret, concealed,
unrevealed, indistinct, indefinite, cloudy or halluci-
natory are in Neptune's domain.
The twelfth is the natural house of Neptune.
Dignified in Pisces, it shares rulership of Pisces with
Jupiter, the traditional ruler; however, in view of
ongoing studies, it seems likely that Neptune is the sole
ruler of Pisces. Neptune is currently believed to be

Pluto
Pluto, the slowest moving planet,
takes 248 years to complete one
circuit of the zodiac, averaging
about twenty-one years in each
sign. Due to the eccentricity of its
orbit, it speeds through Scorpio in twelve years and
slows to thirty-one years while crossing Taurus. The
retrograde period is five months; the stationary period
lasts up to seventeen days. In 1980, the average yearly
motion was 1° in the sign Libra.
Since Pluto's recent discovery in 1930, its influence has
been observed in four signs: Cancer, Leo, Virgo and
Libra. Its transit of Scorpio (1983/84-1955) will give
opportunity for further study. Much that is said about
this planet is theoretical. Pluto appears to be a powerful
planet whose action influences mass destiny. It represents
transformation and regeneration at the highest level,
destruction and annihilation at the lowest. Mob action
lies at Pluto's doorstep; so does the evolution of some
of the greatest movements in history.
Plutonian influence is operative for a long time
before it manifests overtly; when it does, there is no
restraining the force. Plutonian energy is potent, never
weak or mediocre. Pluto's action can be purging,
purifying and spiritually uplifting, or it can be obscene,
degrading and criminal. For good or ill, Pluto-evolved
change always has an irrevocable impact.
The effect this planet has in the personal horoscope
is debatable. Unless Pluto is the horoscope ruler or
occupies a strong position in the horoscope, many
people seem to react only mildly to the Plutonian
influence. Perhaps response is on an inward or spiritual
level and therefore less readily observed, or the
metamorphosis may be so slow and subtle, unfolding
over a period of years, that the individual is unaware
of the fundamental changes taking place.
Pluto acts to eliminate the dross, to cleanse, purify
and rejuvenate on both the spiritual and physical
planes. The horoscope placement of Pluto points out
the means of regeneration and evolvement. Pluto
coerces and urges development, but the individual
makes the final choice. A person may strive for the
heights of greatness or join the dregs of humanity, or
one may resist its influence and stagnate. Plutonian
power is at the individual's disposal; if one misuses
it, there is no turning back.
Retrograde Pluto is indicative of inner changes. The
individual faces a choice between purification of the soul
or spiritual bankruptcy. Stationary Pluto stresses the
potency of this planet for greatness or for degradation,
depending upon the direction of its power.
Pluto rules death, afterlife and rebirth, that cycle of
the soul that is essentially unknown to humankind. It
is associated with age one hundred and over.
Pluto rules the excretory system, the sex organs and
gonads, and the astral cord.
Pluto is the higher octave of Mars. Aswith all higher-
octave planets, there is an occult significance attached.
Pluto governs invisible forces, witchcraft, black magic
and levitation. It is associated with corruption, the
underground. Hades, reincarnation and resurrection.
Reptiles, bats, vampires, plutonium, tungsten and the
digit zero are ruled by Pluto. It has dominion over atomic
fission and all that implies the unleashing of power and
the transformation or recycling of energy.
The eighth is the natural house of Pluto. Pluto rules
the sign of Scorpio, jointly with the traditional ruler.
Mars. Some authorities designate Pluto as co-ruler of
Aries; however, it seems unlikely that the lengthy
gestation of Pluto-induced action is compatible with
the impulsive action of Aries.
Pluto may be exalted in Leo; it is in detriment in
Taurus; it may be in fall in Aquarius. The degree of
exaltation is probably 17° Leo; the degree of fall, 17°
Aquarius.
Each planet brings something into the life of the
individual as summarized in the following poem:

The Moon's Nodes
The points at which a planet's orbit intersects the
ecliptic are called planetary nodes. Other than the
Moon's Nodes, the significance of nodes to astrology
is as yet not fully understood. Lunar nodes are
meaningful: they are entered in the horoscope along
with the planets. The nodes of other planets are usually
omitted. Planetary nodes are discussed in Appendix A.
The position of the Moon's Nodes moves an average
of 3' retrograde each day, although the true motion
is both direct and retrograde. They take about nineteen
years to complete one reverse cycle of the zodiac.
The Moon's Nodes neither possess nor express
planetary energy. They are sensitive points in the
horoscope that indicate an individual's capacity for
growth within the framework of the society in which
he or she lives.
The North Node
The position of the ascending or North
Node, also called the Dragon's Head, is the
point of intersection of the lunar orbit and
the plane of the ecliptic as the Moon travels
from south to north relative to the ecliptic.
The North Node signifies those areas in which the
individual's attitudes are in harmony with current trends.
By reaching out into the realms of new experience as
indicated by the horoscope placement of the North
Node, one can develop more fully and abundantly.
The South Node
The descending or South Node (Dragon's
Tail) marks the orbital/ecliptic intersection
point as the Moon travels from north to
south relative to the ecliptic. The South
Node lies directly opposite the North node
in the zodiac. The imaginary line that links the North
and South Nodes is the Nodal Axis or Dragon.
The South Node represents deeply imbedded habit
patterns that hinder a person's efforts to reach out. The
individual may be out of step with the times and thereby
at a disadvantage in the area of horoscope activation.

Planets and Moon's Nodes in the Signs
The sign a planet occupies describes the manner in
which the energy of the planet is manifested. The
planetary ruler of a sign has a major influence on the
sign and on the planets in that sign.
Each sign is subdivided and planetary sub-rulers are
assigned to various degrees within the sign. The ruler
of a sign may also act as a sub-ruler. In those degrees
that are both ruled and sub-ruled by the same planet,
the characteristics of a sign are unmodified.
A sub-ruler other than the planetary ruler of the sign
acts in conjunction with the ruler; its action is subor-
dinate. Because of the influence of sub-rulers, a planet
passing through a particular sign does not operate in
precisely the same way in all degrees of that sign,
although the basic mode of sign expression remains
unchanged.
Decanates
The signs are divided into three decanates of 10° each.
The first decan of a sign, 0°-10o, is ruled and sub-ruled
by the planetary ruler of the sign; the second decan,
10°-20°, is sub-ruled by the ruler of the next sign in
the zodiac that belongs to the same triplicity: the third
decan, 20o-30o, is sub-ruled by the ruler of the
remaining sign in the same triplicity as follows:

A decanate sub-ruler shades or modifies the qualities
of a sign in its designated decan according to its natural
planetary influence. A planet that occupies its own decan
of a sign in which it has little standing operates more
freely than in other degrees of that sign. For example,
in Scorpio, its sign of fall, the Moon is weakened;
however, in the third decan (sub-ruled by the Moon)
lunar energies are strengthened, and the individual is
better able to cope with the emotional passion associated
with this sign position.
In order to distinguish the decans, each decanate is
known by the name of its sub-ruler. The name of the
sign ruled by the sub-ruler is also applied to the second
and third decans.
Decanates of Aries
The first decan of Aries, a fire sign, is ruled and sub-
ruled by Mars, the planetary ruler of Aries. The
dynamic, initiatory and impetuous qualities of Aries
are emphasized in this decan. The first decan is called
the Mars decanate of Aries.
The second decan of Aries is ruled by Mars and sub-
ruled by the Sun, the ruler of Leo which is the next
sign in the fire triplicity. This is the Leo or Sun
decanate of Aries. The influence of the Sun in the
second decan lends sustaining power to the natural
initiative that is characteristic of Aries.
The third decan of Aries is ruled by Mars and sub-
ruled by Jupiter because Jupiter is the ruler of
Sagittarius, the third sign in the fire triplicity. In this
decan, Jupiter supplements and expands the natural
Aries expression. The third is the Sagittarius or Jupiter
decanate of Aries.
Decanates of Taurus
The first decan of Taurus, ruled and sub-ruled by
Venus, brings out the endurance, obstinacy and
sensuality inherent in this earth sign. The first is called
the Venus decanate of Taurus.
The second decan of Taurus is sub-ruled by Mercury,
the ruler of Virgo that follows Taurus in the earth
triplicity. Mercury's influence here lends greater
flexibility and discrimination than is found in the first
decan. This is the Virgo or Mercury decanate of Taurus.
The third decan of Taurus is sub-ruled by Saturn,
which is the ruler of Capricorn, the third sign in the
earth triplicity. In this decan, Saturn intensifies the
materialistic qualities of Taurus. This is the Capricorn
or Saturn decanate of Taurus.
Decanates of Gemini
The first decan of Gemini, an air sign, is ruled and
sub-ruled by Mercury. Diffusion, restlessness and
superficiality are predominant characteristics of this
decan. The first decan is called the Mercury decanate
of Gemini.
The second decan of Gemini is sub-ruled by Venus as
the planetary ruler of Libra, the next air sign. Venus
enhances the Gemini charm; the style of expression
is perhaps more pleasing and attractive than in the first
decanate. The second decan is the Libra or Venus
decanate of Gemini.
The third decan of Gemini is sub-ruled by Uranus and
Saturn, rulers of the remaining air sign, Aquarius.
Since Uranus is the higher octave of Mercury, Uranus
probably has greater significance in this decan than
does Saturn. Uranus supplements the mental
expression of Gemini and adds spontaneity and
unpredictability. If theSatum influence manifests itself
in this decan, it should increase persistence and
decrease diffusiveness without stifling versatility or
impeding flexibility. The third decan is the Aquarius
or Uranus-Saturn decanate of Gemini.
Decanates of Cancer
The first decan of Cancer, awatersign, is ruled and sub-
ruled by the Moon. Thisdecan emphasizes the nurturing,
protective, emotional and fluctuating attributes of the
sign. This is the Moon decanate of Cancer.
The second decan of Cancer is sub-ruled by Pluto and
Mars, rulers of Scorpio. This decan strengthens the
Cancer tenacity but also increases turbulence. Plutonian
influence in this decan can help transform Cancer
sensitivity into productive creative expression. The
second is the Scorpio or Pluto-Mars decanate of Cancer.
The third decan of Cancer, sub-ruled by Neptune and
Jupiter as rulers of Pisces, reinforces the psychic nature
of Cancer and strengthens compassion. This decan also
heightens secretive tendencies and mystical inclina-
tions. This is the Pisces or Neptune-Jupiter decanate
of Cancer.

Decanates of Leo
The first decan of Leo. the second fire sign, is ruled
and sub-ruled by the Sun. This decan produces great
vitality and power in the expression of the Leo
qualities. This is the Sun decanate of Leo.
The second decan of Leo is sub-ruled by Jupiter, ruler
of Sagittarius, the fire sign which follows Leo in the
zodiac. The Sagittarius or Jupiter decanate of Leo
exhibits a freer and more versatile expression of the
Leo characteristics.
The third decan of Leo is sub-ruled by Mars as ruler
of Aries, the remaining fire sign. The Aries or Mars
decanate of Leo expresses greater assertiveness,
independence and courage.
Decanates of Virgo
The first decan of Virgo, the second earth sign, is ruled
and sub-ruled by Mercury. The Mercury decanate of
Virgo emphasizes perception and discrimination,
sensitivity to detail and fastidiousness.
The second decan of Virgo is sub-ruled bySaturn, ruler
of Capricorn. The Capricorn or Satum decanate of Virgo
promotes a businesslike approach and reinforces the
organized methodical expression of Virgo.
The third decan of Virgo is sub-ruled by Venus as ruler
of Taurus. The Taurus or Venus decanate of Virgo
strengthens the practical qualities of the sign and
increases stability.
Decanates of Libra
The first decan of Libra, ruled and co-ruled by Venus,
stresses harmony and companionship. The Venus
decanate of Libra emphasizes expression through
combined efforts on a partnership basis.
The second decan of Libra is sub-ruled by Uranus and
Saturn, rulers of Aquarius. Uranus injects greater
freedom and independence into Libra expression, but
it does not override the unity and cooperation that
is basic to Libra. If the Saturn influence predominates
in the Aquarius or Uranus-Saturn decanate of Libra,
Saturn stabilizes and thus reinforces Libra qualities.
The third decan of Libra is sub-ruled by Mercury as
ruler of Gemini. Mercury sharpens intellectual
expression in the Gemini or Mercury decanate of
Libra; it fosters flexibility and versatility, but it also
adds restlessness.
Decanates of Scorpio
The first decan of Scorpio is ruled and sub-ruled by
Pluto and Mars. The Pluto-Mars decanate is the most
powerful decanate of this sign and perhaps the
harshest, for the intense Scorpio characteristics are
essentially unmodified.
The second decan of Scorpio is sub-ruled by Neptune
and Jupiter, rulers of Pisces. The Pisces or Neptune-
Jupiter decanate reflects a more subtle manifestation
of Scorpio attributes. Neptunian influence may, in
some instances, subvert the higher motives of Scorpio
expression.
The third decan of Scorpio is sub-ruled by the Moon,
ruler of Cancer. In the Cancer or Moon decanate, the
Moon softens the harshness of the sign and lends to
sympathy and kindness in a rough sort of way, for there
is no real gentling or taming of Scorpio expression.
Decanates of Sagittarius
The first decan of Sagittarius is ruled and sub-ruled by
Jupiter. The Jupiter decanate emphasizes the optimistic
and idealistic qualities of the sign, but exaggerates
Sagittarian restlessness and wanderlust as well.
The second decan of Sagittarius is sub-ruled by Mars,
ruler of Aries. The Aries or Mars decanate shows
increased daring, initiative and immoderation.
Martian influence promotes fool hardiness, improv-
idence and opportunism.
The third decan of Sagittarius is sub-ruled by the Sun,
ruler of Leo. In the Leo or Sun decanate, the Sun
enhances Sagittarian vitality. Leonine influence adds
staying power and modifies the restless attributes of
Sagittarius so that expression is more stable than in
the first and second decans.
Decanates of Capricorn
The first decan of Capricorn is ruled and sub-ruled
by Saturn. The Saturn decanate of Capricorn is
predominantly goal-oriented. This decan stresses the
diligence, perseverance and status-consciousness that
is associated with this sign.

The second decan of Capricorn is sub-ruled by Venus
as ruler of Taurus. Venus augments the materialistic
and acquisitive characteristics of Capricorn in the
Taurus or Venus decanate.
The third decan of Capricorn is sub-ruled by Mercury
as ruler of Virgo. Mercury mellows the dogmatism of
the sign. Common sense and greater flexibility
underscore Capricorn expression in the Virgo or
Mercury decanate..
Decanates of Aquarius
The first decan of Aquarius is ruled and sub-ruled by
Uranus and Satum. The Uranus-Satum decanate is pro-
gressive, unpredictable and indicative of sudden change.
The second decan of Aquarius is sub-ruled by Mercury
as ruler of Gemini. The Gemini or Mercury decanate
of Aquarius emphasizes the intellectual expression of
the sign. This decan is associated with unprecedented
ideas and inventive genius. The second decan does not
modify the natural Aquarian tendencies; its action is
to supplement.
The third decan of Aquarius is sub-ruled by Venus as
ruler of Libra. Venus lends warmth to the impersonal
Aquarian expression. There is greater scope for
acceptance of the Aquarian movement in the Libra or
Venus decanate.
Decanates of Pisces
The first decan of Pisces is ruled and sub-ruled by
Neptune and Jupiter. The Neptune-Jupiter decanate is
given a highly spiritual connotcition. It is said to bring
out the inevitable. In this decan the self-sacrificing
elements of Pisces expression are emphasized.
The second decan of Pisces is sub-ruled by the Moon,
ruler of Cancer. The Moon heightens impressionability
and emotional vulnerability. The Cancer or Moon
decanate exhibits a morbid, self-pitying or maudlin
mode of expression?
The third decan of Pisces is sub-ruled by Pluto and Mars,
rulers of Scorpio. Pisces, a comparatively weak sign, is
strengthened by Pluto and Mars. Piscean expression may
manifest as either spiritual regeneration or degradation
because of the Plutonian influence in this decan. The
Scorpio or Pluto-Mars decanate is representative of the
power within the self to overcome inner weaknesses or
bring about self-destruction.
Duads (Dwadasamas)
A further subdivision divides the signs into twelve
duads, sometimes called dwadasamas, of IVz" each.
The first duad is ruled by the planetary ruler of the
sign; the second duad is ruled by the ruler of the sign
that immediately follows in the zodiac; the third duad
is ruled by the ruler of the next sign in the zodiac and
so on. The final duad is ruled by the ruler of the sign
that directly precedes the sign of interest. The duad
ruler is subordinate to both the planetary ruler of the
sign and the decanate sub-ruler.

The Venus influence as expressed in Taurus is
unmodified in this duad. The final duad (IT'T'-SO0)
of Taurus is ruled by Mars, planetary ruler of Aries,
the sign that precedes Taurus in the zodiac. Venus
remains the planetary ruler of Taurus: Saturn is sub-
ruler of the third decanate. Mars as duad ruler lends
more initiative than is found elsewhere in this sign,
initiative that is expressed in accordance with the
Venus/Saturn influence in the third decanate.
Navamsas
A ninefold division of signs based on Hindu astrology
describes the sub-influence of signs within a sign. Each
sign is divided into nine equal parts called navamsas,
of S'A0 each. Beginning with the first navamsa of
Aries, a sign is assigned to each navamsa in order
according to natural zodiacal sequence, repeating the
sequence as necessary to the ninth navamsa of Pisces.
The navamsa sign colors natural sign expression thus
creating slight variations within a sign.

Until recently navamsas were given little consideration
by western astrologers and are not commonly used in
natal astrology. They have application in astrological
health questions. For example, if Capricorn, which rules
bones, is a health factor in a horoscope, the Pisces
navamsa would specify foot bones since Pisces rules the
feet. Future studies may shed more light on the function
of navamsas.
Special Degrees
Critical Degrees
Critical degrees, which stem from the Hindu concept
of the twenty-eight Lunar Mansions (subdivisions of
the zodiac based upon the Moon's average daily
motion), are, unlike navamsas, widely accepted by
western astrologers. Critical degrees roughly separate
the Lunar Mansions, each of which spans 12-%° of the
zodiac. The critical degrees are 0°, 13°, and 26° in
cardinal signs (Aries, Cancer, Libra and Capricorn),
9° and 21° in fixed signs (Taurus, Leo, Scorpio and
Aquarius), 4° and 17° in mutable signs (Gemini, Virgo,
Sagittarius and Pisces).
Critical degrees supplement planetary strength, and
they can be the deciding factor in determining which
of two planets is the more influential. Of two planets
that otherwise carry equal weight in a horoscope, the
one occupying a critical degree is deemed the stronger
of the two.
Anaretic Degrees
The last degree of a sign, from 290to 30°, is called the
anaretic degree. Anaretic degrees signify an urgent
need to correctly utilize the planetary energy of the
planets placed therein. The individual is directed to
deal with fundamental issues as indicated by the
horoscope placement of the planets that occupy
anaretic degrees. These planets activate conditions
which one cannot ignore but must cope with in order
to grow in that area.
An anaretic degree placed on a house cusp draws
attention to the affairs of the house. If the individual
neglects these matters, a stalemate develops; the affairs
of the house stagnate, and progress in this area is
retarded.
Nodal Degrees
A planet that falls in the same numerical degree (not
necessarily in the same sign) as the Moon's Nodes is
given special significance. If placed in a nodal degree
a planet is said to indicate crisis or catastrophe at some
later point in life.
Fixed Star Degrees
A planet that occupies the same position by sign and
degree as one of the major fixed stars is given added
emphasis in the horoscope. This emphasis is not a
matter of planetary standing or strength. Fixed stars
are classed as benefic or malefic. According to its

=== Page 48 ===
Planets ami Moon's Nodes in the Signs 59
nature, a fixed star influences the action of a planet
that is placed in its zodiacal position. Major fixed stars
are listed in Appendix B.
Planetary Expression in the Signs
As a planet travels through the signs of the zodiac,
its energy is expressed in a manner that is consistent
with the characteristics of the sign it occupies at a
particular time. The signs do not alter the basic
energies or fundamental principles of the planets;
rather each provides a unique means of expressing
planetary energies.
The Sun in the Signs
The Sun represents the ego. The sign in which the Sun
falls describes the manifestation of the drive for self-
expression. The Sun sign influences one's approach to
goals in life and the method one chooses to accomplish
objectives. Some physical characteristics of the Sun
sign may be observed in the individual, but usually
one's appearance is determined largely by the sign on
the Ascendant, especially if the Ascending sign is the
stronger of the two or if the planetary ruler of the
Ascendant is stronger in the horoscope than the Sun.
For basic modes of Sun-sign expression, review the
signs in Chapter 2. Pay particular attention to the
personal characteristics which describe the individual's
drives and motivation.
The Moon in the Signs
The sign in which the Moon is placed colors emotional
responses and instinctive actions. The Moon sign
influences one's reaction to events and people
encountered throughout life. It describes the attitudes
that have been acquired as a result of early childhood
training, the maternal relationship, and home and
family attitudes.
The new Moon denotes inspiration, initiation, the
beginning of a cycle. The full Moon signifies matura-
tion, fruition, the peak of a cycle.
If the Moon is increasing in light (in the waxing
phase from new to full) in the natal horoscope, the
individual reacts quickly and in an active manner
within the limits of sign characteristics. If the natal
Moon is decreasing in light (in the waning phase from
full to new), response is more passive and introverted
according to the dictates of the sign. A lunation Moon
(new Moon) or full Moon in the horoscope can be
critical depending upon other astrological factors since
it marks a turning point or transition from one phase
to another. The lunation cycle is discussed in greater
detail in Chapter 10.
The Moon in Aries stimulates the emotions. The result
is a quick temper, impetuous responses and headstrong
attitudes that prompt instinctive rejection of discipline
and interference. This placement calls for developing
patience and safeguarding against mishaps due to haste
and rash actions. The individual whose Moon is in
Aries notices Arian traits in his or her mother whether
she is Arian or not. This person thinks of the mother
as outgoing, aggressive and perhaps bossy. Family
relationships and home life are active and competitive.
The Moon in its sign of exaltation, Taurus, steadies
the emotions and fosters consistent attitudes and stable
reactions. Domestic and financial security are
important to emotional well-being. This placement
contributes to an affectionate, though somewhat
possessive, nature. The mother is considered by the
individual to be caring and reliable, someone who is
there when needed. The individual values the home
and family life and works hard to preserve and protect
these interests.
The Moon in Gemini intensifies natural lunar
changeability and generates fluctuating emotions,
shallowness, restlessness and loquacity. This
placement is indicative of a flighty emotional nature.
Feelings are intellectualized and verbalized. The
maternal relationship is friendly, more sisterly than
parental. Outside activities are often of more concern
than home and family interests.
The Moon in its sign of dignity. Cancer, adds depth
to the emotions and gives rise to strong family ties.
A pronounced need to nurture and cherish and, in
turn, be approved of and loved is evident. This
placement generates a tendency to brood and
withdraw when hurt: it also increases psychic
sensitivity. The mother is pictured as a protector and
homemaker who cares deeply tor her child.
Throughout life, the individual maintains an ongoing
interest in home and family.
The Moon in Leo vitalizes the emotions and stirs a
dramatic and somewhat ostentatious sell-centered
response to the situations encountered. This placement

=== Page 49 ===
60 Compendium of Astrology
is indicative of a sunny temperament, a love for
children and a great deal of pride in home and family.
The mother is regarded as noble and aristocratic,
generous and warm. Usually the home is as lavish and
showy as the individual's finances will allow.
The Moon in Virgo inhibits the emotions and results
in reticence, modesty and a quiet demeanor. The
individual is conscious of details, scrupulous in work
and personal habits. This placement emphasizes
concern for health, hygiene and diet. The mother is
remembered as efficient and critical. The individual's
own home is meticulous, and much fussing and worry
accompany its maintenance.
The Moon in Libra creates an emotional aversion to
discordant conditions and disharmonious relation-
ships. Compatible relationships are a must for
emotional well-being. The individual will go to great
lengths to avoid a scene. Refinement, social grace, tact
and a need for approval are present with this
placement. The mother is thought of as fair and just
but somewhat indecisive. The individual's home
reflects an innate appreciation of nice things.
The Moon in Scorpio, the sign of fall, produces intense
emotional drives and deep passions. This placement
gives strength of purpose and determination; however,
strict control of turbulent emotions is needed. If
emotional control is lacking, the individual may be
prone to volatile anger, jealousy, resentment or
vengeance. The mother is seen as demanding and
forceful. Home life is seldom peaceful or serene,
although the family is deeply loved by the individual.
The Moon in Sagittarius interjects a need for emotional
independence and freedom. There is a natural inclination
to avoid ties that impinge upon personal liberty. The
individual loves travel and feels a need for movement
and activity. This placement produces high ideals,
optimism, daring and recklessness. The mother's
spiritual and religious qualities may be admired or
resented by the individual, but in either case they leave
a lasting impression. The individual is averse to
household routine, tends to form loose-knit family ties
and likes to change residence frequently.
The Moon in Capricorn, its sign of detriment, subdues
emotional expression and induces aloof, reserved,
controlled responses. A cautious, serious outlook and
a degree of pessimism accompany this placement.
Emotional security is linked to status and material
security. The mother is viewed as conscientious though
emotionally cool. Family relationships and home life
reflect materialistic concerns as well as a desire for
personal privacy.
The Moon in Aquarius depersonalizes the emotions;
the sympathies lie with humankind as a whole rather
than with a particular human being. A detached sort
of friendliness is present and one insists upon complete
emotional and personal freedom. The individual is
unconventional, a typical non-conformist. The mother
is regarded as odd or eccentric (by the individual).
Family relationships appear unusual to the outsider;
home life is non-traditional. Home furnishings and
decor tend toward the modernistic.
The Moon in Pisces sensitizes the emotions and
enhances receptivity to people and external conditions.
Psychic tendencies are marked. The individual is
compassionate but may be gullible and impractical.
This placement gives creative imagination; it also
breeds discouragement and escapism. The mother
impresses the individual as being loving, tender and
kind. Close family ties are maintained. A relaxing
home life can reinforce emotional stability.
For a more comprehensive understanding of the
Moon in the signs, reread the section on the Moon
in Chapter 3 and the mode of expression associated
with each sign as described in Chapter 2.
Mercury in the Signs
The sign in which Mercury is placed describes thinking
and study habits, mental and conversational expression,
the formulation and communication of ideas.
Mercury in Aries quickens thought processes and urges
immediate and direct expression of ideas. This
placement encourages competitive thinking, a love for
debate, argumentiveness, impatience, impulsive
decisions and ill-considered plans.
Mercury in Taurus inspires practical thinking and
common sense. Financial and material considerations are
an important part of decision making. This placement
restricts mental ingenuity and flexibility, but gives good
powers of concentration and prudent judgment.

=== Page 50 ===

Mercury, dignified in Gemini, indicates an agile,
perceptive mind, objective thinking capacity, logical
reasoning ability and fluent speech. This placement
creates an avid curiosity and the desire to learn;
however, mental interests may be scattered and
inconsistent, knowledge superficial.
Mercury in Cancer links the intellectual processes to
the emotions. Personal feelings and subconscious
memories intrude upon decisions and ideas, thus
hindering objectivity. This placement produces a good
memory, but thinking is apt to be influenced more by
the past than by the future.
Mercury in Leo. the sign of fall, channels mental
energy to produce continuity and cohesiveness in
thinking and planning. This placement inclines toward
a creative mental outlook and the dramatic expression
of ideas; however, the tendency to be opinionated or
intellectually arrogant may exist as well.
Mercury in Virgo, the sign of dignity, blends precise
logic, a penchant for detail and reasoning ability into
accurate analytical capabilities. This placement
contributes to efficient planning and the practical
utilization of ideas as well as to preoccupation with
trivial facts.
Mercury in Libra combines mental ability with a sense
of intellectual impartiality. Decisions are weighed
carefully. Overconcern with fairness and justification
can cause vacillation and indecision. This placement
effectively unites subtle persuasive powers and tactful
speech.
Mercury in Scorpio gives intuitive insight and a
probing mind that goes beyond the obvious and
penetrates the depths of a matter. This placement
indicates the desire and ability to perceive the inner
or hidden nature of things. Tendencies to be secretive,
shrewd, cunning, blunt and sarcastic also exist.
Mercury in Sagittarius, the sign of detriment, produces
idealistic concepts, intellectual versatility and
comprehension. Mental viewpoints are based largely
on principle. This placement activates the desire to be
well-informed and abreast of events, but failure to
grasp the finer points or specifics of a topic can limit
depth of understanding.
Mercury in Capricorn fosters mental discipline, good
concentration and well-ordered thought. Practical
considerations form the basis for judgment. This
placement indicates methodical reasoning ability
and common sense but gives little intellectual
resourcefulness.
Mercury in Aquarius, the sign of exaltation, creates
an unemotional intellectual outlook. The mind is
inventive; the trend of thought is progressive and
original. This placement permits an unbiased view of
human events and conditions; it gives rise to advanced
concepts but also promotes rather extreme ideas.
Mercury in Pisces, the sign of detriment, heightens
emotional perception and psychic awareness to the
extent that intellectual impressions may be distorted.
Ideas are imaginative and creative though not necessarily
realistic or practical. This placement hinders the ability
to discriminate between fact and fancy.
Venus in the Signs
The sign in which Venus is posited indicates the way a
person expresses himself or herself as a social companion,
romantic partner or spouse. It describes one's aesthetic
tastes, financial habits and material preferences.
Venus in Aries, the sign of detriment, induces
aggressive social and romantic expression. These
people are competitive, enthusiastic and passionate in
their relationships. They frequently form ties
impulsively. They show much initiative toward
moneymaking activities; however, they often spend
their money as fast as they earn it.
Venus tn Taurus, the sign of dignity, signifies lasting
friendships. These people forge serious romantic links
and permanent marital bonds. They are steadfast in
love and inclined to be possessive with loved ones.
The arts, material comforts and gourmet food are
appreciated. They possess strong financial drives.
Venus in Gemini denotes a friendly, charming, witty-
companion who is somewhat inconsistent. The
individual may be a social butterfly and a flirt.
Nonetheless, these people are likeable and popular.
They enjoy conversation, reading and travel Many
have a tendency to squander money frivolously
Venus in Cancer forms strong emotional ties. Marriage
is associated with security. These people tend to
"mother" and cling to those they love. They enjoy
entertaining at home. Although they spend money on

their pleasure needs. They like to entertain and gamble
and usually do both in a big way.
Venus in Virgo, the sign of fall, inclines one to be very

In their associations these people value harmony above

Venus in Scorpio, the sign of detriment, gives rise to a

Venus in Sagittarius shows a sociable disposition and

Venus in Aquarius displays an unconventional attitude

These people seek intellectual stimulation and gravitate

Despite erratic spending and saving habits, they are

With Venus in Pisces, the sign of exaltation, love

Impractical in financial matters, they show little
concern for money or the lack of it.
Mars in the Signs
The sign in which Mars falls shows how one gives
expression to energy and gratifies physical desires.
Mars in Aries, the sign of dignity, indicates direct and
immediate action. These people go after what they
want without a second thought. They are energetic,
impulsive, outgoing, aggressive and competitive.
Although they possess initiative, courage and
enthusiasm, they frequently fail to finish what they
start. Their haste and thoughtlessness often cause
mishaps, particularly burns, scalds, cuts and injuries
due to shooting incidents or traffic accidents. These
people possess a strong sex drive.
Mars in Taurus, the sign of detriment, retards the
natural Martian initiative, yet it gives practical
direction to the energies and strengthens determina-
tion. These people are slow starters, but their action
is purposeful. The individual's desires are linked to
moneymaking activities and material gain. They like
to work with money or materials from the earth. They
have a very basic approach to sex.
Mars in Gemini expresses energy through intellectual
channels and the skilled use of the hands. Competitive
and aggressive in mind and speech, these people find
an outlet for their energy either through action or in
being quarrelsome. Much restlessness is evident with
this placement. These people waste energy by starting
too many projects at the same time, finishing few. Out
of boredom they may affect ill-considered and
impetuous changes. They hold a cavalier attitude
toward sex.
Mars in Cancer, the sign of fall, emotionalizes the
physical drives. Highly emotional about everything
they do, these people tend to get overly involved on
a personal level. It is difficult for them to be objective

Mars in Capricorn, the sign of exaltation, increases

Sexual response is unemotional, cool.
Mars in Pisces reduces stamina and gentles drives.

Saturn in the Signs
The frustrating or inhibiting action of Satum is expressed
through thesignit occupies. Since Satum remains in one
sign for approximately two and one-half years, the house
placement in the horoscope is of greater personal
significance than sign influence. The sign position
indicates how a person handles serious issues,
approaches obstacles in life, relates to authority and

Satum in Aries the sign of fall, blunts the initiative yet

Satum in Cancer, thesign of detriment, gives the tenacity

Security-conscious, these people handle difficulties in a
manner that presents the least threat to emotional and
material security. Because of their emotional restraint,

Saturn in Leo. the sign of detriment, narrows creative
self-expression. These people may be hampered by
their own egos. They try to resolve problems and settle
issues in a self-centered manner. If they are to find a
permanent solution to difficulties, they need to

Satum in Virgo attaches importance to detail and

Satum in Scorpio prompts reserve and taciturnity. The

Satum in Sagittarius inspires conscientious intellectual

Satum in Capricorn, the sign of dignity, can give rise

headed, practical manner. They know the value of
hard work, but they must overcome the tendency to
accumulate and hoard material assets if they are to
enjoy the fruits of their efforts.
Saturn, dignified in Aquarius, heightens personal

standpoint. Frequently they stir opposition with their
impersonal and unconventional views. Through their

rejection.
Saturn in Pisces restricts compassion and induces an
attitude of hopelessness and despair These people
must develop a realistic attitude toward ditticulties
and learn to implement practical solutions to their
problems. Troubles are exacerbated by discourage-
ment and the failure to cope.

Uranus in the Signs
The significance of Uranus in the signs has a very
general application since this planet occupies the same
sign for approximately seven years. Its influence in
twentieth century development is pointed out in
Chapter 28. A more personal emphasis may be given
if other astrological factors warrant it. The sign in
which Uranus is placed gives expression to the
rebellious spirit, the desire for freedom, and the urge
for change and breaking with traditions.
Uranus in Aries asserts independence and prompts
change. There is danger of impetuous action that severs
ties and causes estrangement, action that is motivated
by impatience and a desire for freedom at any price.
Uranus in Taurus, the sign of fall, induces practical
innovations. Changes designed to serve utilitarian
purposes and produce concrete results are associated
with the use of material resources.
Uranus in Gemini enhances ingenuity and inven-
tiveness. However, action is erratic and novel ideas
may be left to flounder due to the individual's lack
of perseverance. Change may be promoted merely for
the sake of change.
Uranus in Cancer contributes to emotional unpredict-
ability and a certain amount of emotional instability.
Emotional considerations underlie the breaks initiated
and the changes effected.
Uranus in Leo, the sign of detriment, produces changes
of the kind that increase power potential and
leadership capacity. The individual may overstep the
bounds of propriety and common sense in order to
satisfy the urge for prominence and change.
Uranus in Virgo promotes systematic research, especially
in job methodology and health. On a personal level, the
individual may tend to adopt food fads and unconven-
tional methods of medical treatment.
Uranus in Libra generates instability in relationships.
The desire for freedom and change can disrupt
cooperative endeavors, partnerships and marriage.
Uranus in Scorpio, the sign of exaltation, gives rise
to massive changes of a profound nature. Death and
destruction may herald the need for change. Rebellion
and self-will are strong motivating factors.
Uranus in Sagittarius magnifies .the urge for intellectual
freedom. Far-ranging views, advanced abstract concepts
and unorthodox ideas are all part of the progressive
intellectualism indicated by this placement; however,
there may be lack of consistency in opinions.
Uranus in Capricorn gives a more conventional
expression to the Uranian demand for change.
Tradition is reordered and modernized rather than
dispensed with entirely. Future security is the prime
motivation behind change.
Uranus in Aquarius, the sign of dignity, produces
humanitarian inspired changes that have far-reaching
implications. Innovations are inventive, original and
often much ahead of the times. Future trends are bom
here.
Uranus in Pisces awakens the intuitive intellect; it may
prompt fundamental spiritual revelations. All too
often the results from subsequent changes are
disappointing because Utopian hopes are founded on
illusory ideals.
Neptune in the Signs
Since Neptune spends about fourteen years in each
sign, the sign placement has little effect on the
individual unless other indications in the horoscope
elevate the importance of this planet. The sign in which
Neptune falls is indicative of the imagination, the
spiritual and intuitive faculties, and the mystical
leanings: all those intangible qualities in human nature.
Neptune's influence in world trends and generational
developments during the twentieth century as it
traverses the zodiac from Gemini into Aquarius is
discussed in Chapter 28.
Neptune in Aries (1861/62-1874/75; circa 2024-2038)

imaginative impulses and psychic promptings. Perhaps
Neptune's entry into Aries in the twenty-first century
will herald daring underwater exploits, a new
approach to psychic phenomena and a world-wide
awakening on a spiritual level.
Neptune in Taurus (1874/75-1887/88; circa 2038-2053)
lends concrete expression to the imagination. It
encourages practical application of spiritual inspiration.
This position reflects a generation that channels
Neptunian energies into avenues of material concern.

The Moon's Nodes in the Signs
The Moon's North and South Nodes always fall in
opposing signs. The sign in which the North Node
appears shows how a person reaches out to others in
order to overcome inertia and to outgrow habits which
block progress. The North Node's sign denotes the
manner in which one approaches the new experiences
that are essential to development.
The sign the South Node occupies describes the way
a person expresses habitual tendencies that are
responsible for stagnation, those tendencies that retard
potential development.
The North Node in Aries and the South Node in Libra
require initiative and self-assertion to overcome the
tendency to rely on others. Indecision and the failure
to strike out on one's own inhibit growth.
The North Node in Taurus and the South Node in
Scorpio call for practical and determined action as the
means of releasing deep-seated emotional frustrations
which limit development. In some instances there may
be sexual connotations with these sign positions. If so,
the individual can find meaningful expression in sexual
love only after self-centered passions are conquered.
The North Node in Gemini and the South Node in
Sagittarius emphasize the need for a logical, objective
approach that shows concern for central facts. It is
necessary to correct the habit of acting on generalities
without giving sufficient consideration to essential
details.
The North Node in Cancer and the South Node in
Capricorn indicate that one must reach out with feeling
and display sensitivity and protective concern toward
others as the means of overcoming selfish ambition,
emotional coolness and indifference.
The North Node in Leo and the South Node in
Aquarius signify the need to extend creativity and
personal warmth in order to open doors that have
remained closed because of impersonal attitudes or
eccentric habits.
The North Node in Virgo and the South Node in Pisces
stress the importance of discrimination and attention
to detail. These sign placements emphasize the need
to overcome laziness, indecision and aimlessness.
The North Node in Libra and the South Node in Aries
show that growth comes through cooperation and
association with others. Willfullness and argumenta-
tiveness that interfere with establishing productive
relationships must be stifled.
The North Node in Scorpio and the South Node in
Tourus specify the need for regenerating the spirit and
mastering materialistic tendencies. So positioned, the
Moon's Nodes also have sexual implications, which
attach significance to healthy sexual expression and
require control of licentious tendencies.
The North Node in Sagittarius and the South Node
in Gemini point out ethical action based on high-
minded principles as the key to growth. Clever or
cunning habits that stand in the way of honesty must
be overcome.
The North Node in Capricorn and the South Node in
Cancer call for a well-organized approach and
constructive action. It is imperative that the individual
deal with emotional obstacles that create the tendency
to withdraw from others.
The North Node in Aquarius and the South Node in
Leo require open expression of friendliness founded
on humanitarian concepts. One must master egotism
and play down self-importance in order to grow.
The North Node in Pisces and the South Node in Virgo
present self-sacrifice and a deep spiritual concern for
the suffering of others as the way to outgrow
faultfinding and overly critical tendencies.

The Houses of the Horoscope
The twelve houses are the basic units of the horoscope.
A line drawn from the outer circle of a horoscope to
the center of the chart marks the beginning (cusp) of
one house and the end of the preceding one. Refer to
Chapter 1, Figure 2.
Hemispheres of the Horoscope
Each house represents specific areas or conditions of life.
Larger divisions within the horoscope, hemispheres and
quadrants, have a general application.
The Ascendant-Descendant Axis
The cusp of the seventh house, the Descendant, lies
directly opposite the cusp of the first house, the
Ascendant. The line that connects these two houses,
the Ascendant-Descendant axis (horizontal axis),
represents the horizon.
The section of the horoscope above this axis, the
southern hemisphere, charts signs and planets that
appear in that part of the sky above the horizon at
the time and place of birth. Houses seven through
twelve, which lie above the Ascendant-Descendant
axis, the axis of intellectual expression and spiritual
reaction, are referred to as collective or dispersive
houses. A large number of planets placed in the
collective houses of the southern hemisphere or day
section of the horoscope indicates outgoing, active,
intellectual expression and mental objectivity in a
general way.
Signs and planets that appear below the horizontal
axis are those that are below Earth's horizon. Houses
one through six, which fall below this axis in the
northern hemisphere or night section of the horoscope,
are termed personal or focal houses. A majority of
planets occupying personal houses signifies receptive,
passive intellectual expression and mental subjectivity.
The Midheaven (MC)-Imum Coeli (IC) Axis
The IC falls directly opposite the MC in the horoscope.
The line joining these two angles is defined as the MC-
IC axis, or vertical axis. The vertical axis, the axis of
physical action and emotional response, separates the
eastern and western hemispheres of the horoscope.
In a quadrant system of house division (unequal
house system), the MC denotes the cusp of the tenth
house and the IC marks the cusp of the fourth house.
In such a system, the houses are not the same size:
that is, depending upon the time and place of birth,
one house differs from another in the number of
zodiacal degrees it contains.
An equal house system is one in which each house
is comprised of 30°. The cusps of the fourth and tenth
houses are dependent upon the degree of the
Ascendant (as are the other house cusps). The angles
of a horoscope occupy the same sign and degree in
all house systems for any particular set of birth data.
Regardless of the house system used, the MC and IC
always form the vertical axis even if these points differ
from the cusps of the tenth and fourth houses.
The houses that lie in the eastern section of the
horoscope (left of the vertical axis) are collectively termed
independent houses. In a quadrant system of house
division these are houses one, two, three, ten, eleven and
twelve. Heavy planetary emphasis in the eastern
hemisphere of a horoscope denotes self-motivation and

=== Page 60 ===
72 Compendium of Astrology
self-directed endeavor. Action is not contingent upon
circumstances; the individual will force opportunities.
Houses in the western hemisphere of the horoscope
(right of the vertical axis) are dependent houses. These
are houses four, five, six, seven, eight and nine in a
quadrant system. A preponderance of planets in the
western hemisphere indicates that freedom of action
is limited to some extent by society. A passive or
receptive response to circumstances is more typical
than self-initiated activity. The individual tends to go
along with conditions as they are rather than introduce
changes; one is more or less dependent upon society
for opportunities.
Refer to Chapter 1, Figure 2, for positions of the
houses in a horoscope.
The Vertex-Anti-Vertex Axis
The Vertex marks the intersection of the ecliptic and
the prime vertical (the vertical great circle that passes
through the east point of Earth's horizon, zenith and
nadir) in the west; the opposite point is the Anti-
Vertex. The axis connecting these two points is called
the third angle of the horoscope. The astrological
significance of these two points and the hemispheric
division created by their axis is not fully established.
It is believed that the Vertex indicates fateful or karmic
events that play an important part in the life of an
individual. Vertex events are not fateful in the sense
that something must happen; these events are related
to cause and effect. For example, a person through his
or her actions (Anti-Vertex) can set up chain reactions
which lead to a specific result (Vertex). The Anti-
Vertex indicates self-action that begins the chain and
the Vertex indicates the point of result. If, however,
action is changed or modified anywhere along the line,
the end result will be changed or modified accordingly.
The Vertex is also known as the wish-fulfillment
factor, but wishes are apt to be fulfilled in a very
perverse manner. For instance, if the Vertex activates
the eighth house, which rules insurance and legacies,
the wish for a large sum of money might be fulfilled
through collection of insurance stemming from
destruction of possessions or through a legacy, a direct
result of a death. Either way, suffering, tragedy and/or
sacrifice is the price of wish fulfillment. Self-activation
(Anti-Vertex) in the form of the wish involved second
house (financial) matters in this case, perhaps because
of unconscious desires for economic security or
financial status.
The Vertex is always on the western side of a
horoscope and usually falls^between the fifth and
eighth houses. As a rule, other people are involved
in whatever is implied by the sign, house, and aspects
associated with this point. Personal relationships may
be significant here, or others may be responsible for
related external conditions, depending upon all
astrological factors concerned. The Anti-Vertex, found
in the eastern section of the chart, indicates the point
of beginning action in relation to the Vertex.
Much more needs to be learned about the true
nature of the Vertex in order to determine its exact
significance in natal astrology. Current data does
suggest that a conjunction between the Vertex and a
planet (both in the same sign and degree) lends power
to both. For example, if Neptune conjuncts the Vertex
in the seventh house, which rules marriage and
partnerships, unrealistic (Neptune) expectancies
(Vertex) in matters concerning partners and mate
(seventh house) are indicated. Expectations are self-
oriented (Anti-Vertex in the first house opposite the
seventh house); social interaction (seventh house)
depends upon personal development, a first house
matter. If the conjunction is in Virgo, the individual
might expect perfection in relationships and be
disappointed if hoped-for perfection failed to
materialize. However, the ability to handle these
relationships comes through self-development and
self-understanding as indicated by the Anti-Vertex.
Other planets that influence the conjunction would
indicate how the individual might deal with Vertex-
related situations.
It is good practice to insert the Vertex, abbreviated
V, in a horoscope and study its connection with actual
events or relationships that seem to be related.
Calculations for computing the zodiacal positions of
the Vertex and Anti-Vertex are given in Chapter 12.
East Point
The East Point is the precise degree of zodiacal
longitude rising at the equator at the time of birth.
Also called the equatorial Ascendant or hidden
Ascendant, the East Point describes the inner or hidden
side of the personality. These traits, though not always
observable, frequently manifest when the individual
is under stress. Aspects to the East Point give
important clues as to how one forms and maintains
relationships. If an individual has trouble relating to
the inner aspects of the personality, he or she will

=== Page 61 ===
The Houses of the Horoscope 73
probably have difficulty in relating to others. Stressful
aspects to the East Point indicate difficulty in
expressing all facets ot the personality and in
overcoming conflicting modes of expression. Study of
the East Point reveals karmic lessons and karmic
relationships that were self-formed and impressed
upon the inner self. The East Point and its opposite
coincide with the Ascendant and Descendant for births
occurring along the equator (0° latitude). East Point
calculations are given in Chapter 12,
Quadrants of the Horoscope
The angles (Ascendant, Descendant, MC and IO
separate the four quadrants (quarters) of the
horoscope. Each quadrant is part of two hemispheres
(eastern or western and northern or southern) in
relation to both the horizontal and vertical axes, and
combines the hemispheric influences attributed to its
area of the horoscope.
The first quadrant, bounded by the Ascendant and
IC and consisting of houses one through three, describes
qualities of both the northern and eastern hemispheres.
Planetary emphasis in the first quadrant implies mental
receptivity and subjectivity (northern hemisphere) in
combination with outgoing emotional and physical
expression (eastern hemisphere emphasis).

QUADRANT
The IC and Descendant bound the second quadrant,
which contains houses four, five and six. A combina-
tion of northern and western hemisphere emphasis is
shown here. When a large number of planets is placed
in the second quadrant, tendencies toward intellectual,
emotional and physical passiveness are emphasized.
The third quadrant is bounded by the Descendant and
the MC. A majority of planets occupying this quadrant
combines emotional and physical receptivity with mental
objectivity and outgoing intellectual expression.
The MC and Ascendant bound the fourth quadrant.
Heavy planetary distribution in this quadrant indicates
outgoing intellectual, emotional and physical activity
(see Figure 6).
Quadrants are also associated with stages of
developing the self in relation to the general focus of
the houses contained therein. This aspect of quadrant
emphasis is discussed in this chapter in the section
entitled "Developmental Focus of Quadrant Houses"
following individual house descriptions.
The term occidental is used variously to denote all
the houses in the western hemisphere (second and third
quadrants) or to specify houses one, two, three, seven,
eight and nine, which form the first and third
quadrants. The term oriental is sometimes applied to
all houses in the eastern hemisphere (first and fourth
quadrants) and sometimes to those houses in the
second and fourth quadrants, namely houses four,
five, six, ten, eleven and twelve. These terms are
misleading when applied to houses and, if used, should
be explicitly defined.
It is less confusing and always correct to refer to
a planet as being oriental of the Sun when it rises and
sets before the Sun or as occidental if it rises and sets
after the Sun.
Hylegiacal and Anaretic Places
Hylegiacal places, also called aphetic places, are
portions of the horoscope that are termed life
supportive. The hylegiacal places are the last 5° of the
twelfth house, the first 25° of the first house, the last
5° of the sixth house, the first 25° of the seventh house
the last 5° of the eighth house, all ot the ninth house
the entire tenth house and the lirst hall of the eleventh
