A benefic planet that is posited in a hylegiacal place
and is strong and well aspected is designated the Hyleg
or Apheta of the horoscope, the giver of life. In a man's
horoscope, the Sun, if qualified, is the Hyleg; if the
Sun is not in a hylegiacal place, or is afflicted and weak
by sign, the Moon is used; if neither planet qualifies,
the planetary ruler of the Ascendant is considered next,
then Jupiter, Mercury and Venus in that order. In a
woman's horoscope, the Moon is considered first in
determining the Hyleg, then the Sun, the Ascendant
ruler, Venus, Jupiter and Mercury. If all such planets
are afflicted, the hylegiacal benefic that is least afflicted
is chosen Hyleg. The Hyleg is associated with
longevity and the sustaining of life.
The Anareta, the most influential malefic, which
occupies or rules the sign on the cusp of the fourth, sixth,
eighth or twelfth house, is the destroyer of the horoscope;
it is associated with death. Its position is the anaretic
place, which describes the termination of life.
House Classifications
The houses are classified according to similar or
complementary association.
Modal Houses
Modal houses are classed according to the general
mode of activity shared by the houses in each group.
This threefold division classifies the houses as angular,
succedent or cadent.
The angular houses are one, four, seven and ten.
Each of these houses is ruled naturally by a cardinal
sign, and each reflects cardinal qualities in its activities.
These houses are indicative of initiatory, dynamic
action. Planets placed in angular houses are powerful,
for they act as motivators.
Succedent houses (two, five, eight and eleven),
naturally fixed houses, are associated with reliable,
steady action in a general sense. Specific action in any
house is determined by the planets and signs involved.
Ideas and activities that originate in angular houses
are carried out in these houses.
The cadent houses, ruled naturally by mutable signs,
are three, six, nine and twelve. Adaptability and diver-
sified action are shown here. These houses disperse the
results of angular and succedent house activity.
Functional Houses
Functional houses are grouped according to
complementary function; that is, each house in a group
represents a particular branch of the same general
function described by the group to which it belongs.
This important classification is composed of four
groups: individual houses (one, five and nine), all ruled
naturally by fire signs, temporal houses (two, six and
ten), ruled naturally by earth signs, relative houses
(three, seven and eleven), ruled naturally by air signs
and terminal houses (four, eight and twelve), ruled by
water signs.
Individual houses are associated with the person,
the self, life. In this context, the first house represents
the body, the fifth house represents the creative spirit,
and the ninth house represents the abstract intellect.
This group is also called the Trinity of Life.
Temporal houses have bearing on the material
aspects of life. Money and possessions are associated
with the second house, work and service are associated
with the sixth house, and prestige and career interests
are associated with the tenth. These houses are known
as houses of substance or possessive houses and form
the Trinity of Wealth.
Relative houses are concerned with human
relationships. The third house represents close relatives
and neighbors, the seventh house represents business
and marriage partners, and the eleventh house

=== Page 63 ===
The Houses of the Horoscope 75
represents friends and colleagues. These houses
constitute the Trinity of Association.
Terminal houses pertain to endings and results. The
fourth house deals with the closing years of life, the
eighth deals with death, and the twelfth deals with the
ultimate consequences of life. As water houses, these
are also considered occult houses; they form the
Trinity of Psychism.
The Significance of Each of the Houses
By studying the signs and planets that influence a
house, the astrologer determines conditions and
activity relevant to affairs governed by that house.
The sign that appears on a house cusp is the ruling
sign of that house: the planetary ruler of the cusp sign
is the ruler of the house. Planets occupying a house
are co-rulers of the house.
In an unequal house (quadrant) system of house
division, it is possible for all 30° of a sign different
from that on the cusp to fall within a house. A sign
that does not appear on a house cusp but is contained
entirely within a house is called an intercepted sign.
Though its expression is somewhat subdued and
obscured by the cusp sign, this sign is significant in
house affairs and its planetary ruler is also co-ruler
of the house.
The natural sign and planetary ruler associated with
a house bear some influence in the affairs of that
house, for these three, though they function
differently, share common rulerships.
The First House
The first house is the most personal of houses. It
represents the individual, the appearance, facial
characteristics, mannerisms, disposition, attitudes, the
body and the condition of the body, and is thus
associated with general health. The first house also
signifies personal affairs and beginnings, including the
beginning of life. This is the house of self. The natural
sign of the first house is Aries: the natural ruler is Mars.
The sign on the Ascendant (the cusp of the first
house), called the rising sign, essentially influences
personal characteristics, temperament, personality and
appearance. Along with the Sun and Moon, the
Ascendant describes the individual. The Sun represents
the ego and defines creative self-expression; the Moon
is associated with the responsive side of the personality;
the Ascendant portrays the outward expression of
personal identity, the projection of the personality.
The planetary ruler of the Ascending sign is
designated the horoscope ruler or chart ruler. The
planetary ruler of a sign that is intercepted in the first
house is not the horoscope ruler: however, it is
considered a co-ruler of the first house.
The Second House
The second house represents personal material resources.
Money, tangible assets, personal belongings, movable
possessions, personal income and expenditures all come
under the dominion of the second house. This house
describes a person's earning capacity, how personal
money is spent, how financial obligations are met, how
one budgets, saves and invests. This is the house of
personal finance. Taurus is the natural sign of the second
house, and Venus is the natural ruler.
The Third House
The third house rules the intellect and communication.
A person's thinking capacity, mental expression,
conversational tendencies, literary interests, reading
preferences and study habits are described in the third
house. Speech, letters, writings, documents, books,
magazines, telephones, and primary and secondary
education are ascribed to this house. Short trips and
commuter travel belong to the third house as does
walking, hiking, bike riding and visiting. The third
house represents brothers, sisters, relatives in general,
neighbors and the neighborhood environment. This
is the house of learning. The natural sign of the third
house is Gemini; Mercury is the natural ruler.
The Fourth House
The fourth house deals with the home, family life and
domestic affairs. Fixed possessions, houses and property
are governed by the fourth house. It represents one s
mother and describes the maternal relationship in
particular, the parental relationship in general. The
fourth house reflects one's inherited tendencies as well
as early childhood environment and experiences. The
conclusion of undertakings rests tn the fourth house and
so do the closing years of life. This is the house of the
home. Cancer is the natural sign of the fourth house,
and the Moon is the natural ruler
The Fifth House
The fifth house governs pleasurable pursuits. Creative
expression, romance, courtship love affairs, social

=== Page 64 ===
76 Compendium of Astrology
activities, recreation, entertainment, amusements,
sports, games, hobbies, gambling interests and
financial speculation are represented by the fifth house.
Although investments fall in the general category of
financial afffairs belonging to the second house, those
of a risky or speculative nature are ruled by the fifth
house. The fifth house is associated with education and
educational institutions and, along with the third
house, has bearing on one's education. A person's
children, and the first child in particular, are also
represented by the fifth house. This is the house of
pleasure. The natural sign of the fifth house is Leo,
and the natural ruler is the Sun.
The Sixth House
The sixth house, is associated with health and one's
capacity for work and service. Matters to do with diet,
nutrition, hygiene, health care, sickness and disease are
ascribed to the sixth house. General working conditions,
one's ability to obtain and hold a job, job efficiency,
occupational hazards, and one's relationships with co-
workers and employees are described by this house. The
sixth house rules pets and domestic animals; it is
connected with animal husbandry. This is the house
of health. Virgo is the natural sign of the sixth house;
Mercury is its natural ruler.
The Seventh House
The seventh house is representative of a person's
interaction with society, one's close associations and
one's dealings with the public. Marriage, divorce,
business partnerships and close personal relation-
ships belong to this house. Open enemies, rivals,
competitors and allies come under the dominion of the
seventh house. This house rules agreements, mergers,
lawsuits and contracts. Note that while the paper,
writing and signing of a contract are third house
matters, the essential agreement is a seventh house
affair. This is the house of partnership. The natural
sign of the seventh house is Libra; the natural ruler
is Venus.
The Eighth House
The eighth house represents death, death benefits, the
affairs of the dead, partnership resources and joint
financial interests. This house describes legacies,
inherited assets, insurance, the marriage partner's
earnings and money-managing tendencies, alimony,
gains obtained through business partners, and taxes.
The recycling of discarded items and the salvaging of
worn articles is attributed to the eighth house. The
eighth house is associated with sexual energies and
regeneration. Interest in life after death and
reincarnation is found here. This is the house of
rejuvenation. Scorpio is the natural sign of the eighth
house; Pluto and Mars share natural rulership.
The Ninth House
The ninth house governs legal affairs, foreign interests,
religion, abstract thought, higher education, publishing,
long-range advertising and lengthy journeys. This house
rules courts of law, foreign countries, churches and
universities. The ninth house represents the relatives of
the marriage partner and describes a person's
relationship with in-laws. Horses, especially race horses,
are associated with this house. It is called the house of
philosophy. The natural sign of the ninth house is
Sagittarius, and the natural ruler is Jupiter.
The Tenth House
The tenth house refers to worldly affairs, professional
and career interests, a person's business life, recogni-
tion, community standing, prestige, one's employer,
one's superiors and the government. This house deals
with a person's public life and achievements and is the
house of worldly attainments. It also represents the
father and describes parental authority in general.
Capricorn is the natural sign of the tenth house, and
Saturn is the natural ruler.
The MC (Midheaven) has much significance in tenth
house affairs. Whether or not it forms the cusp of the
tenth house, the MC indicates the natural direction
of a person's efforts as applied to his or her career,
worldly ambitions and other outside interests of a
public nature.
The Eleventh House
The eleventh house describes the friends a person
chooses and the organizations to which one belongs.
The eleventh house rules fraternal lodges and
cooperative societies. This house represents one's
colleagues, acquaintances and companions, the
potential to advance personal objectives through
friendship and group affiliations lies therein. A
person's hopes and wishes are found in this house. This
is the house of friendship. The natural sign of the

=== Page 65 ===
The Houses of the Horoscope 77
eleventh house is Aquarius; Uranus and Saturn are the
natural rulers.
The Twelfth House
The twelfth house represents sorrows, troubles,
bondage, limitations, anxieties, worries, confinement,
seclusion and all that is secret, hidden or clandestine.
Confidential matters, private affairs, secret societies,
hidden enemies, treachery and deceit are twelfth house
concerns. Charitable organizations, welfare offices and
relief agencies are part of this house. Hospitals,
sanitariums, rest homes, jails, prisons, reformatories
and detention camps are represented by the twelfth
house. This house is referred to as the house of self-
undoing or karma because it is associated with karmic
responsibilities. Pisces is the natural sign of the twelfth
house; the natural rulers are Neptune and Jupiter.
Developmental Focus of Quadrant Houses
The quadrant that contains the largest number of planets
indicates the stage of development on which an individ-
ual naturally focuses his or her attention according to
general properties shared by quadrant houses.
The first quadrant (houses one through three) is the
"me" or "mine" quadrant and the focus is on self-needs.
From this point of view, the first house relates to "me,"
the second to "my" possessions and the third to "my"
environment. The third house also describes learning to
communicate in the manner that enables one to fulfill
self-desires. This quadrant represents the first stage of
development in which a person discovers his or her
needs, desires and abilities. If the first is the most heavily
populated quadrant in the horoscope, the individual
focuses initially on self-development as the first or
beginning step toward total development. This does not
mean that one remains in the first stage of growth
throughout life, but future development is heavily
influenced by self-interests.
The second quadrant (houses four through six)
emphasizes the second stage of development, that of
merging self-desires with the needs of others in the home
and family (fourth house), through children and
creativity (fifth house) and in work and service (sixth
house). Although the second quadrant is below the
horizon, as is the first quadrant, it is in the western
hemisphere and therefore indicates less initiative and
greater dependency on others in the developmental
process. Charts with second quadrant emphasis stress
integrating intellectual, emotional and physical needs on
an inner level to prepare for outward development. This
is difficult to achieve without first learning the lessons
of the previous quadrant. The individual must either
combine both stages of development or begin at the
beginning and learn self-development before
concentrating on second quadrant growth. To begin
development in the second quadrant is comparable to
starting a book in the second chapter; one must
eventually read the first chapter in order to get the most
out of what follows.
The third stage of development, which takes place
in the third quadrant (houses seven through nine),
begins with developing the self through relationships
and social interaction. Third quadrant emphasis
concentrates attention on relationships through social
expansion (seventh house), regeneration of energies
(eighth house) and intellectual or spiritual growth
(ninth house). If third quadrant development is to be
fully realized, the first and second developmental
stages must first be completed.
The fourth quadrant (houses ten through twelve)
indicates the final stage in total development, the
development of responsible action in life through
career goals (tenth house), friends and social awareness
(eleventh house) and spiritual progress (twelfth house).
Fourth quadrant emphasis is the most difficult with
which to deal, for the individual's natural tendency
is to begin at the end of the developmental process.
One cannot achieve the full potential for growth
without mastering each stage of development.

The Influence of the Signs in the Houses
Each of the twelve signs influences the horoscope. The
sign on the cusp of a house indicates the mode of action
applied to the affairs of that house; it shows how one
deals with the conditions described therein. An
intercepted sign also influences the house it occupies
and must be considered along with the sign that
appears on the cusp.
Influence of the Signs in the First House
Signs that influence the first house have bearing on the
total person: appearance, temperament, attitudes and
personal affairs. The sign on the Ascendant (the cusp of
the first house) not only influences the first house, it also
colors the entire horoscope because it largely describes
the personality. The Ascending sign is reflected in part
in everything a person does; it is the astrological
signature of the individual. After reading about the signs
on the cusp of the first house, review the section in
Chapter 2 on the signs. In order to gain a broader
understanding of the significance of the sign that appears
on the Ascendant, observe in particular those traits that
describe personal mannerisms, abilities, physical
characteristics and appearance.
Aries, the natural sign of the first house, lends courage,
daring, initiative, self-motivation, competitiveness and
decisiveness to one's nature when it appears on the
cusp or is intercepted in the first house. These people
are enthusiastic, impetuous and impatient.
Taurus on the cusp of the first house shows patience,
determination, stability, endurance, practicality and an
appreciation for the beauty and comforts in life. These
people are industrious, purposeful and responsible.
Gemini on the cusp of the first house indicates agility,
perceptivity, curiosity, restlessness, a somewhat
nervous disposition, busy hands and a busy mind.
These people are versatile, talkative and unsettled.
Cancer on the cusp of the first house gives active
emotions, sensitivity, impressionability, receptivity,
a tendency toward introspection and a strong maternal
instinct. These people are changeable, creative and
security-conscious.
Leo on the cusp of the first house brings out pride,
self-respect, loyalty, ambition, leadership ability and
a sunny disposition. These people are outgoing and
warmhearted. They usually attract a great deal of
attention whatever they do, wherever they go.
Virgo on the cusp of the first house indicates detailed
powers of observation, discrimination, dedication to
service, a modest manner and a concern with health
and hygiene. These people are retiring and meticulous.
Many are habitual faultfinders.
Libra on the cusp of the first house denotes physical
beauty, charm, natural courtesy, a taste for luxury and
an innate desire for harmony and fair play. These
people are refined and peace-loving They are
persuasive in a tactful way.
Scorpio on the cusp of the first house is indicative
of deep passion, penetrating insight, firm resolve,
inflexibility, fearlessness and an unwavering sense

=== Page 67 ===
80 Compendium of Astrology
of purpose. These people are taciturn, secretive and
very capable.
Sagittarius on the cusp of the first house signifies an
adventurous spirit, a straightforward manner, eagerness,
optimism, exuberance and a keen sense of humor. These
people are idealistic, independent and outspoken.
Capricorn on the cusp of the first house denotes
worldly ambition, concern with status, respect for
tradition, conservatism, self-discipline and a reserved
demeanor. These people are serious, well-organized
and materialistic.
Aquarius on the cusp of the first house lends to
originality, resourcefulness, inventiveness, unpredict-
ability and the urge for intellectual and physical
freedom. Thesepeople are unconventional, impersonal

Pisces on the cusp of the first house shows emotional
sensitivity, sympathy, compassion, moodiness,
indecisiveness and a gentle disposition. These people
are pliable, hesitant and mystically inclined.
Influence of the Signs in the Second House
Signs that influence the second house describe a
person's attitudes toward money and material
possessions. These signs indicate in part how a person
manages personal financial affairs.
Review the second house in Chapter 5 and apply
the mode of expression basic to each sign as described
in Chapter 2 to all elements of this house. Follow this
same procedure after reading the section pertaining
to each house in this chapter in order to acquire a
more comprehensive view of the scope of expression
of the signs.
Aries on the cusp of the second house indicates
motivation and dynamic interest in financial affairs.
One's initiative is directed toward moneymaking
activities. However, savings may be practically
nonexistent because of excessive spending.
Taurus, the natural sign of the second house, lends
to practical interest in financial affairs when it occupies
the cusp of this house (or is intercepted within). The
determination to achieve security and enjoy the
comforts of life motivates moneymaking activities.
Gemini on the cusp of the second house shows diverse
financial interests and multiple moneymaking ideas.
In all probability, regular earnings will be supple-
mented by sideline activities. Fluctuations in income
are likely.
Cancer on the cusp of the second house brings out the
need to protect financial interests and to provide for
the future. Security is equated with a substantial "nest
egg" that must remain intact except in emergencies.
The balance of income, however, may be spent freely.
Leo on the cusp of the second house implies creative
direction of financial affairs. Money is a matter of
pride and income is earned and spent with flair. This
can be the position of the "wheeler and dealer."
Virgo on the cusp of the second house denotes sensible
handling of financial affairs. Accurate accounts are
kept of earnings and itemized expenditures. Money
is usually budgeted carefully and spending geared to
income limitations. Since Virgo is a mutable sign,
normal spending habits vary occasionally, and
extravagant tendencies may emerge from time to time.
Libra on the cusp of the second house shows that a
partner or financial agent can be helpful in managing
monetary affairs. Income and expenditures must be
properly balanced if resources are to be adequately
developed.
Scorpio on the cusp of the second house produces an
intense moneymaking drive that can result in a
lucrative income. Financial affairs are considered
private business and financial dealings are often
shrouded in secrecy.
Sagittarius on the cusp of the second house is
associated with good luck in financial affairs, but little
common sense in handling money. This sign position
suggests the free spender.
Capricorn on the cusp of the second house directs
ambition toward moneymaking activities and the
accumulation of material assets. Financial affairs are
handled in a conservative, cautious manner.
Aquarius on the cusp of the second house inspires
unique moneymaking ideas that may be unconven-
tional, quite unusual and almost always original.

Pisces on the cusp of the second house is indicative

Influence of the Signs in the Third House
The sign on the cusp or one intercepted in the third
house influences a person's manner of intellectual
expression. It also shows how a person relates to close
relatives and the neighborhood environment.
Aries on the cusp of the third house describes an
energetic, aggressive intellect. These people are quick
with new ideas. Decisive, sometimes hasty, they
implement plans as they formulate them. They are
outspoken and argumentative. It is difficult for these
people to concentrate on any one topic for a long
period of time. Intellectual interests and conversation
center around adventure, physical activities and
current events. This sign placement fosters sibling
rivalry and conflict with neighbors.
Taurus on the cusp of the third house gives a practical
intellect and a slow, deliberate mind. These people take
ample time to formulate plans or decisions and
stubbornly resist change once they make up their
minds. They think before they speak and mean what
they say. Possessing good powers of concentration,
what they learn, they learn well. Mental interests
gravitate toward finances, art and music. These people
form strong ties of affection with close kin; they are
thoughtful neighbors.
Gemini, the natural sign of the third house, implies
logical intellect, curiosity and mental alacrity when it
appears on the cusp. These people express ideas fluently.
Easily distracted, they need to cultivate good study
habits. Literature or journalism may be appealing
subjects. Drawn toward varied intellectual interests, their
lack of concentration or focus may keep them from
becoming well grounded in any one particular area.
Often they are adept at languages. They usually maintain
an amiable relationship with brothers and sisters, but
remain free of restrictive ties. They endeavor to keep
abreast of neighborhood events and are likely to visit
and telephone neighbors frequently.
Cancer on the cusp of the third house adds emotional
color to the intellect. Imaginative and subjective, one's
feelings and subconscious memories influence the
mind. These people possess excellent powers of recall
and arc interesting conversationalists. Unless the topic
is of prime interest and they are in the mood, they do
not usually like to study. Mental interests fluctuate
though an affinity for the study of home economics,
infant care and botany is common. They tend to
become emotionally attached to close kin; they are
hospitable to neighbors.
Leo on the cusp of the third house indicates creative
thinking and dramatic expression of ideas. Forceful
speakers, they like to be heard and do not hesitate to
expound their views. They are unbiased but
opinionated. They study topics that appeal to them,
refusing to waste time and energy on subjects they
consider irrelevant. Studies connected with the theater,
the stock market and political science usually interest
them. These people are warm toward brothers and
sisters and cordial toward neighbors.
Virgo on the cusp of the third house shows sound
reasoning ability. These people are observant and
perceptive and formulate detailed plans. Not much for
idle conversation, they voice their thoughts precisely
and unambiguously. Mental interests are practical and
sensible. Studious and able to absorb the specifics of
a particular area of study, they can do especially well
in studies dealing with statistics, accounting and
nutrition. The tendency to criticize may interfere with
the relationship to close kin and neighbors.
Libra on the cusp of the third house denotes a keen
intellect and an active mind. Soft-spoken and tactful,
these people enjoy the companionship that
conversation provides. They are drawn to studies
connected with social or behavioral sciences, the fine
arts and decorating; however, they are not inclined
to study hard. These people try to maintain congenial
relations with brothers and sisters and with neighbors.
Scorpio an the cusp of the thud house indicates a
shrewd mind and intellectual insight. Terse and
brusque in speech, these people do not varnish the

Sagittarius on the cusp of the third house reveals an

Capricorn on the cusp of the third house denotes

Influence of the Signs in the Fourth House
Signs that affect the fourth house are descriptive of
a person's approach to family life and domestic affairs.
Aries on the cusp of the fourth house shows active
interest in family affairs. These people display
initiative in handling matters pertaining to the
home. There is competitiveness in the home and
some squabbling and strife but no lasting animosity
or bitterness.
Taurus on the cusp of the fourth house indicates a
stable family life and a home that is reasonably secure
financially. Comfortable surroundings, good food,
music and art are part of the home atmosphere with
this sign placement.
Gemini on the cusp of the fourth house signifies a
lively home life, varied family interests and numerous
changes of residence. Many of these people maintain
two homes simultaneously. Lines of communication
are open between family members; domestic affairs
are discussed objectively.
Cancer, the natural sign of the fourth house, links the
nurturing and protective qualities of the sign to the
home and family affairs when it is placed on the cusp
of the fourth house. These people are emotionally
attached to their roots. Although many moves are
probable, the pull of one's childhood home often
prompts an eventual return to the birthplace.
Leo on the cusp of the fourth house brings out pride
in family, home and heritage. Warmth, love, loyalty
and generosity are natural parts of family life. Home
entertainment can be a real production, lavishly
designed to impress as well as to entertain.
Virgo on the cusp of the fourth house denotes an
orderly home life. Domestic affairs are handled in a

systematic manner. The household is neat, uncluttered
and probably hygienically clean. Family life is not
devoid of affection, but there is a noticeable lack of
warmth and gaiety.
Libra on the cusp of the fourth house is indicative of a
harmonious home life where companionship and general
accord are valued. Family affairs are treated in a fair

Signs which influence the fifth house bear upon a

Cancer on the cusp of the fifth Ziouse signifies emotional

Leo, the natural sign of the fifth house, fosters a

Influence of the Signs in the Sixth House
Signs which influence the sixth house affect a person's
approach to work and service. These signs show how
one reacts to routine working conditions. They also
have bearing upon health and hygiene.
Aries on the cusp of the sixth house is indicative of
the person who will go out and actively look for a job
rather than wait for opportunities to arise through
chance or circumstance. These people are energetic
workers who would rather boss than be bossed. They
are susceptible to feverish ailments; many are accident-
prone. If these people work with dangerous
equipment, they should follow strict safety procedures.
Taurus on the cusp of the sixth house shows a worker
who is steady and reliable. These people perform
their jobs capably and do not miss work without valid
reasons. They follow job procedures and regulations
consistently. They can give orders as well as take
them, but they prefer the former. These people are
predisposed to sore throats, especially if the job or
home atmosphere is contaminated by irritants such
as smoke or dust.

Aquarius on the cusp of the sixth house denotes an

Leo on the cusp of the tenth house denotes a strong

Aries on the cusp of the twelfth house denotes anxieties

Gemini on the cusp of the twelfth house generates

Cancer on the cusp of the twelfth house signifies

Planets and Moon s Nodes in the Houses
The energy of a planet is primarily directed toward the
affairs of the house it occupies and the house(s) it rules
in the horoscope. A planet has some influence in its
natural house, but this influence is secondary to that of
the planets posited in that house and those ruling the sign
on the cusp or a sign intercepted within the house.
Planets also influence houses ruled and occupied by
other planets with which they form aspects. The strength
and flavor of planetary action channeled through aspects
depends upon the planets involved and the type of
aspects formed. Aspects are defined in Chapter 14 and
discussed in detail in Chapters 16 through 26.
A void house, one which contains no planets, does
not necessarily indicate lack of activity in related affairs.
Aspects to its ruling planet energize an empty house. If
few aspects are formed with its ruler, the individual tends
to be more objective and less personally concerned about
its affairs. Greater interest occurs during periods when
transits or progressed planets occupy the house or
activate it by aspecting its ruler.
Planets and Nodes in the First House
A planet that occupies the first house energizes the
individual's personality and personal interests accord-
ing to the nature of the planet. A person's disposition,
mannerisms, attitudes and physical characteristics
reflect qualities associated with a planet in the first
house within the range descibed by the sign in which
the planet is placed
The Sun in the first house implies pride, self-
confidence, initiative and willpower. These people
possess keen self-awareness. Their ambitions are
clearly defined. A strong urge to achieve power
through self-directed efforts is present. This placement
is indicative of the attention-seeker and the leader. The
Sun in the first house also increases vitality and
personal warmth.
The Moon in the first house indicates an emotional
disposition, a changeable temperament. Intuitive,
impressionable and receptive, these people are subject
to periods of moodiness. They are sensitive to social
pressures and public opinion and instinctively react
to the needs and demands of other people with whom
they come in contact. Many go on eating binges as
an emotional release and, as a result, are apt to gain
too much weight.
Mercury in the first house contributes to intellectual
awareness and versatility. These people like to talk
about themselves, their personal interests and ideas.
Being restless, many tend to develop nervous habits.
Unless Mercury is adversely aspected with the other
planets in the horoscope, these people are agile and
well coordinated; many are ambidextrous.
Venus in the first house signifies social charm. These
people are friendly, companionable and polite. Many
are unusually good looking. Aware of their appearance,
they dress attractively and behave graciously. If Venus
is in disharmony with the other planets, these people may
be self-indulgent, vain or extravagant. Nevertheless, this
placement is conducive to popularity.
Mars is accidentally dignified in the first house because
the first is this planet's natural house. Mars in the first

Jupiter in the first house indicates an exuberant nature

Planets and Nodes in the Second House
Planets occupying the second house activate financial
conditions in the life of the individual; these planets
direct energy toward the handling of personal finances.
The Sun in the second house shows an active interest
in financial affairs. These people display initiative in
moneymaking pursuits and are likely to manage their
finances personally. They are proud of their earning
capacity and their possessions because they equate
power with money and material belongings. Generous
by nature, many are extravagent, ostentatious spenders.
The Moon in the second house is indicative of periodic
financial fluctuations. If the Moon is in a fixed sign,
variations are less broad. Despite changes in monetary
affairs, these people depend largely upon financial
stability for their emotional security. They spend freely
on their homes and families.
Mercury in the second house combines financial and
intellectual interests. These people are seldom at a loss
for moneymaking ideas. They seek education as a
means of increasing their earning power. A bit tricky
when it comes to handling financial affairs, they are
not necessarily dishonest, merely shrewd. They keep
detailed records of income and expenditures.
Venus is accidentally dignified in the second house, its
house of natural rulership. This placement is generally
helpful to financial affairs. These people are rarely
underpaid. They derive much enjoyment and satisfaction
from their money and possessions; purchases reflect a
taste for luxury and pleasure. They are inclined to be
extravagant, but unless Venus is badly afflicted they
probably can afford to splurge. With Venus in the second
house, the individual may benefit financially from
marriage and business partnerships.

Mars in the second house directs incentive toward
moneymaking activities. Where financial affairs are

Jupiter in the second house safeguards one's financial

Neptune in the second house shows a tendency to be

Pluto in the second house indicates that the potential

The North Node in the second house signifies

The South Node in the second house points out the

reduce the potential for financial development.
Planets and Nodes in the Third House
A planet posited in the third house generates mental
activity and sparks one's intellectual drives. It is
associated with learning aptitude, reasoning ability,
and the capacity to communicate ideas verbally or in
writing. A planet in the third house also has influence
on communter travel, neighborhood associations, and
relations with brothers, sisters and other close kin
(except parents).
The Sun in the third house indicates pride, superiority
and self-satisfaction in intellectual matters. These
people possess a compelling drive to acquire
knowledge and to prove themselves intellectually.
They are able to develop good command of language.
Depending upon the aspects, they may be forceful
speakers who are convincing and authoritative, or
opinionated and arrogant braggarts who are given to
pompous speech. They treat brothers and sisters
warmly and take active interest in the neighborhood.
The Moon in the third house aids the memory and
imagination: it also creates a restless mind and a
tendency to daydream. These people find it difficult
to be objective since their emotions intrude upon their
thoughts. Decisions are prompted by emotional
considerations; logic is affected by feelings. Frequent
changes of scenery and routine keep these people from
becoming discontented.
Mercury is accidentally dignified in the third house
because this is Mercury's natural house. This placement
enhances intellectual interest and communicative skills.
These people are curious, perceptive and fluent. They
possess a keen desire to learn, although the mind lacks
perseverance and tends to skip from one topic to another.
Knowledge is diverse but may lack depth. Changeable,
restless and fond of travel, many of these people are
continually on the move. They keep in touch with
brothers, sisters and neighborhood happenings.
Venus in the third house shows that intellectual
preferences lean toward music, the arts and cultural
interests. These people are charming con\'ersationalists

Planets and Nodes in the Fourth House
Planets that fall in the fourth house direct energy into

The Sun in the fourth house signifies that self-

places that reflect their importance. They tend to
dominate the household. The Sun in the fourth house
also implies that the father is the most influential
parent in the individual's early environment. Later
years should be productive and reasonably secure.
The Moon is accidentally dignified in the fourth house,
its house of natural rulership. Individuals whose Moon
is placed in the fourth house form closely-knit family
ties; they identify emotionally with home and family.

Planets and Nodes in the Fifth House
Planets which occupy the fifth house act to energize
creative self-expression and artistic endeavors. These
planets also influence romantic affairs, the pursuit of
entertainment, leisure interests and children.
The Sun in the fifth house, where it is accidentally

work with young people in some way during their

sign in which the Sun is placed and the aspects it forms
with the other planets, these individuals may be prone
to taking unwise speculative risks.
The Moon in the fifth house shows that emotional

literary art forms and intellectual games and hobbies.

partners. They are capricious in love and frequently

births are possible.
Venus in the fifth house increases the chance of happy
romances. Venus here also enhances the pleasure derived

Speculative activities are both gainful and enjoyable.

Mars in the fifth house indicates an aggressive and

Artistic and creative interests might include sculpting,

Saturn in the fifth house restrains creative expression.

Planets and Nodes in the Sixth House
Planets which occupy the sixth house exert a major
influence on conditions relevant to the individual's
work and associated relationships. These planets have
a bearing on the services one performs. They are also
significant to health, sickness and disease.
The Sun in the sixth house gives the tendency to
dominate the workplace. These people find satisfaction
in performing their jobs to the best of their abilities
and in the recognition they receive as a result. If the
Sun is well aspected, vitality and resistance to disease
are strong; if it is afflicted, vigor and recuperative
powers are reduced.
The Moon in the sixth house causes job performance
and work relationships to fluctuate according to the
individual's emotional state. Physical health is
dependent upon emotional health. A lack of emotional
stability can induce psychosomatic ailments.
Mercury in the sixth house, its house of accidental
dignity, indicates that the individual performs work
with detailed accuracy. These people converse freely
with job associates and like to talk about their work
and their health. An aversion to monotonous routine
often prompts numerous job changes. Anxiety and
nervous tension can deplete the individual's health.
Venus in the sixth house is characteristic of the
individual who gains pleasure and satisfaction from
work. Harmonious working conditions and congenial
job relationships are essential to a competent and
productive job performance. These people are usually
cooperative and friendly, well liked by co-workers.
If Venus is afflicted, they may be susceptible to sore
throats and urinary ailments.
Mars in the sixth house gives a strong incentive for
work. Willing and enthusiastic workers, they are also
competitive in their jobs. Job relations are apt to be
discordant, expecially if Mars is adversely aspected.
Machinery, guns, knives, any sort of weapons and fire
present potential occupational hazards. Safety
regulations should be stringently adhered to if the
individual works with or around such hazards. When
ill, these people frequently run high fevers.
Jupiter in the sixth house is helpful to general working
conditions and to health. These people have little
trouble obtaining jobs. Most benefit from service to
others. If Jupiter is afflicted, the individual may suffer
from liver complaints stemming from dietary excesses.
Saturn in the sixth house typifies the serious,
responsible worker; however, work is liable to be
laborious and arduous. These people seldom socialize
with job associates. Saturn in this house weakens the
vitality and makes necessary a lengthy recuperation
period when illness strikes. These people may be
subject to chronic illnesses.
Uranus in the sixth house signifies an unpredictable
or unusual work situation. Unexpected circumstances
often force job changes. Job opportunities may arise
suddenly; jobs may be terminated with little or no
notice. These people prefer to work where they are
free to experiment with new techniques. Friendly,

occupational hazards if Uranus is afflicted.
Neptune in the sixth house introduces deceptive

Planets which fall in the seventh house influence a
person's interaction with society. These planets
activate marriage and the partnerships in which one
becomes involved.
The Sun in the seventh house ties the ego and the drive

The Moon in the seventh house indicates that

Mercury in the seventh house emphasizes the need for
communication and intellectual rapport in marriage
and partnerships. The individual forms relationships
with youthful, intelligent persons. Many of these
people marry early in life, or they choose a younger
marriage partner.
Venus is accidentally dignified in the seventh, its
natural house. This placement fosters a happy
marriage and profitable partnerships. Business
relationships are based on mutual cooperation and
harmony; personal relationships are based on
companionship and love.
Mars in the seventh house promotes initiative and
action in marriage and partnership interests. These

undermined by bickering and strife.
Jupiter in the seventh house is beneficial to marriage
and partnerships. Partnership activities result in

religious differences can be"disruptive to marriage. In

Saturn in the seventh house adds enduring qualities
which are helpful to lasting relationships; however,
marriage or partnerships can be burdensome. These
people are reluctant to assume the responsibilities of
marriage until they or their prospective mates are

in life than their contemporaries.
Uranus in the seventh house provokes exciting and
novel relationships which are apt to be short-lived,

find their personal freedom curtailed by the

Neptune in the seventh house inspires an idealistic
concept of marriage. Depending upon Neptunian

Pluto in the seventh house stresses the importance of

The South Node in the seventh house indicates strained

A planet occupying the eighth house activates joint

Planetary energy is directed toward conditions con-

are not solely the individual's responsibility or do not

The Sun in the eighth house is a good indication of

These people usually gain through inheritance and/or

Planetary Dispositors
The planetary ruler(s) of a sign is said to disposit any
planet(s) placed in that sign. When a planet occupies a
sign other than the one it rules, this planet is disposited
by the ruler(s) of the sign in which it is placed. The
dispositor of a planet influences the action of the
disposited planet and its affairs and is taken into
consideration in the interpretation of the planets in the
various signs. Interrelationships in the horoscope
particularize these meanings. For example, Jupiter,
dispositor of Venus in Sagittarius, influences Venusian
affairs and expression in the manner consistent with its
horoscope standing. If Jupiter is badly afflicted, some
negative Jupiterian qualities manifest in Venusian
activities to the degree indicated by Venus aspects. An
aspect formed between a planet and its dispositor
strengthens the influence of the dispositor on the
disposited planet. If the planets form no mutual aspect
but both are in aspect with the same third planet, their
energies are united by the third planet, and the
dispositor s influence is greater than if no link is shown.
Examination of a dispositor sheds light on motives that
are not immediately apparent in the disposited planet.
In Chapter 13, Figure 18, Jupiter disposits Venus; they
are not in aspect to each other, but both aspect the Sun,
also disposited by Jupiter (Sun conjunct Venus, Sun
square Jupiter). Refer to Chapterl4, "Aspects Defined."
Unconventional standards and group activities that are
not explained by Venus alone, but are reflected in Venus'
influence in the first (Taurus on the cusp, ruled by
Venus), second (naturally ruled by Venus), sixth (Libra
on the cusp, ruled by Venus) and the seventh (occupied
and ruled naturally by Venus) houses are attributed in
part to the influence of Jupiter as dispositor in Aquarius
in the eleventh house.
Two planets that are in mutual reception by virtue
of each occupying the other's sign of natural rulership
(dignity) disposit each other; planetary influence is
mutual. These planets are interpreted first as they
appear in the horoscope, then additional information
is obtained by placing each in its own sign in the same
degree it occupies in the other sign.

Figure 8. The Sun As Final Dispositor
The dispositor of a planet indirectly disposits anv
planets placed in the sign ruled by the planet it
disposits. For example, if (he Sun is in Taurus it is
disposited by Venus, the planetary ruler of Taurus:

=== Page 93 ===
106 Compendium of Astrology
Venus then indirectly disposits all planets in Leo
because these planets are disposited by the Sun, ruler
of Leo, and Venus disposits the Sun.
A planet that occupies its sign of dignity may serve
as indirect dispositor for several planets. It is possible
for one planet to act as dispositor or indirect dispositor
for the remaining nine planets. When this happens the
dispositing planet becomes the final dispositor of the
horoscope and, as such, bears influence on the overall
tenor of the horoscope.
Consider the planetary arrangement shown in Figure
8: Sun in Leo, Moon in Leo, Mercury in Leo, Venus
in Cancer, Mars in Gemini, Jupiter in Leo, Saturn in
Virgo, Uranus in Scorpio, Neptune in Sagittarius and
Pluto in Libra.
The Sun disposits the Moon, Mercury and Jupiter
because these planets are placed in Leo, and the Sun
rules Leo. The Sun in its sign of natural rulership has
no dispositor. Venus is disposited by the Moon, ruler
of Cancer; in turn, the Moon is disposited by the Sun,
which therefore indirectly disposits Venus. Mars in
Gemini and Saturn in Virgo are both disposited by
Mercury, ruler of Gemini and Virgo. The Sun
indirectly disposits Mars and Saturn because it
disposits Mercury. Uranus is disposited by Mars and
Pluto, rulers of Scorpio; Mars is indirectly disposited
by the Sun and Pluto is disposited by Venus, which
is indirectly disposited by the Sun; therefore, both
Pluto and Uranus are indirectly disposited by the Sun.
Neptune in Sagittarius is disposited by Jupiter, which
is also disposited by the Sun. Thus, all planets lead
to the Sun; the chain stops with the Sun because the
Sun acts as its own dispositor. In this example, the
Sun is the final dispositor.
During days in which no planet changes sign, the
final dispositor, if one exists, is the same in the
horoscope of every person bom that day. Because of
astrological variations observed at different times and
in different localities, a single planet seldom influences
any two horoscopes in an identical manner. The final
dispositor links all planets in a horoscope and thereby
colors all planetary action; it describes underlying
motivation that prompts expression of planetary
drives, motivation contingent upon the nature of the
dispositor and its bearing in the horoscope.
The basic principles of a final dispositor describe
general motivation. Its influence is broad and touches
all areas of life. The Sun as final dispositor indicates
that the need for ego-satisfaction and self-esteem is
linked to other drives. For example, Venus rules the
principle of attraction, but the desire to attract others
is a matter of ego if the Sun is final dispositor. Persons
whose Sun is the final dispositor seek relationships and
activities that enhance self-esteem.
The Moon as final dispositor shows that emotional
needs and family^ considerations underlie decisions and
actions. These people enter jobs and form relationships
that provide emotional security and inner satisfaction.
Mercury as final dispositor indicates intellectual
motivation. These people base decisions on logic; they
choose companions and activities that provide mental
stimulation. If Mercury is in Virgo rather than Gemini,
the drive for perfection is evident as well.
In Taurus, Venus as final dispositor emphasizes
material needs. The desire for financial well-being and
physical comfort underlies all decisions and actions.
Venus in Libra as final dispositor brings out needs for
companionship and harmony. Decisions and activities
reflect a desire for balance and cooperation.
Mars in Aries as final dispositor motivates physical
action on all levels. These people find no satisfaction
in sedentary interests. They act decisively to keep their
affairs moving. In Scorpio, Mars as final dispositor
links sexual needs to other drives. Sexual energies
stimulate creativity, worldly ambition, sense of
purpose and activity in all affairs. But fulfillment is
incomplete if sexual satisfaciton, a prime motivating
factor, is lacking.
Jupiter as final dispositor stirs motivation based on
the need for truth and integrity in actions and
relationships. Decisions spring from unselfish desires.
A strong element of self-sacrifice, not shown with
Jupiter in Sagittarius, is pronounced if the planet is
in Pisces. Jupiter in Sagittarius inspires intellectual
motivation; in Pisces, emotional motivation.
With Saturn as final dispositor in Capricorn,
worldly ambition is the driving force behind planetary
drives. The need for recognition and status colors
decisions and actions in personal affairs as well as in
mundane pursuits. Motivation is essentially selfish; in
Aquarius, Saturn-inspired selfishness is tempered by
humane considerations, but ambitious drive remains
the prime motivating factor.
Uranus as final dispositor describes motivation
rooted in the need for change. If Uranus is well
aspected, it is a most significant indication of progress.

Planetary Dispositors 107
Future-oriented, these people are urged onward by the
desire to improve conditions and relationships. If
Uranus is afflicted, precipitous changes produce an
erratic state of affairs. These people find little of the
satisfaction they seek in change, but they are
compelled to continuously explore new interests,

Neptune as final dispositor indicates spiritual

Pluto as final dispositor produces an almost

Two planets in mutual reception share final
dispositorship if they jointly serve as dispositors or
indirect dispositors for the remaining eight planets. If one
of the joint dispositors has greater standing in a
horoscope, the stronger planet is the more influential of
the two in respect to dispositorship. If Mars in Capricorn
(Saturn's sign of dignity) shares dispositorship with
Saturn in Aries (Mars' sign of dignity) by virtue of
mutual reception. Mars is the more influential dispositor
of the two because Mars is exalted in Capricorn and
Saturn is in fall in Aries. A mutual reception between
the Moon in Sagittarius and Jupiter in Cancer shows
Jupiter to be the stronger dispositor because Jupiter is
exalted in Cancer and the Moon is peregrine (lacks
standing) in Sagittarius. If two planets in mutual
reception have equal standing in the horoscope according
to sign, house placement and aspects, they exert equal
influence as joint dispositors.
There can be no final dispositor in a horoscope
unless at least one planet occupies a sign it rules or
two planets are in mutual reception. If more than one
planet is dignified and each disposits one or more of
the remaining planets, the dispositing planets are given
added weight in the horoscope, although influence is
not as widespread as that of a final dispositor.
With no planets in ruling signs, it is possible to have
a continuous circle of dispositors. Such is the case for
the planetary sign positions shown in Figure 9: Sun
in Scorpio, Moon in Scorpio, Mercury in Scorpio,
Venus in Sagittarius, Mars in Taurus, Jupiter in
Aquarius, Saturn in Cancer, Uranus in Libra, Neptune
in Sagittarius and Pluto in Libra.

elements are otherwise present in the horoscope: in
a well-aspected horoscope, planetary energies are
mutually supportive.

The Shaping of the Horoscope
Though many horoscopes show similarities, few are
exactly alike. The disparity of a few miles in birth
location alters the horoscopes of persons bom at
the same time. In the natal charts of twins, the
difference of a few minutes in birthtime results in
slight but often important variations between the two
horoscopes. Nevertheless, many horoscopes show
similar planetary arrangements.
The distribution of the planets around the horoscope
forms recognizable planetary patterns or pictures.
Seven such patterns have been identified by the emi-
nent astrologer. Marc Edmund Jones {The Guide to
Horoscope Interpretation, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania;
David McKay, 1941),
A horoscope is classified according to its shaping, that
is, according to the pattern that the planets form within
the horoscope. The planetary pattern has a bearing on
the general character of the horoscope. Shaping is
considered part of the overall picture. It does not
overshadow or equal specific astrological factors such
as planetary influence or aspects, although it may rein-
force these things. The extent and direction of shaping
emphasis is determined by the total horoscope.
All horoscopes fall into one of the seven categories
described by Jones. In some instances the planetary
pattern may not be clear-cut, but one category will
fit more closely than the others. The following
examples picture the ideal planetary distribution for
each type.
The Splash
The Splash is indicated by a
fairly uniform planetary
arrangement. The planets
are more or less evenly
distributed around the
horoscope. Usually no more
than two planets occupy
any one sign. The space
between planets is seldom
greater than that covered by two consecutive signs or
two consecutive houses. Ideally, planets should be placed
no more than a sextile (60°) apart.
This scattering of planets suggests a scattering or
dispersion of interests. Splash people are versatile. They
involve themselves in a wide range of activities. Because
of such diversity, interest may be superficial if the rest
of the horoscope shows lack of depth or perseverance.
The Bowl
The Bowl shows all ten
planets occupying approx-
imately one-half of the
horoscope with the other
half devoid of planets. If
the planets happen to fall
exclusively to one side of
either the vertical or the
horizontal axis, the main

thrust of planetary energy is expressed according to
hemisphere emphasis.
Bowl people are self-contained. They direct their
energies toward the areas in which the planets are
placed and tend to exclude or be excluded from
unoccupied areas. The occupied half of the horoscope
represents what these people contribute in terms of
experience; the empty half indicates challenge.
The planet moving away from the empty half of the
horoscope, according to the natural direction of the
zodiac, is designated the leading planet. This planet
leads the group clockwise in the horoscope. The
leading planet is the key to meeting the challenge and
filling the void that exists in the unoccupied half of
the horoscope.
The Bucket
The Bucket is similar to the
Bowl. In this configuration
nine planets occupy one-
half of the horoscope. One
planet is placed in the other
half, roughly opposing the
group of nine, forming the
"handle" of the bucket. If
the handle planet is the
only planet occupying that particular hemisphere, it
is called a singleton. Two planets placed in close
conjunction, within a degree of each other, may serve
together as a bucket handle for the eight planets
occupying the opposite hemisphere.
Bucket people bear some similarity to Bowl people
in that activity is directed toward the occupied section
of the horoscope. However, the handle planet is the
focal point of action. A heavy planet at the handle
gives balance to the horoscope; a lighter planet such
as the Moon is unable to focus planetary energies as
effectively as a heavier one unless it is in close
conjunction with another planet, then the two planets
function together.
The Bundle
The Bundle consists of a tightly packed planetary
arrangement. All ten planets are confined to the space
of a trine (120°) or very nearly so. Only four or
possibly five consecutive signs are occupied by planets.
About two-thirds of the horoscope is empty.
The Bundle is uncommon
and so is the individual in
whose horoscope it appears.
Bundle people are in some
way unique. They confine
and focus their interests,
specializing in the area(s)
indicated by the most
heavily occupied part of
the horoscope. These people are self-contained and
narrow. Because planetary energy is concentrated in such
a small portion of the chart, the scope of experience is
somewhat limited, but activity in that area is powerful.
The planet leading clockwise directs planetary drives.
The Locomotive
^ The Locomotive is the

Bundle. All ten planets are
placed within the space of
two consecutive trines
(240°); one trine (120°) is
empty. This planetary ar-
rangement occupies two-
thirds of the horoscope;
one-third is devoid of planets.
Locomotive people are self-motivated and self-driven.
Essentially goal-oriented, they are dynamic people who
seem to possess almost unlimited energy. Once they
achieve a particular objective, they are ready to begin
working toward another. The planet leading clockwise
signifies motivation; the house it occupies shows the
main focus of energy.
The See-Saw

See-Saw people seek balance. They usually consider

The Splay is somewhat

Splay people are individualists who resist the system.

Few horoscopes meet the ideal requirements of a
shaping category. It is recommended that the student

The Lunation Cycle and Eclipses
The changing face of the Moon has fascinated
earthlings since time immemorial. Who has not
watched the almost invisible new Moon "grow" into
a round full Moon and then "shrink" to another new
Moon? As the Moon travels around Earth, following
Earth's orbit of the Sun, it turns on its own axis. In
so doing it seems to change shape. Of course, it does
not, but as its position changes relative to Sun and
Earth so does the visible portion of the Moon, the
portion that reflects sunlight to Earth.
The Lunation Cycle
The time interval between two successive new Moons
(lunations), the lunation cycle, is about twenty-nine
and one-half days. The lunation cycle is divided into
two phases, waxing and waning (see Chapter 4). Each
of these phases is sub-divided into two quarters; each
of the four quarters consists of two stages.
The first stage of the first quarter of the lunation
cycle begins with the new Moon, starting the waxing
phase. At the time of lunation, the Moon is in the same
sign and degree of the zodiac as the Sun (conjunct the
Sun). As the Moon moves away from the Sun's
zodiacal position, a crescent becomes visible within
a few days. The crescent Moon completes the first
stage of the first quarter of the lunation cycle. In
approximately one week following the new Moon, a
waxing half-moon, called the first quarter Moon,
appears, ending the first quarter and beginning the
second. At this point in the lunation cycle, the Moon's
zodiacal position is 90° past that of the Sun.
The first quarter Moon enlarges to a gibbous Moon
(about three-quarters of a circle) in the first stage of
the second quarter, then swells to a full Moon to mark
the completion of both the second quarter and the
waxing phase and the beginning of the third quarter
and the waning phase (see Figure 10). At the full
Moon, the Sun and Moon lie exactly opposite each
other in the zodiac; the Moon then starts to approach
the zodiacal position of the Sun.

During the fourth quarter a second crescent, the
balsamic Moon, is formed in the first stage; the
quarter ends with a new Moon and another lunation
cycle begins.
The solar-lunar relationship described by the stage of
the Moon's cycle at birth has bearing upon personality
integration. Assimilation and utilization of solar energy
depends upon the lunar cycle as follows:
New Moon (Moon conjunct Sun to Moon 45° ahead
of Sun): Motivation is instinctive, actions impulsive.
People born during this period in the lunation cycle
seek and meet challenges eagerly. They are magnetic
and relate vividly to others. Because they project
feeling and personality, many are good actors.
Crescent Moon (Moon 45° to 90° ahead of the Sun):
This stage represents struggle against the established
pattern; the new is pitted against the old, but the old
always hangs on in some form. These people strive
to break with the past and seek new vistas.
First Quarter Moon (Moon 90° to 135° ahead of the
Sun): These people are survivors; they act through and
deal with crises. They attract active, stimulating, noisy
situations. Dynamic and energetic (within sign
dictates), they may try to move ahead too quickly.
Gibbous Moon (Moon 135° to 180°—opposite—ahead
of the Sun): Motivation is based in self-
analysis. These people are conscious of their actions
and feel prompted to make life something of value.
They tend to keep a running score or evaluation of
personal progress.
Full Moon (Moon opposite to 135° behind the Sun):
Motivation stems from relationships; action is
objective, structured, purposeful. These people seek
self-perfection through bonding instinct and intellect.
Disseminating Moon (Moon 135° to 90° behind the
Sun): Distribution of knowlege and information is
important in this phase. Natural communicators of
ideas in which they believe, these people pursue their
causes with dedication and purpose.
V
Last Quarter Moon (Moon 90° to 45° behind the Sun):
This stage is associated witfra crisis in consciousness.
An inner or hidden germinating process prods
reorientation of self and reality resulting in continuous
states of revision and change.
Balsamic Moon (Moon 45° behind to conjunction with
the Sun): Commitment to destiny is represented here.
These people sen§e that something larger than self can
manifest through them if they permit it. They may be
prophets of the future or martyrs to it.
The rhythmic cycle of the Moon describes a fluid,
changing relationship as the Moon moves through the
signs. Two successive lunations usually occur in
sequential signs of the zodiac but not always.
Sometimes when a new Moon occurs in an early
degree of a sign, the next new Moon falls in a late
degree of the same sign. A new Moon that occurs in
the same sign as the previous lunation signifies the need
to re-evaluate relationships as indicated by sign and
horoscope position.
The Moon crosses the ecliptic an average of twice
during a lunation cycle, once at its North Node while
traveling from south to north, and once at its South
Node as it moves southward (see the section on the
Moon's Nodes in Chapter 3). If, at lunation, both
luminaries are equidistant from the celestial equator
(both are in the same degree of declination; refer to
Chapter 1) and both are placed within 19° of one of
the Moon's Nodes, an eclipse can occur.
Solar Eclipses
When the Sun, Moon and Earth are
in direct alignment as the Moon
' - passes between the Sun and Earth,
jRrtHO the Sun is eclipsed, either hidden
wholly (a total eclipse) or in part (a
partial eclipse) from Earth. A solar eclipse always occurs
during a new Moon, but an eclipse does not take place
at every new Moon.
Other specific criteria must be met in order for the
Sun, Moon and Earth to be properly aligned for a solar
eclipse event. For a solar eclipse to develop, both the
Sun and Moon must be either north or south of the
celestial equator (both luminaries must lie on the same
side of the celestial equator) and the luminaries may

=== Page 100 ===
The Lunation Cycle and Eclipses 115
not be separated by more than 1° declination. In
addition, one of the Moon's Nodes must fall within
18° 31' of the zodiacal position of the Sun and Moon.
If the Moon's Node is found within 9°55' of the
zodiacal longitude of the Sun and Moon at the time
of an eclipse, the eclipse is total. If the distance between
the Moon's Node and the luminaries is between 9° 55'
and 11° 15', the eclipse may be either total or partial;
at greater distances up to the eclipse limits of 18°31',
solar eclipses are always partial.
A solar eclipse may last from about one minute to
a maximum of seven minutes and forty seconds. An
eclipse begins on the western side of the Sun and moves
across its face to the eastern side. Solar eclipses usually
occur twice a year at six-month intervals, although
there can be as many as five solar eclipses visible at
some point on Earth in a given year. Solar eclipses
operate on an approximate eighteen-year cycle called
the Saros Cycle. An average of forty-one solar eclipses
take place during one Saros Cycle.
During a solar eclipse, the Moon blocks sunlight from
Earth; its shadow effectively reduces the Sun's astro-
logical influence on Earth and in the natal horoscope.
A solar eclipse that occurs at the time of birth
weakens the Sun's action in the horoscope of the
individual whether or not the eclipse is visible at the
birthplace. The affairs governed by the Sun lack
strength unless other planetsenergize these areas. The
individual's vitality is depleted.
Lunar Eclipses
A lunar ecplise (eclipse of the Moon)
takes place at the time of a full Moon
when the luminaries occupy opposite
points in the zodiac. As the Earth
passes between the Sun and Moon,
the Moon is darkened by Earth's shadow moving across
the Moon's surface from east to west.
In order for a lunar eclipse to occur, one of the
luminaries must be in north declination and the other
in south, and both in the same degree of declination or
within 1° of each other. Each luminary must lie within
12° 15' of the zodiacal position occupied by one of the
Moon's Nodes. If the luminaries and the Nodes are not
separated by more than 3° 45' zodiacal longitude, the
lunar eclipse is total. If the luminaries and Nodes are
separated by less than 6° but more than 3°45', the
eclipse may be either total or partial; at separating
distances greater than 6° and less than 12° 15', the lunar
eclipse is partial.
A lunar eclipse may last as long as one hour and forty
minutes. The maximum number of lunar eclipses that
occur in one year is three; there may be none. One Saros
Cycle usually contains twenty-nine lunar eclipses in
addition to the forty-one solar eclipses for a total of
seventy eclipses. When a lunar eclipse occurs, it always
precedes or follows a solar eclipse within about two
weeks. Lunar eclipses never take place without a
companion solar eclipse: solar eclipses can occur as
single events.
The function of a lunareclipse in the natal horoscope
differs from that of a solar eclipse. The Moon has no
light of its own; it reflects the radiance of the Sun. When
the Earth blocks the Sun's rays, the Moon is dark and
cold. A lunareclipse in a natal horoscope frustrates the
emotions and warps instinctive reactions. The affairs
governed by the Moon are dependent upon the planets
with which the Moon is in aspect.
Comparatively few people are born during eclipses.
Those that are tend to be extremely sensitive to future
eclipses if these eclipses occur in the same degree
occupied by a natal planet or one of the angles of the
horoscope. Later eclipses that activate a natal
horoscopebring pressure to bear upon the affairs ruled
by the planets and houses affected.
The Prenatal Eclipse
Because an eclipse has an astrological after-effect, the
solar eclipse that directly precedes birth stamps the
natal horoscope even if the eclipse occurred six months
prior to birth.
The first solar eclipse that precedes birth, regardless
of the time difference, is called the prenatal eclipse. The
prenatal eclipse elevates the house that contains the sign
and degree of the eclipse. In effect, the prenatal eclipse
sensitizes the affairs ruled by the house in which it falls;
subsequent eclipses that fall in this house or aspect its
rulers re-emphasize the affairs of the house throughout
life. This can be a sore spot for the individual if the rulers
of the house are afflicted in the natal horoscope; if the
rulers are well placed and well aspected, the prenatal
eclipse reinforces the promise of the house. The influence
of the prenatal eclipse depends entirely on the horoscope;
it merely emphasizes what is there for good or ill.

=== Page 101 ===
116 Compendium of Astrology
Occultations
If a planet other than the Sun or Moon is eclipsed, the
event is termed an occultation. The energy of an occulted
(hidden) planet, absorbed by the eclipsing planet, which
blocks Earth's view, is distributed in the horoscope via
the eclipsing planet. The eclipsing planet dominates the
house(s) and affairs ruled by the occulted planet. For
example, if Uranus, occulted by the Moon, rules the
eleventh house and the Moon rules the fourth, matters
pertaining to friends and organizations (eleventh house
affairs) operate through the home and family (fourth
house); change, a Uranian quality, manifests through
the emotions, a lunar function.

CALCULATIONS

=== Page 103 ===
11 The Took of Astrology
Because numerous computer services are now
available, many astrologers no longer construct
horoscopes. These astrologers devote their skills to
delineating (interpreting) horoscopes. For the person
seriously interested in astrology, however, there are
advantages to knowing how to correctly erect one. An
astrologer who is familiar with the calculations can
readily spot any errors that may exist in a prepared
horoscope. As beginners learn how to calculate and
erect an accurate horoscope, they gain understanding
of the basis for astrology. One begins to get the feel
of a horoscope during the process of drawing it up.
The two major steps in calculating a horoscope are
as follows: (1) determining the house cusps and (2)
locating the planets. The essential data required are
the exact time, date and place of birth. The following
tools are needed: (1) an atlas or longitude and latitude
table, (2) a time zone/time changes book, (3) a Table
of Houses and (4) an ephemeris. Prepared chart forms
(horoscope blanks), printed calculation sheets and a
calculator are helpful
Geographic Longitude and Latitude
It is necessary to describe the location of the birthplace
in terms consistent with those used in astrological
calculations. The location of a place is defined by its
geographic longitude and latitude. Longitude and
latitude tables list the locations of numerous towns and
cities throughout the world.
Longitude and latitude are given in degrees and
minutes. Some tables also include seconds of arc. The
symbol for degrees is _L, for minutes: ' and for
seconds: Jl. One writes 10° 35' 06" instead of 10
degrees, 35 minutes and 6 seconds. There are sixty
seconds of arc in each minute of longitude and latitude
and sixty minutes in each degree of longitude and
latitude.
One should not confuse minutes and seconds of
longitude or latitude with minutes and seconds of time.
Longitude describes the distance in arc a place is
situated east or west of Greenwich, England. The
longitude of Greenwich is 0°. In writing, the direction
of longitude follows the degrees. West is abbreviated
"W" and east "E." Eighty degrees west longitude is
written: 80° W. If minutes and/or seconds are
included, the direction of longitude is inserted between
the degrees and minutes. Eighty degress and forty-eight
minutes west longitude is written as 80° W 48'.
Latitude describes the distance in arc a place is located
north or south of the Earth's equator. The latitude at
the equator is 0°. Latitude is written in the same style
as longitude: "N" stands for north and "S" stands for
south. Forty-three degrees and seventeen minutes
south latitude is written 43° S 17'.
Cities and towns are arranged alphabetically in
longitude and latitude tables according to country and
state, or province where applicable
(Meridians of longitude pass through the North and
South Poles as they encircle the Earth. The prime
meridian, 0° longitude, from which all other meridian
lines are measured passes through Greenwich.
England. Lines of latitude are drawn parallel to the
Earth's equator, which is designated 0° latitude.)

Time
Time zone/time changes books give the world
standard time zones and the Standard Time Meridian
(longitude) on which a country or section of a country
bases its clock time. There are twenty-four standard
time zones in the world. Clock time increases one hour
for each 15° longitude east of Greenwich and decreases
one hour for each 15° longitude west of Greenwich.
Planetary positions are listed in reference books
according to Greenwich Mean Time (universal time),
which is standard clock time in Greenwich, England.
Birthtime must be converted to Greenwich Mean Time
(GMT) in order to complete the calculations that are
needed to erect an accurate horoscope.
Standard time zones are designated by a number
and/or a letter of the alphabet. The number assigned
to a time zone indicates the number of hours by which
standard clock time in that particular zone differs from
Greenwich Mean Time. Greenwich is in the zero zone.
A plus sign (+) preceding a time zone number
signifies that the specified number of hours is added
to standard clock time in that zone to equal Greenwich
Mean Time. Time zone hours are added to standard
clock time in the western hemisphere in order to
convert to Greenwich Mean Time because clock time
in places west of Greenwich decreases one hour for
every 15° longitude.
A minus sign (—) preceding a time zone number
indicates that the hour(s) differential is subtracted from
standard clock time in that zone to convert to
Greenwich Mean Time. Time zone hours are
subtracted from clock time in the eastern hemisphere
to convert to Greenwich Mean Time because clock
time increases one hour for each 15° longitude east
of Greenwich.
Letters of the alphabet are sometimes used to
designate time zones. Zero degrees longitude, at which
Greenwich lies, is the Standard Time Meridian for the
"Z" zone; each 15° zone east of Greenwich is lettered
consecutively "A" through "M" with the omission of
zones west of Greenwich are lettered "N" through
"Y" (refer to Figure 12).
Seven standard time zones are in effect in the United
States. The Eastern Standard Time zone (EST) is based
on the Standard Time Meridian at 75° west longitude;

=== Page 105 ===
The Tools of Astrology 121
the Central Standard Time zone (CST) is based on
90° W; the Mountain Standard Time zone (MST) is
based on 105° W; the Pacific Standard Time zone (PST)
is based on 120° W; the Yukon Standard Time zone
(YST), which affects parts of Alaska, is based on
135° W; the Alaska-Hawaii Standard Time zone
(AHST) is based on 150° W, and the Nome Standard
Time zone (NST), which is also in force in parts of
Alaska, is based on the Standard Time Meridian at 120°
west longitude.
If the Standard Time Meridian on which a locality
bases its time is known, the zone number can be
calculated by dividing the longitude of the Standard
Time Meridian by fifteen; a plus sign precedes the zone
number if the longitude of the Standard Time Meridian
is west: a minus sign precedes if the longitude is east.
