contraparallels are entered in the same column
opposite the symbol of the aspected planet. Ascendant
or MC. Parallels and contraparallels formed with the
North Node or Part of Fortune are entered in the same
square as the zodiacal aspects.
Next, enter in the second row and corresponding
column the aspects made by the Moon. Do not enter
a Moon/Sun aspect; it belongs in the first row; no
aspect is entered twice. Complete the tabulation of the
Moon's aspects in the same manner as the Sun's.
Mercury's aspects, except those formed with the Sun
or the Moon, are entered in the third row in the
column headed by the planet Mercury aspects;
parallels and contraparallels are listed in the third
column headed by Mercury in the row which
corresponds to the aspected planet. Venus' aspects are
considered next and so on until all aspects are entered
in the aspectarian.
Basic Significance of the Aspects
Aspects are classed as hard (difficult) or easy (soft).
Hard aspects stimulate action and induce motivation.
Except for the conjunction and parallel, all hard
aspects are disharmonious to some extent depending
upon the strength of the aspect and the natures of the
planets involved. These aspects create tension, friction
or difficulties, which in tum produce activity. The
conjunction and parallel may be harmonious or
disharmonious; either way, they stimulate planetary
energies as do all hard aspects. Easy aspects generate
harmony; they blend planetary energies smoothly and
create conditions of ease and accord. They partially
mitigate difficulties or hardships imposed by
inharmonious aspects and contribute to "good luck."
Planetary action in a horoscope depends largely upon
the aspects formed. The same aspect will not have the
same effect in one horoscope as in another. All relevant
factors, including other aspects, are weighed in
determining the influence a given aspect exerts in a
particular horoscope. In any case, the essential
characteristics of an aspect remain unchanged although
its significance may be modified by other factors.
Conjunction: A major hard aspect, the conjunction
is the most powerful of all aspects. It merges planetary
energies and focuses planetary drives. If the natures
of the two planets in conjunction are in harmony (as
with two benefics), the conjunction unifies and
strengthens planetary influence in a horoscope. If the
planets are naturally discordant (as with a benefic and
a malefic or with two malefics), the conjunction is
disruptive; the stronger planet will overshadow or
distort the weaker planet's influence.
Vigintile: A minor easy aspect, the vigintile is mildly
harmonious but has little effect in a natal horoscope.
Quindecile: A minor easy aspect, the quindecile has
a weak but favorable influence.
Semi-sextile: A minor easy aspect, the semi-sextile is
of some importance in a natal horoscope. The energies
of planets in semi-sextile adapt harmoniously; if these
planets are otherwise afflicted, the semi-sextile may
partially mitigate adverse effects.
Decile: A minor easy aspect, the decile, also called a
semi-quintile, has a harmonious effect although its
influence in the natal horoscope is weak.
Semi-square: A minor hard aspect, the semi-square
ranks as the most influential of the minor aspects. The
semi-square is irritating and creates friction between
the planets in aspect. Mild stress accompanies the
dispersion of planetary energies.
Septile: Probably a hard aspect, the septile is seldom
used. This minor aspect is said to produce an intangible
effect that may have to do with karma or destiny.
Sextile: A major easy aspect, the sextile is considered
helpful and beneficial; it is associated with opportunities
and advantages.
Quintile: A minor easy aspect, the quintile is favorable
although moderately weak.

=== Page 143 ===
Aspects Defined 159
Square: A major hard aspect, the square is the most
dynamic aspect. The square generates tension and
galvanizes action. It produces difficulties and obstacles
that thwart planetary drives, but it also spurs ambition
to overcome such barriers.
Tredecile: A minor easy aspect, the tredecile is harmo-
nious but carries little weight in a natal horoscope.
Trine: A major easy aspect, the trine is the most
propitious and influential easy aspect. The trine is
associated with ease and good fortune. A trine to an
otherwise afflicted planet is extremely helpful in
alleviating the difficulties imposed by adverse aspects.
Sesquiquadrate: A minor hard aspect, the sesqui-
quadrate ranks only slightly lower than the semi-
square in influence. This aspect creates agitation
between planetary energies and gives rise to
aggravation and discord.
Bi-quintile: A minor easy aspect, the bi-quintile has
a moderately harmonious effect; it is of slight signif-
icance in a natal horoscope.
Quincunx: A minor hard aspect, the quincunx
emphasizes the need for adjustment; planetary energies
do not combine harmoniously and their expression is
strained, uncomfortable.
Opposition: A major hard aspect, the opposition is
separative in nature. Planets in polarity present a
challenge as well as an attraction and antagonism
between opposing energies. The opposition is second
only to the conjunction in strength.
Parallel: A major hard aspect, the parallel has a
unifying effect for good or ill depending upon the
nature of the planets involved. A harmonious parallel
reinforces planetary influence; a disharmonious
parallel induces discord and conflict.
Contraparallel: A major hard aspect, the contraparallel
is disruptive; planetary energies are at cross-purposes.
Special Aspect Configurations
Several aspects may combine to form a particular
pattern or configuration. The influence of combined
aspects may alter or extend that of the aspects
considered individually.
Stellium or multiple conjunction: This configuration
is composed of three or more planets that form a series
of conjunctions. Some authorities reserve the term
stellium for those series of conjunctions that occur
within one sign; the term multiple conjunction is then
applied to a series of conjunctions that extend from
one sign into another. The stellium focuses planetary
activity in accordance with the houses and signs
involved. A member of a stellium is influenced by
aspects made to other members of the stellium even
if the orb is too wide to normally include that planet.
This is called aspect by association. Associative aspects
broaden the influence of the initial aspect.
T-square: A T-square is formed when two planets in
opposition both square the same third planet. The
squared planet acts as a focal point for the tension
generated by the planets in opposition; it represents
the means of resolving attendant difficulties and
surmounting the obstacles inherent in this
configuration. A cardinal T-square is one in which
each planet occupies a different sign of the cardinal
quadruplicity; it prompts impatience and urges
decisive, often hasty action, which can create greater
problems than existed initially. A fixed T-square
implies endurance and resistance in the face of
adversity, but it can produce inflexibility, which
inhibits progress. A mutable T-square gives more
leeway. The easiest course may be to try to avoid or
ignore difficulties, but such action does nothing to
resolve them. T-squares create conflict but they also
spark ambition. A dissociate T-square (one that
contains signs belonging to mixed quadruplicities) does
not carry the impact that a cardinal, fixed or mutable
T-square wields. The symbol for a T-square is "T";
the crossbar denotes the opposition and the vertical
line indicates the planet, which is square to both ends
of the opposition.
Grand square or grand cross: This configuration
consists of four squares and two oppositions and
contains at least one planet in each member of the same
quadruplicity. This formation differs from that of the
T-square with the addition of another planet placed
opposite the "squared" planet. The extreme tension
produced by the grand square creates a state of
constant struggle and crisis. The affairs of the planets
and houses involved undergo continuous upheaval;
difficulties are consistent with the occupied

=== Page 144 ===
160 Compendium of Astrology
quadruplicity. There is no focal planet in this
configuration; each planet is under stress. The planet
in the grand square that forms the largest number of
favorable aspects with other planets is the key to
partial resolution of problems. A trine or sextile is
extremely helpful here. A dissociate (mixed) grand
square signifies conflict as described by the individual
aspects, but it is not as difficult as a cardinal, fixed
or mutable grand square. The symbol for the grand
square is "Kl." Each corner of the square represents
a squared planet; the X signifies the two oppositions.
Grand trine: This configuration is formed when three
planets that occupy different signs of the same triplicity
form mutual trines. A most fortunate combination,
it indicates ease and a smooth flow of planetary
energies. A grand trine does much to alleviate the
strain produced by adverse aspects. The affairs of the
planets and houses that are affected by the grand trine
bring benefits and pleasure. A grand trine that is placed
in fire signs confers inspiration and creativity; an earth
grand trine is associated with material blessings; an
air grand trine enriches intellectual expression and
mental development; a water grand trine stresses
compassion, receptivity and responsiveness. A grand
trine composed of mixed elements (dissociate) lacks
cohesiveness; nonetheless, three trines in a horoscope
are certainly advantageous. The symbol for a grand
trine is "A"; the element (triplicity) is noted in the
center of the triangle.
Yod: A yod occurs when two planets in sextile both
form a quincunx with the same third planet. The planet
that is in quincunx with the other two represents the
action point of the yod; the point directly opposite
in the zodiac is the reaction point. The reaction point
will be at or near the midpoint of the two planets in
sextile. Planetary action induced at the action point
produces consequences at the reaction point; the effect
influences all three planets as well as the affairs of the
house that contains the reaction point. The yod has
a karmic connotation; the action point represents
cause, the reaction point shows effect. The yod is
associated with circumstances not of one's own
making; one shapes his or her destiny in the affected
areas according to how such conditions are met. The
symbol for the yod is 'Y.' The arms of the Y represent
the planets in sextile; the vertical line indicates the
planet to which the other two are quincunx.
Aspect Lines
Lines that connect planets in aspect may be drawn on
the face of the horoscope to give a visual represen-
tation of the aspects and aspect configurations. Major
aspects may be indicated by a solid line, minor aspects
by a broken line. It is easy to spot the various aspects
if a different color is used for each. Conjunctions,
parallels and contraparallels are not usually indicated
by lines. Nor are aspect lines drawn to the angles.
Nodes or the Part of Fortune. Aspect lines permit one
to see at a glance which planets are well aspected and
which are afflicted and to readily identify special
aspect configurations.
Midpoints
Sensitive degrees in a horoscope, called midpoints, are
usually calculated along with aspects. A direct
midpoint is that point in the zodiac and in the
horoscope lying exactly midway between two planets.
When aspected by a third planet it describes by house
and sign position a common focus of interest, which
links the three planets as indicated by the aspect. There
are two such points for each pair of planets. For
example, 10° Virgo is a midpoint of Venus at 10° Leo
and Jupiter at 10° Libra; the opposite degree and other
direct midpoint, 10° Pisces, also lies midway between
the two planets. Planets that aspect these midpoints
(within 1° orb) influence both Venus and Jupiter,
although not as strongly as if in direct aspect with the
planets themselves. The conjunction, the most
influential midpoint aspect, provides a direct channel
for release of the energies of all three planets involved.
Any point in a horoscope that forms an angle of 45°,
90° or 135° (semi-square, squareor sesquiquadrate) with
a direct midpoint is an indirect midpoint. Aspects to these
points give clues to subtle relationships among planets.
Indirect midpoints are frequently omitted in a natal
horoscope. They are, however, useful in determining
future trends and events, as are direct midpoints.
Potentials described in the natal horoscope often
manifest when a progressed or transiting planet comes
to the degree occupied by a midpoint (conjuncts the
midpoint). Midpoint conjunctions are most significant
when the two planets involved form a natal aspect,
as in the Venus/Jupiter example above (Venus sextile
Jupiter). A progressed or transiting planet that

=== Page 145 ===
conjuncts the midpoint of two planets in aspect natally
prompts an outward function of the natal aspect. A
progressed or transiting conjunction to a midpoint of
two planets not in aspect natally sets the stage for
events, but activation depends upon reinforcement by
planetary aspects (natal or progressed).
For clarity, midpoints, also called half-sums, are
listed in zodiacal sequence rather than entered in the
horoscope; they are written in the following style:

When calculations for midpoints and aspects are
completed, the horoscope is ready for study and
delineation.

Methodology
Delineation of a horoscope involves more than
interpretation of astrological factors. A horoscope
contains a wealth of information and the key to
delineation lies in synthesizing the various components
into a cohesive whole. Some items of information may
seem to conflict with others. It is up to the astrologer
to analyze and weigh the data, to correlate the findings
and to place the proper emphasis on each astrological
fact. If apparently contradictory findings appear, the
astrologer must first determine if the deductions are
valid from an astrological point of view. If no error
is discovered, the astrologer must decide whether one
piece of data outweighs the other in influence or if the
items represent a point of major conflict in the
character or life of the individual.
Bear in mind that the planets energize the horoscope,
the signs color the expression of planetary energies,
the houses denote the direction of these energies and
aspects qualify planetary energies and direct planetary
influence throughout various parts of the horoscope.
No single component of the horoscope can be isolated
from the others.
With practice, every astrologer develops the
particular system of organizing data that is most
natural for him or her. The beginner usually makes
comprehensive notes based on each of the astrological
factors and the corresponding deductions (interpre-
tations). One method is to list interpretational notes
under specific categories that correspond to the areas
of life described in the horoscope. A piece of
astrological information that applies to more than one
area of life is entered under each applicable category
and interpreted accordingly. Each astrological factor
is listed beside the corresponding deduction(s). This
procedure serves as a check against omissions and
other mistakes and enables one to verify the findings.
It is simplest to jot down interpretational notes on large
index cards or in a loose-leaf notebook, reserving one
card or one page for each category. It is an easy matter
to insert additional cards or pages as needed for lengthy
categories. Suggested categories include physical
characteristics, intellectual aptitudes and interests,
emotional qualities, career potential, financial prospects,
romance, marital outlook, family life, children,
friendship, social interests, hobbies, health and miscel-
laneous activities. Other categories may be added or
some combined to suit the individual horoscope.
Obvious characteristics of a horoscope may be
noted on the chart form for easy reference. Where
applicable, deductions based on these characteristics
are entered in the interpretational notes under the
correct category; then each element of the horoscope
is studied in detail. The following procedure assures
that no important points are overlooked.
1. Consider the general planetary distribution in the
horoscope.
(a) Note the number of planets which lie east and
west of the MC-1C axis and the number which
lie north and south of the Ascendant-
Descendant axis. In the interpretational notes
enter a general observation based upon hemi-
spheric and quadrant emphasis.
(b) Identify the shaping pattern of the horoscope.
Base the identification on the distribution of
planets only; disregard the Nodes and Part of

=== Page 148 ===
166 Compendium of Astrology
Fortune. Enter a corresponding deduction in
the interpretational notes.
2. Consider planetary distribution among the signs.
(a) List the number of planets in each triplicity;
enter in the interpretational notes a deduction
concerning the general characteristics of the
individual based upon the most heavily occu-
pied triplicity. If the same number of planets
occupy more than one triplicity, and these
triplicities are the most heavily populated,
consider the sign on the Ascendant as a
deciding factor. If the Ascending sign does not
belong to one of the triplicities of interest, use
the sign on the MC. If it is unsuitable and the
Sun sign belongs to one of the dominant
triplicities, give emphasis to that triplicity. If
no deciding factor is found, give equal weight
to the most heavily occupied triplicities. Do
not count the Nodes or Part of Fortune.
(b) List the number of planets in each quadrupli-
city and enter a deduction based on the
dominant quadruplicity. In case of an equal
distribution, use the above sequence to
determine dominance.
(c) List the number of planets in positive and
negative signs; enter a deduction based on
positive/negative emphasis. Equal distribution
denotes balance between dynamic and passive
qualities.
3. Consider planetary distribution in the houses.
(a) Enter a deduction based on house distribution
according to angular, succedent and cadent
house emphasis.
(b) Enter a deduction based on planetary domi-
nance in the individual, temporal, relative and
terminal houses.
4. As a reminder when determining planetary
influence in the horoscope, note on the chart form
all planetary dignities, debilities and mutual
receptions. Also note the chart ruler (the planetary
ruler of the sign on the Ascendant).
5. In the interpretational notes, enter a general
observation based on the final dispositor or a circle
of dispositors if either exists.
6. Note any special aspect configurations. Interpret.
7. From the aspectarian, determine if about half of
all major zodiacal aspects are of one particular
kind (conjunction, sextile, etc.). Do not include
the parallel or contraparallel in the count. These
are not zodiacal aspects; they are based on
declination. Note the general influence of the type
of aspect that is in the majority. Conjunction
emphasis lends the power of unification to
planetary drives; conditions that permit the
focusing of energies and encourage the merging
of interests are indicated; activity is expressed with
and through other people. A majority of sextiles
signifies opportune circumstances that foster
productive use of energies and enable one to
handle the affairs of life to best advantage. Square
emphasis stimulates ambition; the individual must
rise to the challenge of obstacles and trying
conditions or be defeated by adversities. Trine
emphasis denotes harmonious conditions that
allow one's affairs to flow smoothly; the rewards
of life come easily and abundantly to the
individual. A predominance of oppositions gives
the individual a sharp awareness of the polarities
and contrasts in life; conflicting conditions and
opposing interests force the individual to
adequately balance internal and external affairs.
8. Note any planet that has no major or minor
aspect. An unaspected planet has no effective
outlet. Its influence is limited and weakened
because its energy is not integrated in the
horoscope and, therefore, corresponding drives
are not integrated in the totality of the person.
9. Note the position of the prenatal eclipse.
10. Note the event if a solar or lunar eclipse occurred
on the birthdate.
11. Interpret and record the meaning of the sign on
the cusp of the first house (the Ascendant) and any
sign intercepted within the house. Interpret
according to sign and house position the planet(s)
that occupies the first house, the planet(s) that
rules the sign on the cusp and the planet(s) that
rules a sign intercepted within the house. Interpret
the aspects that these planets form. Study the
natural ruler(s) of the house and any planets that
occupy the natural sign of the house to determine
the influence these planets exert in this house.
Repeat the same procedure for each house in the
horoscope. Include interpretation of the Nodes
and Part of Fortune, and evaluation of the Vertex,
East Point and eclipse effects.

=== Page 149 ===
Methodology 167
When interpreting sign positions, consider the
decanate, duad and degree (anaretic, critical, nodal
or fixed star).
In judging a planet's strength, evaluate its standing
in the horoscope according to the guidelines given in
Chapter 3. When determining the emphasis of
planetary action, consider the effect of the planet's
motion (direct, retrograde or stationary). Study a
planet's total sphere of influence, which includes the
characteristics, drives and affairs naturally governed
by the planet: the affairs of the house it rules and
occupies in the horoscope, the affairs of its natural
house; the affairs associated with the sign in which
it is placed; and the natural affairs of the houses that
are ruled and occupied by the planet(s) it aspects.
Weigh a planet's influence in each area in light of the
influence other planets exert in the same area.
An aspect's influence is weighed in terms of the other
aspects formed by the same two planets with other
planets in the horoscope. An aspect that forms part of
a special configuration is interpreted accordingly. The
aspect meanings given in Chapters 16 through 26 are to
be interpreted in relation to the affairs or characteristics
the aspects influence. Consider whether the aspect is
approaching or departing, applying or separating.
The house of the prenatal eclipse is emphasized; the
eclipse event must be considered in the interpretation
of the astrological factors that influence this house.
If a natal solar or lunar eclipse occurred on the
birthdate, the effects of the eclipse are taken into
account in the interpretation of the eclipsed luminary.
An alternate order of procedure that may be
substituted in Step 11 follows. Instead of methodically
studying the astrological factors that influence each
house, one organizes the interpretation around the
planets. Beginning with the Sun or chart ruler, each
planet's sign and house position are interpreted. Its
aspects are interpreted, its influence in the house it rules
in the horoscope and the signs associated with that house
are interpreted, and its influence in its natural house is
noted. Lastly, the Nodes, Part of Fortune, Vertex and
East Point are interpreted. With either procedure all the
information contained in the horoscope is transferred
to the interpretational notes and arranged systematically
under the various categories.
After all astrological factors are interpreted and
listed in appropriate categories, findings are analyzed
objectively as they relate to specific areas of life. As
the interpretational notes are reviewed, the same
notation will probably be discovered beside different
astrological factors, and this is as it should be. More
than one indication is needed to confirm a given point.
It is usually easier for the beginner to write the final
analysis of a horoscope rather than to give it verbally
in person or on tape. Before writing or giving an oral
report, it is wise to make an outline that covers all
areas of life. The information contained in the
interpretational notes can then be easily condensed
into a readable or listenable form that is coherent
and complete.
Delineation Exercise: The First House
The general characteristics of a horoscope, noted in
Steps 1 through 10, are incorporated, as applicable,
in the analysis of the four major features: planets,
signs, houses and aspects.
Susan's Ascendant (refer to Susan's horoscope.
Chapter 13, Figure 18), 23049' Taurus, is in the
Capricorn (third) decanate of Taurus, ruled by Venus
and sub-ruled by Saturn, and the Aquarius (tenth)
duad, sub-ruled by Uranus and Saturn. Saturn is
relatively strong in the chart, exalted (in Libra), in a
critical degree (0° of a cardinal sign) and fairly well
aspected (a sextile, square, trine, quincunx and
quintile). It emphasizes the materialistic qualities of
Taurus, reinforces worldly ambition and adds a
serious aspect to the personality as Ascendant sub-
ruler (decanate and duad).
Uranian influence (tenth duad) introduces
progressive attitudes and behavior that is more
unconventional than is characteristic of either Taurus
or Capricorn (decan). Aquarian tendencies are more
pronounced than one would normally expect from
duad influence because the Sun is in the Aquarius
(third) duad of Sagittarius, and Uranus, disposited by
the Moon, is the leading planet in a Locomotive (the
shaping of the horoscope), which indicates sell-
motivation and dynamic action (refer to Chapter Q).
As the leading planet in the second house, Uranus
indicates that Susan is materially-oriented as well as
goal-oriented (leading planet of Locomotive and ruler
of the tenth house, Aquarius on the MC) supporting
indications described by the Ascending sign. Uranus,
as leading planet, also shows thai she is motivated by
a drive for progress and change, a desire for emotional

second house influence, financial inconsistencies (refer
to Chapters 3, 4, 7, 8 and 17).
The square between Satum and Uranus, the sub-

Cardinal influence in the Ascendant (Capricorn

Zodiacal aspects are about evenly divided between

Modal house distribution, fairly well balanced, places

Because Aries is the cardinal/fire sign, the

Venus, chart ruler (Ascendant ruler), placed in the

Rather weak ties link Venus with its dispositor,

Jupiterian influence promotes broader interests than

Venus is accidentally dignified in the seventh house,

With both the chart ruler and the Sun placed in the

The trines (applying, see Chapter 14) mitigate

The only other major Venus aspect, a contraparallel
with Pluto in combination with the Pluto/Ascendant

refined taste associated with Venus as Ascendant ruler
and indicates discord in seventh house relationships
(Pluto rules Scorpio, which appears on the cusp).
The one minor Venus aspect, the quintile to Satum,

because Saturn sub-rules the decanate and duad

Venus aspects, examined narrowly as they apply to
the first house, have a broader connotation in terms

it rules, the sixth house, which it also rules in Susan's

tied to the first house and all that Venus and the Sun
govern and aspect in the horoscope.
Aspects to the Ascendant as well as those to the ruler
of the Ascendant are considered in analyzing first

major aspect with the Ascendant (within a 5° orb).
The North Node forms a sextile (South Node a trine)
and the Part of Fortune a trine with the Ascendant

Of the three minor aspects that planets form with

The Moon/Ascendant quintile reinforces the

The Mercury/Ascendant quincunx implies a need

quincunx has little significance unless other Mercury
aspects or related factors give added weight.
Through rulerships, dispositorships and aspects, the

An astrologer who establishes a good rapport with
clients and earns their trust will find that clients return
again and again for consultations, for astrology does
not stop with the natal chart; that is merely the
beginning. Potentials in the natal chart are brought
to life when they are activated by progressed and
transiting planets. The dynamics of the natal chart in

Counseling
Astrology reveals a person's strengths, weaknesses and
potentials. It points out the mode of approach or focus
best suited to the individual as the means of over-
coming obstacles and making the best possible use of
his or her potentials in each area of life. It neither
condemns nor sanctions a particular way of life. In
translating the symbolism of the horoscope into
language meaningful to the client, the astrologer deals
with astrological facts. It is not the function of the
astrologer to make moral judgments; personal views
and standards are not acceptable in delineation.
Many clients tend to develop close ties with their
astrologers, whom they regard as confidants and friends.
It is difficult at times for an astrologer not to exert
personal influence, unwittingly perhaps, when a troubled
client inquires about a specific course of action.
However, an astrologer's advice is correctly limited to
pointing out all ramifications evident in the horoscope
that pertain to the inquiry. The choice to act or not and
in what direction rests with the client. The astrologer is
ethically bound to protect confidences revealed in
consultations, to honor the client's trust and to counsel
as objectively and honestly as humanly possible.

Sun Aspects
The interpretation of a particular aspect depends
upon the basic significance of the aspect, the nature
of the planets that form the aspect, the signs that these
planets occupy, and the houses and affairs that come
under the influence of the planets in aspect. The
interpretations given in the text must be modified
according to sign expression and adapted to the
affairs governed by the planets in aspect. An
aspect's influence may be qualified by other aspects
to the same planet; however, one aspect does not
cancel out another aspect. For example, a trine or
sextile to an afflicted planet may ease the discomfort
associated with difficulties or enable one to cope more
readily with difficulties, but it will not prevent
difficulties from arising.
Sun Conjunctions
A person's life force and the drive for self-expression
are brought into focus by the energies of planets in
conjunction with the Sun. In the final analysis, the
effect of a conjunction depends largely upon the
aspects made to the conjunction by other planets. A
conjunction which has an orb of 30' or less is termed
cazimi. The energy of a planet which lies so close to
the Sun is thought to be "burnt up" by the heat of the
Sun. A planet which forms a cazimi conjunction with
the Sun has no identity of its own; its principles-are
engulfed by the ego. A conjunction whose orb is
between 31' and 3° is called combust. A combusted
planet does not operate independently of the Sun; its
energy is integrated with that of the Sun. Except when
it forms a cazimi or combust conjunction, the Sun
vitalizes any planet it aspects. A cazimi or combust
conjunction weakens a planet, but it gives greater force
to the Sun's drives.
Sun Conjunct Moon: This aspect unites the ego and the
emotions. The drive for achievement is closely allied with
instinctual urges. Self-satisfaction is increased because
the drive for self-expression is in harmony with the
emotions. Whether or not one's actions are correct, the
individual suffers little guilt or remorse unless other
factors in the horoscope indicate differently; this person
feels that what he or she does is right. The new Moon
(Sun/Moon conjunction) strengthens self-motivation
directed toward the affairs ruled by the Sun and Moon
within the context of sign expression. The individual
identifies with the home and views the parents as a unit.
If the conjunction is afflicted, tendencies toward self-
centeredness and lack of conscience are intensified.
Emotional disturbances, if they occur, deplete vitality
and can, therefore, adversely affect physical well-being.
Sun Conjunct Mercury: Since Mercury is never more
than 28° apart from the Sun, the conjunction is the
only major zodiacal aspect that can occur between
these two planets. This conjunction strengthens the
will to act on ideas. The individual does not merely
think over or talk about plans, but gives concrete
expression to ideas through action. This aspect restricts
self-objectivity; one fails to recognize shortcomings
and character flaws because the ego influences thought
patterns. If the conjunction is afflicted, willfulness and
egotism are increased. The individual is inclined to be
nervous and may lack good motor coordination.

Sun Sextiles
Sun sextiles indicate opportune avenues of self-

They enable one to bypass, overcome or find the

Sun Squares
Sun squares block creative self-expression in the areas
of horoscope influence and create obstacles that hinder
the individual's drive to achieve. They indicate ego-
frustrating experiences and produce stress, which can
be harmful to one's health.
Sun Square Moon: This square generates much inner
tension. The individual derives little emotional satis-
faction from personal achievements. Discontentment
and emotional frustration hinder natural self-expression.
Self-consciousness creates strained relations with the
public in general and with members of the opposite sex
in particular. Parental conflicts during childhood color
the individual's adult attitudes toward home and family.
Sun Square Mars: This aspect unleashes the passion
of Mars and the vitality of the Sun. Much hardship
is created through impulsive actions, many of which
are motivated by arrogance or anger. A favorable
aspect to Satum from either the Sun or Mars will do
much to stabilize the unrestrained energy and ambition

a hot temper, pugnacity, argumentativeness, extreme
competitiveness and, if other aspects confirm, an
inclination toward cruelty and violence.
Sun Square Jupiter: This square produces conceit, self-

Sun Square Satum: This aspect severely restricts the

Trying circumstances and heavy responsibilities

resistance to disease are impaired.
Sun Square Uranus: This aspect brings out rebellious

Sun Oppositions
Sun oppositions bring conflicts of will into play.
Interests that are influenced by a Sun opposition are
thrown into prominence. The individual is challenged

Sun Opposite Moon: This opposition creates emotional

and vitality. The individual is cold, insecure, withdrawn
and ultra-conservative. Low self-esteem and lack of
physical vigor are typical of this aspect.
Sun Opposite Uranus: This aspect indicates sudden
breaks and unexpected disruptions in the affairs
influenced by the Sun and Uranus. The individual is
willful, independent and insistent. Dictatorial
inclinations evoke much opposition and controversy.
Self-expression is abrupt, uncoordinated and
incongruous. This opposition generates much nervous
tension: the individual is high-strung and excitable.
Sun Opposite Neptune: This opposition introduces
confusion and chaos into the areas governed by the
Sun and Neptune. Many of these people are deluded
by a false sense of well-being and misplaced trust; they
may be the victims or the perpetrators of subterfuge
and deceit. Self-expression is unrealistic and muddled.
This aspect generates negative psychic energy and
warns against contact with the spiritual world as well
as misuse of drugs or alcohol.
Sun Opposite Pluto: This aspect produces an
unrelentless drive for power. The individual strives
for absolute domination and control in the affairs
influenced by the Sun and Pluto. Self-expression is
forceful, coercive and demanding. The tension
generated by this aspect creates an invisible aura of
formidable force, an aura that inexplicably frightens
or intimidates many of the people who come into
contact with the individual. This aspect is associated
with the autocrat or despot.
Sun Opposite North Node Conjunct South Node:
These aspects emphasize the need to overcome selfish
tendencies and egocentric attitudes, which inhibit
growth. Self-development depends largely upon the
individual's capacity to reach out and cooperate with
others in areas indicated by the North Node. Eclipse
action near the birthdate is suggested by this
configuration: such action should be verified and
interpreted if applicable to the horoscope.
Sun Opposite Part of fortune: This opposition
indicates self-interests, which hinder the success
promised by the Part of Fortune. It places the indi-
vidual at a disadvantage in the affairs influenced by
the opposition.
Sun Opposite Ascendant Conjunct Descendant: These
aspects emphasize marriage, partnerships and
coordinated activities over those endeavors that are
primarily self-oriented. These people exert leadership
and influence in their associations.
Sun Opposite MC Conjunct IC. These aspects imply
that a harmonious and productive family life is
essential to the individual's progress in the world.
Without a satisfying home life, this person does not
function at full capability. The extent of worldly
attainments hinges upon one's capacity to establish the
kind of home life that fulfills individual needs.
Sun Parallels
Parallels that occur between planets that also form a
zodiacal aspect assume the tenor of the zodiacal aspect;
these parallels strengthen the influence of the zodiacal
aspect. For example, a parallel acts in a manner similar
to that of a conjunction and when formed between two
planets in trine gives added force to the trine. If a parallel
occurs between two planets in square, the stress induced
by the square is greatly magnified by the parallel. A
parallel that occurs between two planets that
simultaneously form a minor zodiacal aspect elevates the
minor aspect to the status of a major aspect.
Parallels that are unaccompanied by a zodiacal
aspect are given the same general meaning as that of
a conjunction. However, because parallels can occur
between planets that are widely separated by sign
and house, the influence of a parallel that stands alone
is not as focused as that of a conjunction. An
unaccompanied parallel exerts less impact and is
interpreted more broadly than a conjunction.
The meaning of a conjunction may be modified, as
it applies to an unaccompanied parallel, by the
signs that the planets in parallel occupy. Planets that
are mutually friendly form a harmonious parallel
regardless of sign position. Planets in parallel that are
naturally neutral or antagonistic toward each other
operate smoothly when they occupy different signs of
the same triplicity. Neutral or antagonistic planets in
parallel react favorably if one is in an air sign and the
other is in a fire sign, it these signs do not oppose,

=== Page 160 ===
178 Compendium of Astrology
the same is true if one planet occupies an earth sign
and the other a water sign, if the signs are not in
polarity. The effect is discordant when neutral or
antagonistic planets, which occupy different signs of
the same quadruplicity, form a parallel. If planets in
parallel occupy the same sign but are not within orb
of a conjunction, the parallel takes on the full character
and influence of a conjunction.
Sun parallels unify the creative life force of the Sun
with the drives that are basic to the planet(s) in
parallel. If a zodiacal aspect exists between the Sun
and a planet in parallel with the Sun, strong willpower
and ambition are expressed according to the influence
of the zodiacal aspect. The interpretation for this
parallel corresponds to the meaning of the zodiacal
aspect; the combined aspects are given greater weight
in the horoscope than single aspects of the same type.
If no zodiacal aspect is formed between the Sun and
a planet in parallel with the Sun, the parallel is
interpreted as a Sun conjunction with some modifi-
cations. Except for parallels with Mercury or Venus,
the effect of a Sun parallel is milder than that of any
major zodiacal aspect the Sun forms. As with all
aspects, the influence extends to the houses and affairs
governed by both planets. The natural emphasis of
a corresponding Sun conjunction may be qualified by
the relationship (harmonious or discordant) that exists
between the Sun sign and the sign occupied by a planet
in parallel. In addition, the following ideas are to be
considered when adapting the interpretation of a Sun
conjunction to a Sun parallel that stands alone.
Sun Parallel Moon: This parallel permits emotional
drives to constructively support creative self-expression.
It does not give the emotional harmony and self-
satisfaction that a Sun/Moon conjunction describes
unless the luminaries occupy compatible signs.
Sun Parallel Mercury: This aspect merges willpower
and mental energy; it bears equal strength with that
of a Sun/Mercury conjunction regardless of sign
positions.
Sun Parallel Venus: This parallel is given the same
meaning and power as a Sun/Venus conjunction
except that it does not carry the connotation of
possible male effeminacy.
Sun Parallel Mars: This aspect takes on the emphasis
of an unafflicted conjunction when the Sun and Mars
are in harmonious signs. If neither planet is afflicted,
the parallel is interpreted as a mildly favorable
conjunction even if the planets occupy uncongenial
signs. If either the Sun or Mars forms major adverse
aspects with other planets, and they are in discordant
signs, the parallel is interpreted as an afflicted
conjunction.
Sun Parallel Jupiter: This aspect has the same
significance as a favorable Sun/Jupiter conjunction
except the effect is milder.
Sun Parallel Saturn: The emphasis of this parallel
depends upon whether or not the signs occupied by
the Sun and Saturn are harmonious.
Sun Parallel Uranus: In this aspect the energies of the
Sun and Uranus do not blend compatibly unless the
planets occupy harmonious signs.
Sun Parallel Neptune: This parallel carries a positive
or negative influence according to sign harmony or
discord.
Sun Parallel Pluto: This aspect is not as potent as a
Sun/Pluto conjunction; nevertheless, it increases the
power potential of the individual, and, if sign place-
ments agree, gives greater capacity to control that
power.
Sun Parallel North Node: This parallel has a slightly
different orientation than a Sun/North Node conjunc-
tion. Although the individual's attention is directed
toward channels of self-development as with the
conjunction, this person may not recognize or want
to improve restrictive habits, which hinder growth.
Sun Parallel Part of Fortune; This aspect is as favorable
as a Sun/Part of Fortune conjunction. Sign relationships
have no bearing on the emphasis of this parallel.
Sun Parallel Ascendant: This aspect has a very
personal connotation. It is harmonious and
constructive regardless of the signs involved.
Sun Parallel MC: This parallel intensifies one's worldly
ambitions and promotes the desire to succeed; it

provides a direct link between creative self-expression
and achievement.
Sun Contraparallels
Except for contraparallels formed with Mercury or
Venus, Sun contraparallels carry less weight in the
horoscope than the major zodiacal aspects; they are
equal to Sun parallels in strength. A Sun contra-
parallel generates conflict between the drives of the
Sun and the energies of the planet in aspect. The Sun
and a contraparalleled planet operate at cross-
purposes. The meaning of a Sun contraparallel formed
with the Ascendant or MC corresponds to that of an
afflicted conjunction. Other Sun contraparallels are
treated as Sun oppositions; however, Sun contra-
parallels are not as challenging as oppositions and
create slightly less tension.
A Sun contraparallel that occurs with Mercury or
Venus is as influential as a Sun/Mercury or Sun/Venus
conjunction, but the influence is separative in nature
rather than unifying.
Sun Contraparallel Mercury: This contraparallel
fosters ill-planned actions in relation to the affairs ruled
by the Sun and Mercury. Depending upon the nature
of the signs that the Sun and Mercury occupy, the
individual may implement plans without adequate
forethought, or may hesitate so long that action comes
too late. Fire and air signs indicate haste; earth and
water signs denote slower action.
Sun Contraparallel Venus: This aspect encourages self-
gratification and preoccupation with creature
comforts. The individual is inclined to be lax about
the affairs influenced by the Sun and Venus. The desire
for luxurious living is in conflict with the urge to
achieve. If other astrological factors confirm, pleasure-
seeking can become a way of life.
Minor Sun Aspects
It is customary to include the semi-sextile, semi-square,
sesquiquadrate and the quincunx in the interpretation
of a natal horoscope. The use of other minor aspects
is a matter of the astrologer's choice.
The semi-square, sesquiquadrate and quincunx, all
minor hard aspects, are considered stronger than the
semi-sextile, a minor easy aspect.
Minor Easy Aspects Formed by the Sun: A minor easy
aspect, which is formed between the Sun and another
planet, supports positive characteristics of both planets.
These qualities blend in a harmonious fashion in
accordance with the aspect's basic significance (Chapter
14) and supplement the creative self-expression and
vitality of the Sun. Make a determination based on the
nature of the Sun and the planet in aspect, the signs these
planets occupy and the meaning of the aspect. Apply
these findings to the houses and affairs influenced by
the Sun and the planet in aspect. Consider the compar-
atively weak influence the minor aspect bears in relation
to other astrological factors in the horoscope. As a guide
to interpreting a minor easy Sun aspect, read the
meaning for a Sun sextile and a Sun trine. A minoreasy
aspect does not confer the easy flow of expression that
is associated with a trine nor does it denote the
opportunities and advantages signified by a sextile.
However, a minor easy aspect does generate other
similar favorable characteristics, although the effect is
much less pronounced.
Minor Hard Aspects Formed by the Sun: A minor hard
aspect, which occurs between the Sun and another
planet, brings out minor discordancies in the natures
of the two planets. Such an aspect indicates friction,
which irritates self-expression. To interpret a minor
hard Sun aspect, consider discordant characteristics
of the two planets in aspect and the basic significance
of the aspect. Determine the manner in which friction
is produced and decide to what extent irritation or
stress is generated. Include the Sun sign and the sign
the planet in aspect occupies in the determination.
Friction and irritation will manifest in the houses and
affairs governed by the Sun and the planet in aspect.

Moon Aspects
The Moon is receptive: it assumes characteristics of
the sign it occupies and of the planets it aspects. Moon
aspects have a decided bearing upon one's emotional
nature and instinctive responses. How a person reacts
to situations and conditions encountered is described
by the Moon aspects. They also indicate how one
relates to other people, women in particular.
Moon Conjunction
Moon conjunctions have a strong impact on the
emotions. Emotional considerations have a
pronounced influence in the affairs governed by the
Moon and a planet it conjuncts.
Moon Conjunct Mercury: This conjunction unites two
receptive planets; neither acts without the other.
Feelings color reason, and logic influences the
emotions. If the conjunction is in a water sign, one's
moods and emotions tend to override intellectual
considerations; if the conjunction is in an air sign and
not severely afflicted, the individual retains
objectivity; a fire sign indicates impulsive emotions
and impetuous decisions; an earth sign gives more
stability to emotional and intellectual expression. A
mixed conjunction permits a broader scope of
emotional and mental expression because each sign
introduces a different mode of expression. The
conjunction describes a person who is extremely
sensitive because the subconscious and conscious
minds function as one. If unafflicted, it indicates a
good memory and strong powers of recall. If the
conjunction is afflicted, the individual is restless.
overly sensitive to criticism, tends to talk excessively
and to gossip.
Moon Conjunct Venus: This aspect, if unafflicted,
brings out the pleasing qualities in one's personality;
it denotes charm, grace and sociability. This person
is an affectionate individual who feels emotionally
unfulfilled without love. He or she gets along well with
other people and especially enjoys the company of
women. A love of beauty and material comforts is
fostered by this conjunction. It indicates refined tastes
and artistic instincts. Memories of childhood and the
parental home are pleasant; family ties are
affectionate. If the conjunction is afflicted, narcissism,
sensuality, voluptuousness and eroticism are implied.
Moon Conjunct Mars: This conjunction energizes the
emotions. Emotional expression is characterized by
Martian qualities. This aspect produces aggressiveness,
masculinity, courage and intense feelings. Much
energy is directed toward the home and family and
the affairs influenced by the conjunction. If the
conjunction is afflicted, an uncontrollable temper,
vindictive anger and explosive emotions are indicated.
Quarrels and strife disrupt domestic life and the affairs
governed by the Moon and Mars.
Moon Conjunct Jupiter: This aspect gives positive
emotional expression as signified by sign position. The
individual is good-natured, jocular, sympathetic and
generous. One benefits from contacts with the public
and is protected from public censure. Women are
helpful to the individual and vice versa. Domestic
interests are safeguarded as are the other interests

affected by the conjunction. If the conjunction is
afflicted, the individual is inclined to be overly
generous and vulnerable to emotional pleas. Digestive
disturbances and stomach ailments can occur as a
result of dietary excesses.
Moon Conjunct Saturn: This conjunction controls and
suppresses the emotions. Emotional expression is
inhibited and restrained. The individual feels aloof
from the public. Relations with women lack warmth.
Home life is disciplined as are other affairs influenced
by the conjunction. If the conjunction is afflicted, the
individual tends to be morose, melancholy, austere

to overcome emotional depression. Because the rates
of motion of the progressed Moon and transiting

Moon Conjunct Uranus: This aspect prompts abrupt
changes in moods; emotional reactions are unpre-
dictable and erratic. The individual craves emotional
excitement. If it is unafflicted, this conjunction confers
intuitive foresight and a good sense of timing. This
person shows an aversion for conformity, which is
manifested in the affairs governed by the Moon and
Uranus. Domestic arrangements are suited to the
individual's unique lifestyle and tastes. If the
conjunction is afflicted, emotional instability and
nervous disorders may occur.
Moon Conjunct Neptune: This conjunction implies
spiritual attunement; it heightens emotional sensitivity
and psychic awareness. The individual tends to pick
up the emotional coloring of the environment and is
receptive to the moods and feelings of others.
Sympathetic and self-sacrificing, one is deeply touched
by the sorrows others experience. The aspect also

is very intuitive about the affairs influenced by the
Moon and Neptune. If the conjunction is afflicted, the
inclination to withdraw from the world is present;
escapism can take the form of isolation, fantasy or the
use of drugs or alcohol.
Moon Conjunct Pluto: This aspect generates powerful
emotions. The individual instinctively senses weakness
in another and subconsciously brings emotional
pressure to bear as a means of attaining control. This
person desires to dominate the home and the affairs
influenced by the conjunction. In a male horoscope
this aspect indicates domination of women. If the
conjunction is afflicted and other factors in the
horoscope confirm, sadistic tendencies can manifest.
Moon Conjunct North Node Opposite South Node:
These aspects show that a lunar or solar eclipse occurred
near the birthdate. If the eclipse is a natal or prenatal
eclipse, the interpretation is emphasized accordingly.
These aspects enable one to instinctively adapt to trends
associated with the affairs influenced by the Moon and
North Node. Even if the Moon and North Node occupy
a fixed sign, this person is subconsciously aware of
prevailing conditions and has the capacity to utilize those
conditions advantageously; it is through such action that
the individual can outgrow the limitations signified by
the South Node.
Moon Conjunct Part of Fortune: This conjunction
describes an individual who derives much emotional
satisfaction from the successes achieved in the affairs
influenced by the conjunction.
Moon Conjunct Ascendant Opposite Descendant:
These aspects give the ability to project the personality
in a manner that is pleasing to the public if the
Moon/Ascendant conjunction is not afflicted. Unless
contrary factors indicate otherwise, the individual is
receptive and responsive. This person is changeable
and moody. Appearance and mannerisms reflect lunar
characteristics.
Moon Conjunct MC Opposite IC: These aspects
indicate an aptitude for public life. The individual
instinctively senses public opinion and has the ability
to use this gift. Women may be helpful in advancing
the career. This person attracts favorable publicity
unless the Moon is badly afflicted.
Moon Sextiles
Moon sextiles point out those areas that offer the
greatest opportunity for constructive emotional
expression. One's subconscious is active in the affairs
ruled by the Moon and a planet in sextile. The
individual is sensitive to the conditions affected by the
sextile and responsive to associated opportunities.
Moon sextiles also describe a pleasant childhood and
a happy relationship with the mother, a relationship

that reflects favorably on adult attitudes toward
women and the home.
Moon Sextile Mercury: Thissextileproduces intelligence,
a good memory, common sense, and intellectual
perceptivity. Because it fosters fluent communicative
skills, it is an asset to the linguist, the lecturer and the
writer. The affairs influenced by the Moon and Mercury
are handled in an intelligent manner. This aspect helps
prevent psychological problems because the emotions
and mind are in harmony. These people are usually
happy with the decisions they make.
Moon Sextile Venus: This aspect indicates personal
charm and popularity. These people are kind, gracious,
amiable and loving. Because they instinctively know
how to put others at-ease, they are in demand socially.
Most are artistically inclined. This aspect produces a
happy marriage and a fulfilling home life unless strong
contradictions are present in the horoscope. In a
woman's horoscope, this sextile is one indication of
fertility if neither planet is in a barren sign. The affairs
ruled by the Moon and Venus usually prosper financially
unless these planets are heavily afflicted. With afflictions,
prosperous developments are possible, but attendant
expenses can reduce the overall benefit.
Moon Sextile Mars: This sextile gives much emotional
force with the control necessary to direct this energy
productively. These people are resolute, vigorous and
energetic. They take an active interest in the affairs
governed by the Moon and Mars. Because action is quick
and direct, these people lose few of the opportunities
generated by this sextile.
Moon Sextile Jupiter: This is a good luck aspect. These
people possess sound instincts about the affairs ruled by

healthy emotional nature. It fosters optimism,
magnanimity, benevolence and high principles.
Moon Sextile Saturn: Any aspect between the Moon
and Saturn restrains emotional expression to some
degree. This aspect produces good emotional control
and efficient use of emotional energies. The individual
is patient, prudent and provident. The affairs influenced
by the Moon and Saturn are handled in a responsible
fashion. This sextile induces introversion and subdued
emotional reactions.
Moon Sextile Uranus: This sextile adds sparkle to the
personality. These people come across as vivacious and
exciting. They are intuitive, progressive and
individualistic. They respond swiftly to the
opportunities associated with this sextile. They are able
to take advantage of changing conditions that influence
the affairs governed by the Moon and Uranus; they
benefit from the original and timely manner in which
they conduct these affairs.
Moon Sextile Neptune: This aspect fosters spiritual
inspiration. The subconscious and unconscious minds
are mutually supportive. Highly intuitive and extremely
psychic, these people are drawn toward the mystic arts.
They are imaginative; many possess a photographic
memory. These people are sensitive to conditions
influenced by the Moon and Neptune and are responsive
to the opportunities produced by this aspect.
Moon Sextile Pluto: This aspect permits regeneration
of emotional energies; these people are never
completely drained emotionally. This intense
emotional strength generates a powerful sense of
purpose. In addition, these people are able to
transform emotional energy into physical energy. They
exert tremendous energy into the affairs ruled by the
Moon and Pluto. This aspect also promises
opportunities that can lead to Plutonian evolvement
on the highest level.
Moon Sextile North Node Trine South Node: These
aspects enable the individual to advance in the areas
described by the Moon and North Node because this
person is aware of public opinion and helpful trends.
One is able to shed outmoded ways as indicated by
the South Node, ways that might otherwise restrain
progress and hinder development.
Moon Sextile Part of Fortune: This sextile alerts one
to advantages that arise in the areas influenced by the
Moon and Part of Fortune. One's instincts play a large
part in related successes.
Moon Sextile Ascendant Trine Descendant: These
aspects denote harmonious relationships with the
general public and with close associates. This person
is able to create a receptive emotional climate under
most conditions unless the Moon is badly atflicted or
in its detriment.

Moon Squares
Squares formed between the Moon and other planets
are indicative of subconscious blocks and inner
frustrations, which obstruct emotional expression.
Subconscious inhibitions or prejudices that are
hereditary and environmental in nature can retard the
progress of affairs influenced by the Moon and a planet
in square. Frustrating experiences stand in the way of
emotional fulfillment. The individual must develop a
constructive approach in order to overcome the
obstacles generated by Moon squares.
Moon Square Mercury: This aspect indicates a restless
mind and changeable moods. It shows a lack of
continuity of thought; the mind is easily distracted. These
people are seldom happy with their decisions; they tend
to rethink past decisions over and over again. Emotional
impulses block clear judgment in matters ruled by the
Moon and Mercury. These people are inclined to be
irritable, moody, critical and loquacious. This aspect
supports any other factors in the horoscope that point
to possible psychological problems.
Moon Square Venus: This square blocks feelings of
affection. Depending upon the quality of the signs
involved, romantic expression may be hesitant, fickle,
maudlin or too intense. Family interests and
relationships with women provide little happiness or
emotional satisfaction. Sentimentality and
extravagance create setbacks which impede the affairs
governed by the Moon and Venus.
Moon Square Mars: Hostile feelings and violent
emotional reactions are characteristic of this aspect.
These people are quick to take offense at petty remarks
and trivial criticisms; they resent interference of any
kind. They encounter many obstacles of their own
making because they have little regard for the
consequences of their actions. The affairs influenced
by this square are beset by arguments and quarrels;
the domestic sphere is discordant.
Moon Square Jupiter: This square induces profuse
emotional expression. These people are overly
indulgent with loved ones, overly generous to the
disadvantaged, overly sympathetic with the
downtrodden; they are too liberal in their reactions
to anything or anyone that appeals to the emotions.
Unless good aspects offset this square, these people
are vulnerable to a sob story. The affairs governed
by the Moon and Jupiter suffer as a result of action
that is motivated by misplaced sympathy.
Moon Square Saturn: This aspect severely inhibits
emotional warmth. It generates despondency, self-
pity, gloominess, unhappiness, discouragement, fear
and anxiety. These people tend to draw into a shell.
It is imperative for their emotional well-being that they
learn to be more optimistic and outgoing. Because the
approach is narrow and lackluster, affairs ruled by the
Moon and Saturn develop slowly. This square creates
the tendency to accept hardships as necessary burdens,
an attitude that reduces the capacity to overcome
obstacles. The home environment is cold and
somewhat depressing.
Moon Square Uranus: This aspect generates an
emotional need for change and excitement. Restless
and discontented, these people turn from one interest
to another in the search for increasingly greater thrills.
They are seldom satisfied with the course of events
influenced by this square; their actions in these areas
reflect a radical departure from the norm. Home life
and family relationships are generally disruptive.
Moon Square Neptune: This square creates a chaotic
emotional state. These people are confused about their
feelings, unable to sort out inner frustrations. They
tend to fantasize; many have difficulty in
distinguishing between fantasy and reality. They cling
to childhood illusions; they delude themselves about
family relationships and domestic interests. These
people suffer disappointments because of the
impractical and muddled way they handle the affairs
governed by the Moon and Neptune.
Moon Square Pluto: This square signifies forceful and
intense emotional expression. These people refuse to
be dominated emotionally; they can be abusive. The
lust for power is directed toward the affairs influenced
by the square. If other factors in the horoscope
confirm, these people can gain control of large

Moon Trines
A trine formed by the Moon enables one to express
emotional energy in a positive way. The individual
is sensitive to the feelings of others. This person in-
stinctively strikes a harmonious rapport with the
people encountered in the course of affairs ruled by
the Moon and a planet in trine. The individual derives
much emotional fulfillment and happiness from the
success attained in the areas influenced by a Moon
trine. A Moon trine also indicates by sign placement,
house position and rulership that part of childhood
that makes a favorable impression and is reflected in
relations with women and in adult family life.
Moon Trine Mercury: This trine gives intellectual
expression to the emotions and adds emotional coloring
to the mental processes. These people express their ideas
and feelings fluently and tactfully, without
embarrassment or misunderstanding. They instinctively
sense another person's response and thus are able to
phrase ideas in a way that is acceptable. Energy flows
freely between the subconscious and conscious minds.
These people possess more than adequate learning
ability; they readily assimilate and retain the knowledge
to which they are exposed. A good memory, common
sense and eloquent expression of ideas are characteristic
of this trine. These people are witty, mentally alert and
intellectually versatile. They treat domestic affairs and
those interests governed by the Moon and Mercury with
perceptivity, feeling and good sense. They communicate
well with their families.
Moon Trine Venus: This aspect denotes good taste,
gentility and charm. These people are kind,
sympathetic, affectionate and sociable. Both sexes get
along well with women, and most enjoy a happy,
fulfilling domestic life. Because of their sweet and
thoughtful ways, they encounter much good fortune
in the areas influenced by the Moon and Venus. This
trine attracts material benefits and prosperity. It
generates interest in the arts and a desire for the finer
things in life.
Moon Trine Mars: This trine activates emotional
energy, which can be channeled constructively into
the affairs governed by the Moon and Mars. These
people feel strongly about what they do; therefore,
action is backed up by emotional force. They achieve
success because they are ambitious, purposeful and
aggressive. They are active in family life and in the
affairs influenced by the trine; in related matters, they
take the initiative. If a family inheritance is suggested
elsewhere in the horoscope, this trine confirms a
substantial legacy.
Moon Trine jupiter: This trine indicates good fortune
in the affairs ruled by the Moon and Jupiter. It
provides a natural outlet for emotional frustrations,
which are caused by afflictions to the Moon if present.
These people hold high ideals and are devoted to the
causes or principles that they support. Although
spiritual rewards are part of the promise of this trine,
material abundance also manifests in the areas
influenced by the trine. Family life is pleasant and
usually financially beneficial.
Moon Trine Saturn: This aspect stabilizes the
emotional nature. It inspires caution, conservatism and
efficiency. Steady, well-planned efforts represent the

Moon oppositions point out contradictions in one's

represented by the opposing planet. One is acutely
aware of the need to develop in the areas influenced
by a Moon opposition. These interests cannot be
ignored despite the antagonism, repugnance or distaste
generated by the opposition.
Moon Opposite Mercury: This opposition hinders the
ability to express thoughts and feelings adequately.
These people are often misunderstood because they
cannot relate to others on an emotional or an
intellectual level. They may chatter incessantly about
nothing in particular, or they may refuse to volunteer

Moon Parallels
One's emotional expression and natural instincts are
linked to the energies and drives represented by a
planet with which the Moon forms a parallel. A Moon
parallel can produce a harmonious or a discordant
merging of planetary energies. The presence or absence
of a zodiacal aspect between the Moon and a planet
in parallel, the natural relationship between the two
planets and the signs the two planets occupy, all have
a bearing on the influence of a parallel.
A parallel that occurs between the Moon and another
planet with which the Moon also forms a zodiacal aspect
reinforces the zodiacal aspect. This kind of parallel is
interpreted according to the meaning of the zodiacal
aspect it supplements. Such a parallel plays a supportive
role to a major zodiacal aspect; it gives the strength of
a major aspect to a minor zodiacal aspect.
Moon parallels that are formed with planets that
do not form a zodiacal aspect with the Moon are
interpreted as Moon conjunctions. A Moon parallel
is not as powerful as the corresponding conjunction
unless the Moon and the planet in parallel occupy the
same sign.
The Moon forms naturally harmonious parallels with
Venus and Jupiter. Any other Moon parallel that stands
alone takes on the positive characteristics of the
corresponding Moon conjunction if the Moon and the
planet in parallel occupy compatible signs. A Moon
parallel formed with any planet other than Venus or
Jupiter is discordant if the Moon and the planet in parallel
occupy different signs of the same quadruplicity. A
Moon parallel is adversely affected by afflictions to either
the Moon or the planet it parallels.
When interpreting a Moon/Satum parallel, disregard
the reference to the Moon/Satum cycle given in the
interpretation for a Moon/Saturn conjunction. This
cycle is based upon zodiacal motion; it does not affect
parallels or contraparallels.

Moon Aspects 189
Moon Contraparallels
Moon contraparallels create emotional conflicts. The
houses and affairs ruled by the Moon and a planet in
contraparallel are sources of emotional distress. Related
activities provide little emotional satisfaction. A trine or
sextile between the Moon and a planet in contraparallel
permits a large measure of satisfaction, but neither of these
helpful aspects can give complete emotional fulfillment
in combination with a contraparallel.
A contraparallel that the Moon forms with the
Ascendant or MC is treated as an afflicted conjunction.
All other Moon contraparallels are interpreted as
corresponding Moon oppositions. These aspects are
given less weight than oppositions except in those
instances when the Moon and a planet forming a
contraparallel occupy opposing signs in the zodiac.
Minor Moon Aspects
Minor Moon aspects describe something about one's
emotional nature and subconscious drives. To interpret
a minor Moon aspect, consider the principles of the
Moon and the planet it aspects, the nature of the signs
involved, and the houses ruled and occupied by the two
planets. Decide how these factors merge in accordance
with the basic significance of the aspect as given in
Chapter 14. Weigh these findings against all other aspects
that affect either the Moon or the planet in question to
determine the relative strength of the minor aspect. The
characteristics shown by minor Moon aspects are less
pronounced and less influential than those indicated by
major Moon aspects.
Minor Easy Aspects Formed by the Moon: The semi-
sextile is the most important minor easy aspect the
Moon forms. This aspect allows a harmonious flow
of energy between the Moon and the planet in semi-
sextile with the Moon. Moon semi-sextiles also point
out secondary avenues that can be utilized as
constructive outlets for frustrations created by
afflictions to the Moon.
All minor easy aspects formed by the Moon permit
favorable emotional expression through the activities
and affairs ruled by the planet that the Moon aspects.
The effect is mild but, nevertheless, beneficial. Although
these aspects (including the semi-sextile) are not strong
enough to overcome afflictions to the Moon, they help
offset adverse effects by indicating areas that provide
some measure of emotional satisfaction.
Minor Hard Aspects Formed by the Moon: Minor hard
aspects formed by the Moon signify mild emotional
stress and negative subconscious drives. The emotions
are disturbed by the affairs and interests associated with
a planet that forms a minor hard aspect with the Moon.
These aspects can create a subconscious dislike or distaste
for the activities and people represented by the Moon
and the aspected planet.

18 Mercury Aspects
Mercury assumes characteristics of the planets with
which it forms aspects. Its aspects influence intellectual
development and mental expression. They describe
learning aptitude, reasoning ability, mental tendencies,
the formulating of ideas, the expression of thought
through speech and writing, and intellectual interests.
Mercury Conjunctions
Mercury conjunctions energize the mind. A planet with
which Mercury forms a conjunction influences the
intellectual processes. Mental energy is channeled into
the houses and affairs ruled by Mercury and the
conjuncted planet according to the modes of expression
associated with the sign(s) the two planets occupy.
Mercury Conjunct Venus: Mercury and Venusare never
separated by more than 76° in the zodiac. The only major
zodiacal aspects that occur between these two planets
are the conjunction and the sextile. These two planets
can also fonn either a parallel or a contraparallel. A
Mercury/Venus conjunction gives a pleasing voice that
can best be described as melodious, mellow or dulcet-
toned. People with this aspect are gifted conversation-
alists. Tactful and persuasive, they express their ideas
with grace and chann and are usually amiable and good-
natured. Sociable and friendly, most are popular.
Intellectual interests gravitate toward the arts and
moneymaking activities. However, if the conjunction is
afflicted they tend to put on social airs. The women are
coquettish, and the men foppish. Speech is flattering;
mannerisms, artificial.
Mercury Conjunct Mars: This aspect indicates a lively,
aggressive mind. These people are mentally active and
quick-witted. Intellectually competitive, they are
always ready to accept the challenge of argument or
debate. They come straight to the point without
apology or excuse regardless of what anyone else
thinks. Most of them possess a satirical sense of humor
and are quick to comment on human foibles and
shortcomings. If the conjunction is afflicted, these
people can be viciously sarcastic; they make malicious
comments and caustic remarks. Speech is abrupt,
abrasive and quarrelsome.
Mercury Conjunct Jupiter: This aspect combines the
concrete and abstract thought processes: mental
capacity and reasoning ability are broadened. These
people are as comfortable with theoretical concepts
as they are with factual topics. Avid students, most
seek some form of higher education. This conjunction
indicates intellectual integrity. If the conjunction is
afflicted, these people tend to think of themselves as
authorities on almost any subject. They insist on
promoting their ideas and many get carried away with
the sound of their own voices.
Mercury Conjunct Saturn: In this conjunction Saturn
disciplines the mind and produces strong powers of
mental concentration. These people are able to block
out extraneous thoughts and focus on a particular idea.
Mental interests are of a practical nature. These people
tend to study subjects that can be applied to career
or business pursuits. Although they may not learn
quickly, they remember and utilize what they do leam

Mercury Squares
Mercury squares create nervous tension and learning
difficulties. Intellectual expression and communication
are inadequate in the areas governed by Mercury and
a planet squaring it. Mental blocks and poor planning
hinder the proper development of the affairs influenced
by a Mercury square. These aspects do not indicate
lack of intelligence; they show by sign position, house
placement and rulership how and in which areas the
individual does not use natural mental abilities to the
best advantage.
Mercury Square Mars; This square energizes the
intellect, but mental energy is difficult to control and
channel productively. Through impulsiveness and
insufficient planning, these people create problems for
themselves in the areas influenced by the square.
Brusque to the point of rudeness, they frequently
antagonize the very persons whose support would be
helpful in developing the affairs governed by Mercury
and Mars. Impatience, argumentativeness and anger
are characteristic of this square. Coarseness of speech
is common. One may risk physical safety performing
dangerous, daredevil feats. Health difficulties can also
occur as a result of the extreme nervous tension this
aspect generates.
Mercury Square Jupiter; This aspect promotes
improvident schemes and excessive talk. Although
these people have fertile minds, they think in terms
that are too grandiose to be practical. They are absent-
minded about details and exercise poor judgment in
the affairs ruled by Mercury and Jupiter. Overly
optimistic about these matters, they frequently over-
look negative potentialities. Tendencies to exaggerate
and boast are common. Many of these people are
conversational bores who do not know how to listen.
This square can indicate an aversion or mental block
toward organized religion.
Mercury Square Saturn: This square indicates a serious
mind and conservative mental attitudes. Often
intellectual development is hindered by narrow ideas
and prejudicial views. These people cling to traditional
thought and the refusal to break with established
methods is a major obstacle to the advancement of
the affairs affected by the aspect. They hold negative
outlooks toward the interests ruled by Mercury and
Satum; dwelling on related problems may cause
much unnecessary mental anguish. Introspective and
reticent to express their opinions, many find casual
conversation awkward.
Mercury Square Uranus: This aspect denotes a
rebellious mind and radical ideas. These people are
intellectual nonconformists who frequently disagree
with current thought just to be different. They may
come up with unprecedented ideas, but few of these
ideas have any practical value. Because of the bizarre
manner in which they conduct the affairs governed
by Mercury and Uranus, many create awkward
predicaments for themselves. In attempting to resolve
one difficulty, they usually stir up even greater
problems. They tend to talk in disjointed phrases and
conversation is generally erratic. If Mercury is badly
afflicted, this aspect can produce stuttering.
Mercury Square Neptune: This square induces
forgetfulness, mental confusion and illogical thinking.
Impressionable, these people tend to believe everything
they read and most of what they hear. They are
bewildered by conflicting ideas and controversial
theories. Indecisiveness and the failure to form
practical plans retard the development of the affairs
influenced by the square. During conversation these
people wander from one topic to another without
making a point. They give evasive answers to pointed
questions; many lie outright if backed into a comer.
Mercury Square Pluto: This aspect produces an intent,
secretive, suspicious mind. These people are close-
mouthed about their plans. Regardless of how voluble

These aspects place the individual at an intellectual
